title: 50Hertz installs two offshore export cable systems at Dierhagen

50Hertz installs two offshore export cable systems at Dierhagen TGS 4C | 4C Offshore News
50Hertz installs two offshore export cable systems at Dierhagen
Progress has been reportedly made on the OST-6-1 grid connection for the
Gennaker
offshore windfarm.
The Installation of two of the three submarine cable systems began in July
at Dierhagen on Germany’s Baltic Sea coast.
The cables have been threaded from a cable-laying vessel through prepared
protective pipes via a platform and pulled beneath the coastline to a drilling
site located just over one kilometre away.
The next phase of the project will involve installation of the third submarine
cable system. Once completed, the connection will provide a total transmission
capacity of over 900 MW.
into the 50Hertz transmission grid through the OST-6-1 grid connection.
The wind farm and grid connection are planned to support Germany's energy
transition and security.

title: Blade testing has begun in a test rig at Blyth
content:
An 88 metre wind turbine blade has been lifted into a test rig at Blyth
as part of a new torsional fatigue testing programme.
Danish wind turbine blade company Bladena is conducting the tests, using
70 sensors to monitor the blade's response to 1 million fatigue cycles
of controlled torsional loading.
The testing is being carried out to address the growing demands of the
offshore wind sector, where turbine blades continue to increase in size.
According to the company, most blades now exceed 70 to 80 metres in length,
and the forces acting on them have not scaled proportionally. As a result,
the risk of torsional loads and deformation has become more significant.
The testing programme will be carried out in two phases. The first phase
involves baseline testing of an unreinforced blade, while the second will
assess whether two structural reinforcement solutions can reduce the deformation
that can lead to blade failure.

title: MacGregor achieves certification for F2F personal transfer
content:
MacGregor's Horizon gangway has received DNV certification for their floating-to-floating
(F2F) personnel transfers.
The certification enables the creation of a walkway that safely connects
two independently moving vessels and follows sea acceptance testing conducted
in accordance with DNV-ST-0358.
MacGregor said the certification provides greater flexibility for operators
of FPSOs, floating rigs, floating wind arrays and offshore service fleets.
According to the company, the system can reduce reliance on port schedules
campaigns to be carried out without being routed through port calls.
"Crew changes can be carried out at sea, service campaigns don't need
to be routed around port calls, and walk-to-work access between vessels
can be based on the field's schedule," said Prateek Sadhana, product
owner at MacGregor.
"In the renewables sector, this supports the service logistics that
floating wind operations demand, where there is no fixed structure to land
The F2F transfer system includes a purpose designed flap at the gangway
tip, while LiDAR-based relative motion tracking provides real time data
to the gangway's motion compensation system.
MacGregor said the F2F capability is being introduced as an extended function
of the Horizon gangway rather than as a standalone product.

title: NKT qualifies new HVDC subsea cable for operation
content:
NKT has qualified a 525-kV HVDC extruded XLPE subsea power cable system
for operations at conductor temperatures of up to 90°C.
The system is designed to provide greater flexibility in the design and
operation of HVDC transmission projects.
According to NKT, the higher temperature capability can be used to increase
transmission capacity, reduce material consumption and improve overall
system efficiency, depending on project requirements.
The qualification is based on an upgraded insulation system. The inner
and outer semiconductive layers were redesigned using a new material developed
and qualified through a joint project between NKT and Borouge International.
The new semiconductive material, Borlink LE0650DC, was developed as part
of a long term collaboration between the two companies.
The upgraded insulation system is intended to support the thermal performance,
reliability and efficiency of HVDC transmission infrastructure.
NKT said the new 90°C
technology portfolio includes power cables rated up to 525 kV HVDC for
both onshore and offshore installation.

Ventyr given extension to submit Sørlige Nordsjø II licence application
The Norwegian Ministry of Energy has granted Ventyr a 12 month extension
to complete a project specific impact assessment and submit a licence application
for the Sørlige
Nordsjø II
offshore wind project.
The new deadline has been set for October 15, 2027, following an extension
request submitted in June 2026.
Ventyr said additional time is needed to investigate alternative routes
for landfall and grid connection, including options around Alcoa's plant
at Lista.
In March 2024, Ventyr, a joint venture between JERA Nex bp and Ingka Investments,
won the allocation for the Sørlige Nordsjø II offshore wind project.
Once operational, the project is expected to have a total installed capacity
of 1.5 GW, enough to supply electricity to around 500,000 Norwegian households.

title: LG Energy Solution North America Head on Battery Market Pivot
content:
Battery Manufacturing
Industry Outlook
Battery Applications
Interviews
LGES North America President Bob Lee explains how Michigan plant balances EV and ESS production amid shifting demand, data center pushback, and emerging chemistries.
August 24, 2026
9 Min Read
The LGES facility in Lansing, MI, officially began production of LFP cells for energy storage systems on August 18, 2026.
M. Anderson / Battery TEchnology
At a Glance
Solid-state batteries will reach consumer electronics a decade before EVs due to manufacturing scalability challenges
AI data centers create unique battery opportunities due to dramatic power swings from compute cluster operations
LG is piloting sodium-ion for stationary storage while developing lithium-metal-rich chemistries for EVs
When Bob Lee, President of LG Energy Solution North America, discusses the company's newly operational Lansing, Michigan battery manufacturing facility, he frames it not merely as another addition to the continent's growing production capacity, but as a strategic response to fundamental market volatility.
In a news conference at the newly in-production plant on August 18, 2026, Lee—alongside Devon Wilson, LG's VP of Sales for grid-scale ESS energy storage division—outlined how the facility has evolved from its original conception as a dedicated EV battery plant into what may be the industry's most adaptable large-scale battery manufacturing operation in North America.
Devon Wilson (l) and Bob Lee talk to reporters at the event marking the start of production of ESS cells at the LGES Lansing facility on August 18, 2026. Credit: M. Anderson / Battery Technology
The transformation reflects Lee's assessment of market realities: automotive programs carry long development cycles and uncertain volume projections, while energy storage systems offer more stable revenue patterns and are experiencing structural demand growth driven by grid modernization needs. LG has repositioned the Lansing facility to balance both opportunities while maintaining the flexibility to shift production as markets evolve.
Related:
LG Energy Solution Opens First US Large-Scale LFP Battery Plant for Energy Storage
Key insights: From AI data centers to solid-state timelines
Lee's perspective on emerging applications and technologies offers a reality check on several topics dominating industry discussions. On artificial intelligence infrastructure, he confirmed that AI data centers represent a distinct ESS opportunity due to their unique power consumption patterns—compute clusters that activate and deactivate simultaneously create dramatic load swings that batteries can smooth far more effectively than conventional generation.
However, Lee emphasized responsible development: "I think now we've gotten better at responsible data center development, so that you need to make sure that the community is not impacted in terms of things like the water and power." Wilson noted that while AI facilities generate attention, "the lion's share of our growth is just based on basic fundamentals of retiring legacy thermal generation assets."
On solid-state batteries—a technology that has attracted billions in investment and countless optimistic timelines—Lee offered a sobering assessment: "You will see that in your smartphones probably a decade before you would ever see it in EVs." The challenge isn't laboratory performance but manufacturing scalability at the large form factors required for automotive and energy storage applications.
Meanwhile, LG is actively piloting sodium-ion technology for stationary storage, maintaining strategic optionality as supply chain dynamics evolve. "We want to have all those options open," Wilson explained, though LFP remains the optimal chemistry for most current ESS projects.
Related:
How LG Energy Solution Navigates North America’s Unsettled Market Dynamics
Another emerging opportunity: battery integration with EV charging infrastructure, which Lee identified as "one of our future growth segments." By co-locating batteries with charging stations, operators can dramatically reduce electrical infrastructure buildout costs—a practical solution LG is beta testing with charging hardware manufacturers.
Originally launched as part of the Ultium joint venture with General Motors, LG has since assumed 100% ownership and fundamentally restructured the facility's mission. The plant now operates with roughly equal capacity dedicated to EV batteries and energy storage systems, with Toyota serving as the anchor automotive customer while multiple ESS clients utilize the facility's production capabilities.
In a major pivot away from its earlier EV plans, GM is sold its half of the Lansing facility to LG in 2024. Credit: GMpivoting away from the Ultium cells that were the centerpiece of its EV strategy.
The technical challenges of converting EV-focused production lines to accommodate different chemistries and form factors are substantial. The shift to lithium iron phosphate (LFP) chemistry for energy storage required significant process modifications.
Related:
GM & LG Energy Solution Strengthen US EV Supply Chain with LFP Batteries
"[With] LFP, usually the coating loading is thicker, so you need to have more roll press to compress, and then there's slight differences in the manufacturing process itself," Lee noted. "So you do need to put in some new equipment and validate that in order to build batteries from one another."
Beyond chemistry changes, the Lansing facility is preparing to produce both LFP pouch cells and LFP prismatic cells—a capability requiring additional line investments but leveraging LG's historical experience with multiple cell formats.
Lee emphasized that LG's long tenure provides crucial institutional knowledge: "We've been in the battery industry for a long time. We've actually had experience with LFP in the past as we moved on to focus on NMC recently. So I think this plant is a great example of how fast we were able to put in the capacity."
LFP cell production at the Lansing facility. Credit: LGES
The company claims to be the first major manufacturer to successfully execute this type of large-scale conversion, positioning the Lansing facility as what Lee termed a "mother plant"—a testing ground for new technologies and processes before broader deployment across LG's North American manufacturing network.
AI data centers create specialized requirements and community concerns
Artificial intelligence computing facilities represent an emerging ESS application with unique technical demands. Unlike traditional data centers with relatively steady power consumption, AI facilities experience dramatic load swings as compute clusters activate and deactivate simultaneously.
"AI data centers are usually unique in which it's clusters of compute that all get turned on at once and then get turned off at once," Wilson explained. "So if you look at the energy demand, it swings up and down, and so while the overall energy need can be met, those swings are problematic."
Battery systems address this challenge through rapid response capabilities that conventional generation cannot match, smoothing load profiles to prevent grid disruption. This requires careful hardware selection—including specific cell chemistries and power conversion equipment—integrated with sophisticated control software.
However, Lee acknowledged that data center deployments face legitimate community concerns that the industry must address responsibly, noting that Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer had addressed these issues in her remarks at the event.
"In general, a lot of people are concerned about water not being available in the intervening area, or power either not being available or prices going up," Lee explained. "So I think now we've gotten better at responsible data center development. I think municipalities and developers are [also] getting much better at doing that.”
Lee emphasized LG's commitment to supporting only responsible data center buildouts that address infrastructure and environmental impacts on surrounding communities.
EV charging infrastructure emerges as growth segment
Battery integration with electric vehicle charging infrastructure represents what Lee identified as "one of our future growth segments for our ESS business." The primary challenge in deploying high-speed charging isn't the charging hardware itself but rather the electrical infrastructure required to deliver power to charging locations.
"There's a lot of opportunities to use batteries, so you don't have to build out all the infrastructure," Wilson noted. "You can reduce those costs by having batteries globally."
LG is conducting beta testing with charging station hardware manufacturers to develop optimized battery system specifications for this application, which differs from both grid-scale containerized solutions and behind-the-meter installations.
Chemistry roadmap balances application needs with manufacturing reality
LG's approach to emerging and alternative battery chemistries reflects careful assessment of both application requirements and manufacturing readiness—a pragmatic stance that distinguishes hype from near-term commercial viability.
For stationary storage applications, where weight and volumetric energy density matter far less than cost, safety, and cycle life, LFP currently offers the optimal balance. "We always look to apply the right chemistry for the application, and stationary is very different than an EV application where weight and density doesn't matter as much," Wilson explained. "LFP is a really great choice when you talk about stationary storage ESS."
However, LG is actively piloting sodium-ion technology to maintain strategic optionality as supply chain dynamics and project economics evolve. The company expects sodium-ion may prove advantageous for certain project types or operational profiles while LFP continues serving the majority of applications.
For automotive applications requiring higher energy density, LG is developing lithium-metal-rich (LMR) and mid-nickel chemistries focused on the affordability that customers increasingly demand. "Those are products that we're working very closely right now with our customers because they're driving toward more affordability," Lee noted.
These advanced lithium-ion chemistries can be accommodated within current manufacturing infrastructure. "If you look at that kind of parameter, I would say we would, in general, be able to produce that in the same plant with some adjustments to our equipment," Lee explained.
Solid-state technology, despite decades of development attention and substantial industry investment, faces a fundamentally different timeline. Lee offered a sobering assessment that challenges the optimistic projections often heard at industry conferences: "You will see that in your smartphones probably a decade before you would ever see it in EVs."
The core challenge is manufacturing scalability rather than laboratory performance. "The problem with solid state is large scale production," Lee explained. "It has very good energy density, so if you're making it in small form formats, you should be able to get that. But if you're starting to make it in very large form factors, it's proven that those companies struggle."
Lee expects initial commercial applications in consumer electronics or highly specialized use cases before solid-state technology achieves the scale required for EVs or energy storage systems. "So yes, it's interesting technology. We're researching. We've invested in companies, but at the same time, I think we have to stay clear-eyed in terms of how fast we can get to scale."
Strategic positioning for market uncertainty
LG's investment trajectory in Michigan—spanning from the 2012 Holland plant launch through multiple presidential administrations—demonstrates long-term commitment despite policy volatility. The Lansing facility's design as a large-scale, single-building operation with diverse customer base and chemistry flexibility positions the company to navigate continued market uncertainty.
Lee's confidence in the plant's medium-term outlook centers on customer strength and technology positioning: "Toyota is one of our main customers here. I would say Toyota is a very strong customer, so I have very high confidence in their ability to be a good customer and produce good vehicles and ultimately sell vehicles into the market."
For the broader battery manufacturing industry, LG's Lansing facility offers a template for managing the transition period as markets mature and technology evolves—demonstrating that manufacturing flexibility and systems-level expertise may prove as valuable as raw production capacity in navigating the decade ahead.

title: Prometheus’ 1.5 GW Texas Data Center Plan Tests Private Power
content:
Data center developer Prometheus Hyperscale is betting that the fastest way to put AI compute in West Texas is to avoid an initial ERCOT grid connection altogether.
The company plans a 1.5 GW data center campus in Pecos, Texas, powered by an islanded generation system. The project has a development path to 2.5 GW, with pipeline natural gas supplying the initial generation and a planned co-located fractionation facility providing ethane fuel flexibility after it enters service.
That approach removes the campus from the initial
ERCOT interconnection process
, but it does not remove the difficult work of supplying power. Prometheus and its eventual customer will need to manage generation, firm fuel supplies, air permitting, maintenance, redundancy, and financing – responsibilities typically handled by a utility in a grid-connected project.
Adam Mirick, Prometheus’ chief energy and business officer, told
Data Center Knowledge
in an interview that the company has already spoken with several prospective customers.
Related:
EdgeCore Says Data Centers Should Pay Their Own Power Costs
The project, however, remains contingent on a customer commitment. Prometheus says a modular deployment could deliver 100-150 MW of compute capacity in 2027.
“If we had a commitment, I’d say in October, perhaps we can bring on 100 to 150 megawatts of compute in 2027,” Mirick said. “It’s very challenging to bring anything to market in ’27 right now between the generation, between the MDCs, the contractors, all of it.”
A Power Plant Behind the Data Center
The 1.5 GW figure represents planned IT load, not generation capacity. Prometheus favors rich-burn reciprocating engines for the initial generation blocks because they can be deployed incrementally and accommodate fuel variability. Larger turbine units could become more attractive as the campus expands.
“We’re leaning towards a rich-burn reciprocating engine for the initial blocks, just because the rich-burn engines accommodate the different fuels better than the lean burns,” Mirick said.
The final generation fleet will depend on the tenant’s reliability requirements and data center design.
Mirick said an initial reciprocating-engine configuration could require about 30% more installed generation than the underlying facility load to provide redundancy.
At a preliminary
assumption of 1.3, a 1.5 GW IT load would produce roughly 1.95 GW of facility demand. Applying the illustrative 30% overbuild would put potential installed generation at about 2.5 GW.
That is not a final project design. Prometheus has not disclosed the final generation configuration or installed capacity for Phase 1.
Related:
Nvidia Backs OpenAI’s Ohio Data Center Buildout With $105B Guarantee
The company expects to use best available control technology and obtain the required air permits for the generation facilities, Mirick said.
The 2027 Test
The first power target depends on more than the generation equipment. A customer seeking 2027 compute would need to accept modular data center construction, according to Mirick. A conventional custom-built facility would take longer.
“Stick-built, custom design, it’s not possible in our view in 2027,” Mirick said. “You’re probably looking at middle of 2028 at this point.”
Modular construction would allow Prometheus to bring smaller blocks online as equipment arrives, rather than waiting for an entire conventional data hall to be built.
A customer commitment would also trigger orders for the modular data centers and generation equipment, firm gas transportation and project financing.
“The tenant commitment is really the magic that unlocks the capital and gets everything moving,” Mirick said.
Prometheus has not signed a binding customer agreement for a Pecos tenant. Mirick said there is strong early interest but declined to characterize the discussions beyond that.
Natural Gas First
The Reeves County project’s planned fuel system is designed around pipeline natural gas, with ethane providing additional fuel flexibility.
Related:
APAC Data Center Pipeline Surges as AI Pre-Leasing Tightens Supply
Istmo Energy’s co-located fractionation facility is under construction, and is expected to enter service in the first quarter of 2028. Until then, the data center’s planned generation would run on pipeline natural gas.
Once the fractionation facility is operating, Prometheus expects a baseline of 85% natural gas and 15% ethane.
Fractionation separates components of a mixed natural gas liquids stream, allowing Istmo to recover ethane for use by the adjacent power system.
“Once you get into ’28 and you’ve got the fractionation, then you’re going to have the ethane backup,” Mirick said.
The precise operating profile of the fuel mix remains dependent on the final generation design. Prometheus also expects on-site ethane storage and, potentially, propane storage.
The company plans two separate methane pipeline connections and firm transportation. If one fuel supply is interrupted, the generators could operate on the other.
“Our base case is 85/15,” Mirick said. “If there’s something wrong with methane pipelines, our checkdown is go full ethane. If there’s something wrong with ethane, you go full methane.”
What Islanding Changes
Located in Reeves County, the Pecos data center will initially have no physical connection to the ERCOT grid, Mirick said.
“We’re building an island because the island is what allows us to deliver the speed, the reliability that’s required,” he said.
The strategy is a direct response to uncertainty around Texas’ large-load interconnection process. It does not, however, put the project outside
Texas regulation
. The generation facilities will still require environmental permits and fuel infrastructure, while the project must secure financing and construct a power system capable of operating continuously.
Prometheus could eventually connect the campus to the grid, but Mirick said that would be driven by the tenant.
“We’re not against being grid-connected in the future, but it has to make sense, and it’ll be tenant-directed,” he said.
For now, the company is focused on operating independently of ERCOT.
“We are solely focused on hitting the timetables and reliability metrics through islanding,” Mirick said.
Taking On Utility-Like Risks
The harder question is whether private generation can deliver hyperscale reliability without simply moving the risks elsewhere. Prometheus expects to use N+1 generation for the initial reciprocating-engine fleet, with the amount of redundancy determined by the customer’s reliability requirements.
“We’re letting them define the number of nines that they want,” Mirick said.
Higher reliability requirements require more generation and electrical infrastructure, he said.
“The more nines, it’s not a linear cost,” Mirick said. “It starts to go up in nonlinear fashion.”
Joshua D. Rhodes, a research scientist at the University of Texas at Austin and a non-resident fellow at Columbia University, said operating generation continuously creates mechanical challenges that are different from the traditional role of standby generators.
“One of the things we’ve seen with running what used to be back up generation full-time is that it increases mechanical stress, and the systems can wear out two to three times as fast,” Rhodes said.
Rhodes said battery storage could serve as a buffer between volatile AI loads and onsite generation, reducing mechanical stress on the engines.
The model shifts more of the operational and commercial risk associated with power infrastructure into the developer-customer relationship.
Prometheus and its eventual customer will have to allocate responsibility for the generation fleet, fuel system and electrical infrastructure that a grid-connected data center would ordinarily obtain through a utility and broader power-supply ecosystem.
The Cost of Going It Alone
Prometheus also sees private generation as a way to give customers greater certainty over long-term electricity costs.
Mirick estimated the cost of islanded generation at roughly $100 to $125 per megawatt-hour, assuming $3.50/MMBtu for natural gas.
The company did not provide a detailed breakdown of that estimate, including the treatment of generation capital costs, financing, fuel transportation, emissions controls, maintenance and redundancy. It is therefore not a direct comparison with a utility tariff.
“Putting in behind-the-meter, you know what your capex is going to be for power,” Mirick said. “You know what your rate’s going to be for power for 15 years.”
The trade-off is greater responsibility for the infrastructure supplying that power.
“Grid is easy,” Mirick said. “You basically toss the problems over the fence to the utility.”
Little Water, More Power Infrastructure
The Pecos campus will use closed-loop cooling rather than evaporative cooling.
Mirick said the cooling system would initially contain about 75% water and 25% food-grade propylene glycol. The loop would be filled initially, with limited makeup water expected during normal operation.
Prometheus does not yet have a final design and cannot provide a firm water-consumption figure. Mirick estimated that combined water use for the power and data hall operations could be below the equivalent of roughly 100 households, but said that estimate is preliminary.
The company does not expect the campus to discharge any water during normal operations.
The Real Test
Pecos is part of Prometheus’ broader strategy of developing data centers around dedicated power systems rather than relying on conventional utility service. The company is also pursuing a Dallas-area project targeting 2027 compute and Wyoming projects targeting 2028.
The strategy can remove one major variable from a data center development schedule: the initial grid interconnection.
But it replaces that variable with a much larger set of responsibilities.
Whether Pecos reaches even its initial 100 MW to 150 MW target in 2027 will depend not on an ERCOT interconnection date, but on whether Prometheus can secure a tenant and prove it can build, fuel, permit, finance and continuously operate its own utility-scale power system.

title: A 3.6 GWh, 18-hour lithium-ion BESS project has secured planning consent in Scotland - Energy Storage
content: The 18-hour Rigifa BESS project in Scotland has secured planning approval, paving the way for investment and construction of the second-largest battery project in the new UK long-duration energy storage (LDES) cap and floor scheme. Field Head of Development Bex Sherwood announced on LinkedIn that the 200 MW/3,600 MWh Rigifa BESS was granted “irrevocable planning consent.” The developer has four other UK sites under construction, as well as six live sites operating in Germany and the United Kingdom. Rigifa BESS is one of five Field projects selected by energy regulator Ofgem for support via the forthcoming LDES cap and floor scheme. The others include three more in North Scotland – including the largest cap-and-floor BESS, Field New Deer (400 MW/7,200MWh) – plus the 200 MW/3,300 MWh Field Long Stratton project under development in East England. For successful projects such as Rigifa, the LDES cap and floor scheme is expected to provide revenue certainty needed to support investment in large-scale, long-duration energy storage projects. The support is similar in design to a cap-and-floor program that was introduced for UK interconnector projects. Cap-and-floor generally provides projects with a guaranteed revenue floor, with revenues topped up if market prices fall below this level. The project owner must also repay any revenues exceeding the agreed price cap. Ofgem published its “minded-to” decisions for LDES projects in June 2026, selecting 16 projects from a shortlist of 77 that was revealed in September 2025. BESS deployment in the United Kingdom has been largely driven by the private sector until this point, with the technology unable to secure the kinds of state-backed revenue guarantees on offer to renewable generators through contracts for difference auction. While the number of BESS projects in the UK pipeline significantly exceeds the required capacity in power rating terms, with two-hour-duration assets proving popular, grid operator NESO has forecast a need for longer-duration energy storage assets in the future. One senior figure at Ofgem told ESS News that when assessing the need for market intervention via an LDES cap-and-floor, the regulator identified a discrete market failure in ability to bring online the type of assets that will be supported by the program. When complete, Rigifa BESS will connect to the Gills Bay substation near Thurso on the north coast of Scotland. Wind generation in Scotland has been subject to significant curtailment, and seven of the 16 LDES cap and floor projects selected by Ofgem are in the north of Scotland. title: Battery storage cuts farm electricity costs by 80% in Spain - Energy Storage
content: Finca La Cuesta, an agricultural operation in Puebla del Príncipe in Ciudad Real, Spain, completed the second phase of an energy self-consumption project in July, combining 150 kW of solar generation with a 125 kW/257 kWh BESS. The solution, implemented by Elecnor using equipment supplied by Suministros Orduña, is designed to reduce the farm’s electricity costs by 75% to 80%. The project addresses a consumption profile typical of some agricultural operations, with relatively high and consistent electricity demand associated with pumping and other processes required for the farm’s daily operations. The installation was developed in two stages. The first, completed in July 2025, added 150 kW of solar capacity using three 50 kW Sungrow SG50CX-P2 inverters. This initial phase reduced the electricity bill by 30% to 35%. After analyzing the farm’s consumption profile for a year, the project was expanded with a 125 kW/257 kWh storage system. The aim of the second phase is to increase the share of solar energy used directly or through storage, avoiding the need to export excess generation during periods of high solar irradiance and subsequently purchase electricity when solar generation is insufficient. The BESS consists of a Sungrow PowerStack ST255CS, an AC-coupled storage system designed for commercial and industrial applications. The system can charge the batteries with excess solar generation and later discharge the stored energy according to the site’s consumption needs and its defined energy strategy. On the generation side, the three SG50CX-P2 inverters have four independent maximum power point tracking (MPPT) inputs, allowing different groups of modules to be managed separately and production to be optimized in response to differences in orientation, irradiance, or operating conditions. One of the project’s main technical challenges was not simply installing the equipment but integrating and coordinating its energy flows. The three solar inverters, PowerStack system, and EMS300 energy management system (EMS) exchange information to adapt the storage system’s operation to changes in the farm’s electricity demand. This architecture allows the battery to respond to changes in consumption and enables solar generation to be used more efficiently. Energy management is therefore a key element in maximizing the economic value of the BESS. The system is not simply designed to increase self-consumption but to determine when the battery should charge and discharge based on solar generation, the site’s demand profile, and electricity costs. The next planned phase involves more advanced system optimization through time-of-use energy arbitrage. Data recorded by the iSolarCloud monitoring platform will be used to adjust the EMS300 parameters based on the site’s consumption profile, hourly electricity prices, power charges, and network tariffs. According to the project estimates, this strategy could increase the financial benefit of the installation by 10% to 15%. Monitoring will also allow the operators to assess the system’s actual performance and progressively adjust the BESS operating parameters. The farm could also expand its storage capacity by adding another PowerStack unit. The medium-term goal is to achieve an energy self-sufficiency rate close to 100%. With the electricity bill expected to fall by 75% to 80%, the system reduces exposure to electricity prices while allowing a larger share of locally generated renewable electricity to be used. The project also reduces associated CO₂ emissions and provides continuous monitoring of the solar plant’s performance and the storage system’s condition. It also highlights the importance of sizing a BESS based on actual consumption data rather than treating storage as an independent component of the generation system. title: Battery storage emerges as revenue asset for industrial sites - Energy Storage
content: BESS Perlen AG, owned by Perlen Industrieholding AG and Valyou Investment Foundation, is investing in a 10 MW/20 MWh battery energy storage system (BESS) in Switzerland. The system, supplied by ADS-TEC Energy, will be installed at the site of paper manufacturer Perlen Papier AG, with commissioning scheduled by the end of 2026. Beyond strengthening the site’s energy infrastructure, the battery will allow the company to turn energy storage into a new source of revenue. By storing electricity when market conditions are favorable and dispatching it when conditions are more attractive, industrial companies can make greater use of flexibility in their energy consumption and generation. Initially, the Perlen system will primarily provide grid services that contribute to the balance and stability of the electricity system. Over time, the battery will also participate in the day-ahead and intraday electricity markets, creating additional opportunities to monetize its flexibility. Swiss energy company Wattss is responsible for the overall management of the project, from development and technical integration to participation in electricity markets. The project illustrates the expanding role of batteries at industrial sites. Rather than serving only as a tool to secure or optimize electricity supplies, they can become economic assets in their own right, generating additional revenue. Depending on site configuration and market conditions, storage can monetize energy flexibility through multiple electricity-related revenue streams. With the installation, Perlen aims to further transform its industrial site into an energy hub capable of actively participating in electricity markets while developing new sources of long-term value. Geiger said the BESS will support the continued transformation of the Perlen industrial site into a modern energy hub while creating new sources of value, with energy becoming an additional economic asset for the business. title: China launches EPC tender for 660 MW/3.96 GWh CAES project - Energy Storage
content: A 660 MW/3.96 GWh advanced CAES project in China’s Henan province has entered the EPC tendering stage, marking another large-scale deployment of long-duration energy storage technology in the country. The Jiyuan 660 MW advanced compressed air energy storage demonstration project published its EPC tender notice on August 18, according to the project document. The facility will be built in Sili town, Jiyuan, some 750 kilometers southwest of Beijing, with a planned static investment of approximately CNY 4.79 billion ($670 million). The project is expected to have a construction period of 36 months. The project is being developed by Jiyuan Hengdong Energy Storage Technology and will include engineering, procurement, and construction works under a single EPC contract. The bidding deadline is Sept. 22, 2026. Unlike conventional compressed air energy storage systems, which require external heat sources such as natural gas combustion during electricity generation, the Jiyuan project will adopt an advanced adiabatic compressed air energy storage (AA-CAES) configuration. In an AA-CAES system, electricity is used to compress air and store it underground. The heat generated during compression is captured and stored in a thermal storage system, then reused when the compressed air expands through turbines to generate electricity. This approach eliminates fossil fuel consumption and improves system efficiency compared with traditional CAES technologies. The project will use pressurized water as the thermal storage medium and construct a new underground cavern for compressed air storage. This differs from projects such as the 300 MW/1.8 GWh CAES facility in Feicheng, Shandong province, which used existing salt cavern resources. Underground storage is a key factor in CAES economics. Salt caverns provide naturally sealed and cost-effective storage space but are geographically limited. Artificial rock caverns, such as the system planned in Jiyuan, can expand deployment possibilities in regions without suitable salt formations, although they require additional excavation and sealing work. China has accelerated the development of advanced CAES in recent years as it seeks alternatives to conventional batteries for multi-hour energy storage. Representative projects include the 100 MW Zhangjiakou CAES demonstration facility in Hebei, the 300 MW/1.8 GWh Feicheng project in Shandong, and several 300 MW to 660 MW projects currently under construction or development in Henan. With a six-hour storage duration, the Jiyuan project reflects China’s effort to scale compressed air storage from pilot demonstrations toward utility-scale applications. However, challenges remain, including the complexity of underground engineering, lower round-trip efficiency than lithium-ion batteries, and the need for appropriate market mechanisms to support long-duration storage assets. title: European Energy starts building battery alongside solar farm in Australia - Energy Storage
content: European Energy has commenced construction of an AC-coupled 40 MW / 80 MWh battery energy storage system (BESS) intended to unlock the full potential of its Mokoan Solar Farm near Winton in northern Victoria. The 58 MW solar farm has been fully operational since early last year, generating approximately 113 GWh of electricity annually. Catriona McLeod, managing director for European Energy in Australia, said the two-hour BESS, which will share the same grid connection as the solar farm, is expected to commence operations by the middle of next year, adding that battery energy storage is a key element of the company’s development strategy. “Batteries are crucial for EE and the whole industry,” she said. “They will truly unlock the full potential of wind and solar and provide more renewable energy when it’s needed most.” “We’ll be doing a lot in this space in the back end of 2026 and into 2027 so there are plenty more announcements to come.” Financial close on the battery project was achieved last month after German lender Deutsche Bank provided a non-recourse package to refinance the existing debt on the solar farm and to support construction and operation of the battery. The progress on the Mokoan battery project follows European Energy’s recent announcement of financial close for the Winton North Solar Farm with battery project. Both the Winton North and Mokoan solar farms are backed by a power purchase agreement (PPA) with global technology provider Amazon Web Services. European Energy Australia currently has a renewable energy pipeline of approximately 10 GW, with projects at various stages from early investigation through to fully operational. title: Harmony Energy switches on 70 MWh Skeeby BESS in UK - Energy Storage
content: UK-based utility-scale battery storage developer Harmony Energy has energized its 35 MW / 70 MWh Skeeby battery energy storage system (BESS) near Richmond, North Yorkshire, England. The project commenced work in early 2026, with a roughly seven-month turnaround from shovel to energization. The project uses unspecified Tesla Megapacks, and with the new asset now energized, it is preparing to enter commercial operations, according to Harmony Energy. The site is a standalone BESS, located directly next to the 55 MW Skeeby Solar Farm, a former Harmony Energy site that it sold in 2023, though it retained the battery project. ESS News understands the project utilizes Tesla Megapack 2XL models, which Harmony has used at other projects, including its Bumpers and Little Raith projects. There are a clear 10 bays of batteries, and Wilson Power Solutions said on its website that it supplied ten 4.2MVA 33kV/480-480V Wilson T2 Ecotrans large distribution transformers and one 100kVA 33kV/433V Wilson auxiliary distribution transformer. It also dug into some of the electrical specifics, saying: “ Our Wilson T2 MV Transformers are custom-engineered to Tier 2 loss levels to interface directly with the site’s Tesla Megapack battery units via a dual 480-480V LV winding configuration. Each unit has twin 480V secondary windings in a Dyn11yn5 configuration, feeding two Megapack groups from a single transformer. ” It also added details of fire-safety improvements. Swiss-ownership Skeeby is part of Harmony Energy’s strategy to build longer-duration storage assets, and it is the company’s first site to go live since July’s announcement that Swiss electricity producer Alpiq had acquired a 90 percent stake in Harmony Energy . The acquisition added approximately 400 MW of assets under construction to Alpiq’s existing BESS portfolio in Europe. Despite the acquisition, Harmony Energy will continue to operate independently, while CEO and co-founder Peter Kavanagh retains a stake in Harmony Energy. Alpiq’s head of BESS, Christoph Bellin, has joined Harmony Energy’s executive management team, while continuing in his role at Alpiq. “Skeeby is an exciting milestone for Harmony Energy, not only because it brings another important battery storage project online, but because it is the first site to be energized since our strategic investment from Alpiq,” Kavanagh said. “That investment gives us additional backing to accelerate the delivery of projects like this across the U.K. and Europe, while continuing to operate with the same team, brand and development expertise that have underpinned Harmony Energy’s growth to date.” In 2025, Harmony Energy commissioned its 100 MW / 200 MWh Chevire BESS at the port of Nantes–Saint‑Nazaire in France. title: Saudi Arabia awards $1.16 billion for 8 GWh of battery storage; ACWA Power, Engie win big - Energy Storage
content: The Saudi Power Procurement Company (SPPC) has signed four storage service agreements for the first group of its independent battery energy storage system (BESS) projects, covering a combined capacity of 2,000 MW, and with a four hour duration for 8,000 MWh. With the SPPC acting as the Principal Buyer in the deal, and projects supervised by the Ministry of Energy, the deal across four projects is for a total investment of more than $1.16 billion. The four large-scale projects, each rated at 500 MW / 2000 MWh, will be delivered under a build-own-operate (BOO) model as has been flagged throughout the tender proecess. Three of the projects – Al Muwyah BESS ISP and Haden BESS ISP in the Makkah Region, and Al Kahafa BESS ISP in the Hail Region – were awarded to a consortium comprising Saudi Energy, ACWA Power, and Al Sharif Contracting and Commercial Development Company, representing the majority of the wins. The fourth development, the Al Khushaybi BESS ISP in the Qassim Region was awarded to a consortium comprising France’s Engie and Haji Abdullah Alireza & Co. The four sites each aim to support the integration of utility-scale renewables into the Kingdom’s electricity system, enhancing operational flexibility and support the security of supply. The accompanying press release noted this will also bolster Saudi Arabia’s global leadership in the energy sector. ‘Vision 2030’ Driven by Vision 2030, Saudi Arabia continues to scale up its renewable energy and storage ambitions, targeting 48 GWh of battery energy storage capacity by 2030. SPPC launched the tender for this initial 8 GWh group in November 2024, and a total of 33 local, regional, and international companies were prequalified for that initial round in December 2024 .. Under the tender structure, the winning consortiums hold 100% equity in special purpose vehicles (SPVs) responsible for developing and operating the assets, backed by 15-year Storage Services Agreements (SSAs) with SPPC. As previously reported by ESS News , SPPC launched the qualification process for the second group in April 2026 . The second tender comprises six projects with a cumulative capacity of 3 GW/12 GWh. In July 2026, SPPC announced a prequalification list of 27 companies for this group , including major global players such as Masdar, EDF, TotalEnergies, and China Longyuan Power Group. title: Solrite expands residential solar-plus-storage VPP to Illinois - Energy Storage
content: Solrite Energy has launched its residential virtual power plant power purchase agreement (VPA) in Illinois, making the program available to qualifying homeowners in the ComEd and Ameren service territories. Under the agreement, Solrite will provide homeowners with a home solar installation and a 60 kWh home battery at zero upfront cost. The company will then sell the solar energy to the homeowner at a rate of $0.12/kWh, with a 2.9% annual price increase over a 25-year term. At that price, the Solrite PPA could represent substantial savings over time for homeowners who sign up for the plan. The $0.12/kWh price is approximately 33% lower than ComEd’s current bundled electricity price of approximately $0.18/kWh, while the 2.9% annual increase is less than the 25-year average annual increase of 3.26% in Illinois electricity prices, according to data from the U.S. Energy Information Administration . Customers who opt to sign up for a battery-only version of the VPA plan pay a flat fee of $20 per month over a 20-year term. These installations can operate in conjunction with a customer’s existing solar installation (pending compatibility verification), or on a standalone basis. The company’s public-facing marketing materials indicate the batteries are supplied by Duracell. The expansion into Illinois is intended to address the state’s changing residential solar market. Full retail net metering for new solar customers in Illinois ended on Jan. 1, 2025, which reduced the financial viability of solar-only home installations. Solrite says its batteries can be a lifeline for Illinois homeowners whose systems were installed after the net metering rules ended, helping them store and use all the solar energy their systems generate and avoid sending energy to the grid for pennies on the dollar in credits. While the installations include a large battery, the company generally does not guarantee a set level of backup energy will be available at any given time. That’s due to the economic value of the stored energy that the company can realize through its VPP operations. Solrite operates its fleet of batteries as a grid-supporting resource, capable of storing generated solar energy on-site, shaving household peaks, and charging and discharging in response to grid conditions. Illinois is the fifth state in which Solrite has rolled out its VPP offering, following programs in Texas, California, Connecticut, and Massachusetts, and given the state’s raft of incentives, it may be among the most lucrative for the company. In addition to revenues from energy sales and payments from grid operators, Solrite earns federal and state incentives, including payments for renewable energy credits (RECs) under the Illinois Shines adjustable block program. Current REC prices in Illinois are between about $70/MWh and $80/MWh, depending on the utility territory where the system is installed. Approved Vendors under the program are paid those prices for all the megawatt-hours a system is likely to generate over the first 15 years of operation. content:
Peter Johnson

opened orders for the Great Han, its new flagship electric sedan that can drive over 1,000 km (621 mi) on a single charge, starting at under $40,000.
BYD opens orders for the flagship Great Han EV
The Great Han, or Da Han as it’s called in China, is the first D-segment flagship sedan under BYD’s Dynasty family.
a sneak peek
of the new full-size sedan in June after it was revealed in the batch of new energy vehicles approved for sale by China’s MIIT (Ministry of Industry and Information Technology).
Lu Tian, the general manager of BYD’s Dynasty series, confirmed last month that the Great Han would be revealed in full at the Chengdu Motor Show, teasing that “more surprises await.”
Tian also confirmed the electric sedan will offer a CLTC driving range of up to 1,008 km (626 miles) on a single charge.
BYD opened pre-orders for the new Great Han at the event, starting at just 249,900 yuan, or about $37,200.
BYD Great Han (Da Han) flagship electric sedan (Soure: Lu Tian)
The flagship sedan is available in three variants with single and all-wheel drive powertrains. Two rear-wheel drive (RWD) options are available: Premium and Flagship, starting at 249,900 yuan ($37,2000) and 269,900 yuan ($40,200).
Both are powered by a single 370 kW (496 hp) motor and 102.326 kWh battery, providing a CLTC driving range of up to 1,008 km (626 miles).
The AWD variant adds a frton electric motor for a combined 570 kW (764 hp). Although it uses the same battery pack as the RWD variants, the AWD version has a CLTC range of 880 km (546 miles).
All Great Han variants are equipped with BYD’s Blade Battery 2.0 and Flash Charging technology. The setup enables vehicles equipped with the new batteries to recharge from 10% to 70% in just 5 minutes using 1,500 kW technology. For a full recharge (10% to 97%), it takes just 9 minutes.
Measuring 5,256 mm in length, 1,999 mm in width, and 1,510 mm in height, with a wheelbase of 3,130 mm, BYD’s flagship sedan is bigger than the Tesla Model S and Lucid Air. It’s closer in size to the long-wheelbase Mercedes S-Class.
Like the flagship Great Tang SUV, BYD said the sedan is loaded with premium standard features, including its DiSus-A dual chamber air suspension system, rear-wheel steering, and zero gravity front seats.
All Great Han variants are also equipped with BYD’s God’s Eye B smart driving system, offering ADAS features like Navigation on Autopilot and remote parking.
The new flagship sedan is part of BYD’s broader push into higher end segments following the Great Tang SUV and several new vehicles under its premium Denza brand.

title: Heybike launches low cost 28 MPH full-suspension moped-style e-bike
content:
Micah Toll
| Aug 24 2026 - 4:55 am PT
Heybike is expanding into a rather different corner of the e-bike market with the launch of the new Heybike Titan, a full-suspension, moped-style electric bike that can be had with either one or two batteries.
And perhaps just as importantly, Heybike is coming out swinging on price.
The new Titan
starts at $1,499
for the single-battery version, while the dual-battery model carries
an MSRP of $1,799
. Early-bird pricing knocks another $100 off each, bringing them down to $1,399 and $1,699, respectively.
That’s some pretty aggressive pricing for this style of bike, especially once you get into the dual-battery version.
But what do you get for that price?
The Titan is powered by a 750W rear hub motor rated for a claimed 1,500W of peak power and 65 Nm of torque. It ships configured as a Class 2 e-bike with a 20 mph (32 km/h) top speed, though Heybike says riders can use the company’s app to adjust the bike up to 28 mph (45 km/h).
The bike also carries UL 2849 certification, which covers the entire electrical system and is becoming increasingly important as more cities, retailers, landlords, and consumers pay attention to e-bike battery safety.
But the more interesting part of the Titan is probably its battery setup.
The single-battery model uses a 48V 15Ah battery, or 720 Wh, and Heybike claims up to 40 miles (64 km) of range. Opt for the dual-battery version and you’re effectively getting 1,440 Wh of capacity, with Heybike doubling its maximum range estimate to 80 miles (129 km).
As always, take those maximum range figures with the usual grain of salt. Riding a heavy moped-style e-bike at higher speeds and relying heavily on the throttle is going to chew through batteries much more quickly. Going full balls to the wall could leave you with half of that range, but the point is that dual batteries are definitely going to take you further, and so having the dual-battery option is a nice feature here.
There are
plenty of moped-style e-bikes and plenty of dual-battery e-bikes,
but the Venn diagram gets considerably smaller when you’re looking for a moped-style bike that combines dual batteries with actual front and rear suspension.
The Titan gets an 80mm-travel hydraulic front fork and 55mm of rear suspension travel, with the rear comprised of dual coil-over shocks as compared to the more common bicycle-style mono-shock setup. Add in those chunky 20 x 4-inch tires, and you’ve got the basic recipe for the increasingly popular mini-moto style of e-bike that prioritizes comfort, cruising, and a motorcycle-inspired riding experience.
Hydraulic brakes are included as well, and the bike has a 300 lb (136 kg) maximum payload rating. Heybike has even fitted rear footrests and describes the long saddle as “two-up ready,” though that same 300 lb payload limit is worth keeping in mind before inviting a friend aboard.
At 85 lb (38.4 kg) for the single-battery version and 93 lb (42.1 kg) with two batteries, nobody is going to confuse the Titan for a lightweight commuter. But that’s increasingly beside the point with this category. These bikes are basically designed to bring a bit of small-motorcycle swagger to an e-bike platform.
And that’s also what makes the Titan an interesting move for Heybike.
The company has traditionally focused much more heavily on conventional fat-tire commuters, folders, step-through bikes, and other mainstream value-oriented e-bikes. The Titan is a pretty clear attempt to reach into the youth-oriented, moped-style segment that has exploded in popularity.
In fact, Heybike isn’t exactly hiding that ambition. Its own marketing materials explicitly identify “trendsetters,” “teen cruisers,” and “parent buyers” among the Titan’s target audiences, while leaning heavily into the bike’s social, customizable and mini-moto image. There’s even a glow-in-the-dark sticker kit included for riders who want to personalize the bike.
That helps explain the aggressive pricing, too. Heybike appears to be trying to go past just adding another variation of an existing commuter here; the company is looking to enter a new part of the market and appears ready to buy itself some market share.
At $1,399 for an early single-battery Titan or $1,699 for the dual-battery version, Heybike is making a pretty compelling argument on the spec sheet. The latter in particular packs full suspension, hydraulic brakes, a 1,500W peak motor and nearly 1.5 kWh of battery into a price point where plenty of competing moped-style bikes still make you choose between range, suspension, or spending considerably more.
That said, we’ll have to see how the Titan rides before knowing whether that aggressive value translates from the spec sheet to the street. Compared to other new entrants to this market, like the
revamped Juiced Scrambler
, which is marginally more expensive but offers higher-end components and is designed to actually be pedalable, the Titan is going to have to demonstrate that it can offer a good ride and not just a good price. But for Heybike’s first serious swing at this increasingly crowded moped-style e-bike market, the company certainly isn’t easing its way in.

title: Tesla loses another top chip engineer to ex-Dojo startup DensityAI
content:
Fred Lambert
| Aug 24 2026 - 6:09 am PT
Tesla has lost another senior chip engineer to DensityAI, the AI hardware startup built out of its own former Dojo team. Shishuang Sun, who spent more than five years as a Tesla AI hardware architect on Dojo and the Autopilot computers, now lists his role as “Packaging and System Hardware” at DensityAI, starting in July.
This is not a junior loss. Sun left Tesla as Senior Director of AI Hardware Design — one of the people responsible for turning Tesla’s custom silicon into working systems, exactly the expertise Tesla needs as it stakes its valuation on in-house AI chips.
A Tesla chip veteran, twice over
Sun’s career traces the entire arc of Tesla’s in-house silicon ambition. According to his LinkedIn history, he first joined Tesla’s Autopilot hardware group during the Jim Keller era, when Tesla was assembling the team that would design its first Full Self-Driving computer and cut its dependence on Nvidia.
He left around the time that chapter wound down, spending just over two years at Waymo as a hardware engineering manager, where he ran the design verification, signal and power integrity, EMC, and PCB teams that make up the guts of self-driving hardware.
Then he came back. Sun rejoined Tesla in January 2021 as a principal engineer on AI hardware for both Dojo and Autopilot, and was promoted to Senior Director of AI Hardware Design in April 2025. His work covered IC packaging, vertical power modules, signal and power integrity, PCB design, and system thermal and mechanical engineering — the discipline of taking a chip design and making it survive in the real world.
The startup was built out of Tesla’s Dojo team
DensityAI is not a random competitor. As
we reported when Tesla shut Dojo down
in August 2025, the startup was founded by former Dojo chief Ganesh Venkataramanan, with roughly 20 members of Tesla’s supercomputer team following him out the door. Fellow Tesla veteran Bill Chang is CTO.
The company is building chips, hardware, and software for AI data centers aimed at automotive, robotics, and industrial customers — effectively the mission Tesla walked away from when it killed Dojo and shifted to Nvidia for training compute.
Losing packaging talent at the worst possible time
Sun’s specialty — advanced packaging and system integration — is the part of chipmaking that has become the industry’s real bottleneck. Getting the transistor design right is only half the job; getting power into the chip and heat out of it, at scale, is where high-performance AI silicon lives or dies.
Tesla is leaning on custom silicon harder than ever. It
taped out its long-delayed AI5 chip in April
, nearly two years behind Musk’s original timeline, with volume production not expected until mid-2027. AI6 is slated for Samsung’s 2nm process, which has hit yield problems, and Musk has floated a “Dojo 3” on top of that. On the manufacturing side, Tesla and SpaceX are pitching the
$20 billion-plus “Terafab” chip factory in Austin
Every one of those bets depends on people who can turn a tape-out into a shipping product — the packaging, power delivery, and thermal work that Sun did at Tesla for five years.
Electrek’s Take
DensityAI has now pulled in Tesla’s former Dojo leadership, roughly 20 of its engineers, and — a full year later — a sitting Senior Director of AI hardware, who appeared to be promoted into an exec role after the talent drain.
It shows continued bleeding, well after Tesla supposedly regrouped around AI5 and AI6. When a company pins its entire valuation on becoming an AI and robotics chip player, the steady loss of the people who actually build that hardware matters.
The irony is hard to miss. Tesla killed Dojo, watched the team spin up a competitor. Custom silicon is a people business before it’s a fab business, and right now the people are moving in one direction.

title: Watch Tesla FSD v14 Lite drive over a giant log without stopping
content:
A Tesla owner posted dashcam footage of his car driving straight over a log lying across the road while running Full Self-Driving (FSD) v14.1 Lite, without braking or slowing down.
The clip has more than 800,000 views, and it adds to a growing list of problems we’ve documented with Tesla’s “Lite” version of FSD on older Hardware 3 cars.
In the video, posted by X user @donvarri on August 21, the car is on a wet, foggy rural road with the “Self-Driving” visualization active at 32 mph. A log sits across the lane. The Tesla runs right over it. No braking, no swerve.
“Mine drove over a log in the road it def wouldn’t have stopped,” the owner wrote. He later confirmed the car is a Hardware 3 vehicle running the latest v14.1 Lite build.
The problems with v14 Lite keep stacking up
FSD v14 Lite is a compressed version of the HW4 v14 model, squeezed onto HW3’s memory-constrained AI3 computer, which has 8GB of RAM and roughly one-eighth the bandwidth of the newer hardware. Tesla started rolling it out to Hardware 3 cars in June.
Since then, the reports haven’t been good.
Owners have documented HW3 computers overheating under the extra processing load, triggering an APP_w141_ECU_Thermal_Issue fault above 90°C, with some temperatures hitting 96°C. In several cases the system threw “red hands” and forced a disengagement, and a few computers shut down entirely and needed replacement. On top of that, drivers reported phantom braking, hesitation, and brake stuttering.
Tesla shipped v14.1 Lite partly to address the overheating. This log incident is on that supposedly improved build.
And the bigger issue hasn’t gone anywhere. HW3 simply can’t deliver the unsupervised autonomy Tesla sold, the company has admitted it has no clear plan to get there, and it sold roughly 4 million cars as “full self-driving capable” for as much as $15,000.
The complacency problem, in the driver’s own words
The replies quickly turned into a fight about whose fault it was. Several people told the owner he should have been watching the road and intervened.
His answer is the whole story: “2 things can be true I should have been paying attention but the car definitely should have stopped.”
That’s the trap with a Level 2 system that’s good most of the time. One commenter put the blame squarely on the driver: “No, YOU allowed that to happen for the opportunity to post a video, by failing to properly supervise.” The owner pushed back that he’s no Tesla hater, that he’s driven 70,000 miles, and that it’s the best car he’s ever owned.
But here’s the problem. The better FSD gets at routine driving, the more the driver relaxes. And that’s exactly when it plows over an obstacle a human would have caught from a hundred feet away. The system trains its own supervisor to stop supervising.
Electrek’s Take
Both things are true. He should have been paying attention, and the car should have stopped for a log in the middle of the road at 32 mph. Blaming the driver lets the system off the hook, and blaming the system ignores what supervision is for.
Top comment by Beario
I paid for autonomy on the two cars that we have with FSD. What we have is a system that we use sparingly on the highway on long trips. It CANNOT be trusted because it is not capable of doing what it was intended to do. The hardware just can't and now we are just shy of a hardware 5 which is 2 full hardware upgrades ahead. I fully do not expect Tesla to do anything as they will wait for the cars to disappear with time. The lawsuits pending in Europe are the right move and it most certainly should be done the same here. Tesla should be held accountable yesterday with lawsuits, not tomorrow.
I’ve been on the wrong end of this. Almost a decade ago I had a similar but less severe accident in a Model 3, and it still cost my insurers around $15,000 in suspension and frame repair. Hitting a solid log at 32 mph is a lot more violent than what I went through. I wouldn’t be surprised if this car ends up totaled once someone looks at the underbody.
To think that the driver would have done it on purpose is ridiculous.
The complacency issue is real, but it’s a design problem as much as a driver problem. Tesla keeps pushing more capable software onto hardware it already admitted can’t do the job, and the result is a system smooth enough to lull you and brittle enough to run over a log. HW3 owners paid for autonomy. What are they actually getting?

title: XPeng robotics raises $900M at $6.3B valuation for IRON robot push
content:
XPeng’s robotics business has raised over $900 million at a post-money valuation of more than $6.3 billion, the Chinese EV maker announced today. XPeng calls it the largest single-round private financing in the history of China’s embodied AI industry.
The round is meant to push XPeng’s IRON humanoid robot into mass production by the end of 2026 — a timeline that keeps the automaker ahead of Tesla’s stalling Optimus program.
A record raise, and a carve-out
The financing was led by IDG Capital, with participation from Gaorong Ventures and strategic backing from Tencent and Alibaba, according to XPeng.
The company frames the round as validation of its “leadership in Physical AI” and its “ability to scale production.” Of the $900 million-plus committed, roughly $600 million comes from external investors, with about $200 million from an XPeng subsidiary and $100 million from leadership.
The raise comes alongside a corporate restructuring. XPeng is spinning its robotics assets, IP, and staff into a standalone subsidiary over the next 18 months while retaining roughly 82% ownership, which keeps the unit consolidated on the group’s financial statements but gives it a separate market valuation. CEO He Xiaopeng took direct control of the robotics business in June 2026.
What IRON actually is
XPeng unveiled the next-generation IRON at its AI Day event in November 2025, where the robot’s fluid, human-like walk was so convincing that online viewers accused the company of hiding a person in a costume. He Xiaopeng responded by cutting open the robot’s leg on stage to reveal the wiring underneath.
The hardware is genuinely ambitious. IRON carries 76 degrees of freedom across its body and 21 in each hand, wrapped in what XPeng calls a “fully enclosed flexible lattice structure” — a synthetic skin meant to balance safety and a human-like appearance.
On the compute side, IRON runs three of XPeng’s in-house Turing AI chips delivering a combined 2,250 TOPS. That lets the company run its Physical AI foundation model directly on the robot, which XPeng says allows IRON to “autonomously perform complex tasks without remote operation.”
Rival humanoid demos are frequently teleoperated by humans off-camera, and XPeng is explicitly claiming on-device autonomy — a claim that will be worth scrutinizing once IRON is in customers’ hands rather than on a stage.
The manufacturing argument
Top comment by BCGeiger
This is why right now I wouldn't touch Tesla stock. Their cars are old with aged and increasingly second class technology. Sales are dropping because of it. Musk is betting the company on two things. Grok, which is an also-ran that almost nobody outside of X is using because it is massively worse than the top AI systems. And Optimus which is a decade or more behind the top systems from Chinese, European, or even other US companies. Musk's hat is out of rabbits. It's going to be a brutal few years for the markets and Musk.
Keep in mind that 1929 was almost exactly 100 years ago. History repeating and all that.
XPeng’s core pitch is that it can bring “automotive-grade quality standards and large-scale mass production” to humanoid robots by leaning on the supply chain and factories it built for EVs.
XPeng reported 103,295 vehicle deliveries in the second quarter of 2026, up 64.8% quarter-over-quarter, so the company is scaling actual hardware at volume right now. It says the robotics unit is targeting monthly capacity of more than 1,000 IRON units and has floated a goal of 1 million units by 2030.
The plan is for IRON to enter mass production by the end of 2026, starting inside XPeng’s own stores and campuses, before an official launch with deliveries in China and overseas markets in 2027.

content:
集邦光储观察获悉，近期，锂电及储能产业项目持续推进，中创新航、海阔电源、鹿文科技分别推进磷酸铁锂材料、储能系统集成等项目。
中创新航新建30万吨磷酸铁锂项目
近日，立鼎材料科技（四川）有限公司年产30万吨磷酸铁锂材料项目进行第一次环评公示。
项目位于四川眉山彭山经开区，总投资33.6亿元，拟新建磷酸铁锂材料生产线及配套生产、辅助设施。项目建成后，预计形成年产30万吨磷酸铁锂材料的生产能力。
据了解，立鼎材料为中创新航旗下企业，叠加此前已建成的10万吨磷酸铁锂产能，中创新航在眉山规划的磷酸铁锂总产能将达到40万吨/年。
海阔电源储能锂电池项目建成投产
近日，南阳市海阔电源有限公司储能锂离子电池及系统集成生产项目在河南镇平县建成投产。
项目位于镇平县开发区，总投资3.28亿元，布局钢壳、软包锂电池生产线及正负极材料配套生产线，覆盖储能电池研发、生产及系统集成等环节，产品主要应用于户用、小型工商业及便携储能等场景。
鹿文科技推进10GWh储能系统集成项目
8月18日，安徽鹿文科技有限公司年产10GWh储能系统集成项目（重新报批）环评文件拟获马鞍山市和县生态环境分局审批。
据了解，该项目规划产能为10GWh，项目建成后将新增储能系统集成产能。此次环评进入拟审批公示阶段，意味着项目建设推进进一步落地。

title: 智光电气/派能科技/果下科技发布最新业绩
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，近期，智光电气、派能科技、果下科技相继披露2026年半年度业绩。上半年，三家企业储能业务均保持较快增长。
8月23日晚，广州智光电气股份有限公司披露2026年半年度报告。报告期内，公司实现营业收入22.69亿元，同比增长38.06%；归属于上市公司股东的净利润4383.50万元，同比增长179.48%，实现扭亏为盈；扣除非经常性损益后的净利润4175.90万元，同比增长175.78%。
报告期内，公司储能设备销售及系统集成业务订单保持快速增长，由于上半年电芯价格波动较大导致部分项目交付节奏放缓而未能及时确认收入，报告期实现营业收入9.19亿元；公司已采取多种措施保障电芯供应及合理的成本控制，进一步保障下半年相关项目的及时交付，预计储能设备销售及系统集成业务全年仍将实现较快增长。
独立储能电站业务成为上半年业绩的重要组成部分。报告期内，智光电气投资的清远电站二期、三期于6月进入商业运行，平远电站一期于3月进入商业运营。上半年，公司独立储能电站运营业务实现营业收入1.54亿元，净利润1.09亿元。5月，公司完成对平远恒元少数股东股权的收购，实现100%持股，并计划推进平远二期项目商业运营。
产能方面，截至2026年6月30日，智光电气已拥有云埔、南沙、永和、增城（在建）四个生产制造基地，大型储能系统年产能达到15GWh。
8月21日晚，派能科技披露2026年半年度报告。上半年，公司实现营业收入26.44亿元，同比增长130.07%；归母净利润7928.62万元，同比增长469.92%；扣非净利润2651.88万元。
报告期内，公司持续优化销售端和研发端资源配置，随着国际储能市场需求持续增长，公司欧洲、中东、东南亚地区家储及工商业储能需求持续放量，国际市场销售快速增长；同时国内轻型动力业务持续增长，加之国内业务毛利情况得到改善，整体盈利能力提升。
从业务来看，储能仍是主要收入来源。上半年，公司储能电池系统收入22.60亿元，轻型动力电池及其他业务收入3.55亿元。2026年上半年的产品销售量为3431MWh，同比增长158.36%。二季度产品销售量2254MWh，同比增长143.15%，环比增长91.50%。
产品方面，派能科技继续向大容量储能电芯及系统拓展。报告期内，公司发布基于588Ah大电芯的6.25MWh、0.5C电池储能系统，以及基于601Ah大电芯的8MWh、0.25C长时储能系统；同时推出73.6kWh单簇容量、可扩展至294.4kWh的工商业储能产品，以及60kW/126kWh四合一储能系统。
钠离子电池也是公司重点布局方向。上半年，派能科技针对新能源车辅助电源、轻型动力及储能市场推出多款钠电产品，其中储能领域开发了300Ah以上大容量铝壳钠离子电芯，循环寿命超过1万次。
在产能方面，派能科技持续推进电芯及储能系统产线建设。公司称，安徽子公司软包电芯产线已实现国际家储和共享换电电池稳定交付，轻型动力PACK产线及工商业储能系统产线生产效率持续提升。目前，公司已形成以软包规模化制造为基础、铝壳电芯柔性供应为补充的制造体系。
8月20日，果下科技股份有限公司披露2026年半年度业绩公告。报告期内，公司实现营业收入14.27亿元，同比增长106.5%；毛利2.74亿元，同比增长217.7%；期间利润6024.7万元，同比增长980.7%；毛利率为19.2%，较上年同期提升6.7%，盈利质量与经营效率同步改善。
储能系统解决方案仍是果下科技主要收入来源。上半年，公司储能系统解决方案收入12.84亿元，同比增长100.6%，占总营收的90.0%。其中，大型储能系统收入10.38亿元，同比增长102.4%；户用储能系统收入2.34亿元，同比增长87.0%；工商业储能系统收入1229.6万元。
出货方面，2026年上半年果下科技国内储能系统出货量达到3.7GWh，同比增长105.6%。公司表示，国内大型储能项目需求持续增长，同时全球储能市场增速加快以及海外市场拓展力度加大，共同推动储能系统解决方案收入增长。
产能布局方面，果下科技上半年新增成都及连云港两大生产基地，形成四大生产基地格局，并推进大型储能智能化产线建设及户用储能产线扩容。推进各基地数字化转型，逐步降低对外部代工的依赖；并通过全球供应链整合、精益化生产与规模化采购，有效缓冲原材料价格波动，保障盈利水平稳定。
下半年，公司表示将继续推进储能系统产品研发，深化国内大型独立储能电站市场，同时重点拓展欧洲和非洲市场，并推进虚拟电厂及“绿电—储能—算力”等业务。

title: 注资合计超4.15亿元，又3家储能新公司设立
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，近期，海博思创、宁德时代、易储数智分别成立3家储能新公司，业务覆盖风光储能项目开发、电池制造等方向。
海博思创合资设立新公司
8月18日，滨州博创棣滨新能源科技有限公司成立。
据企查查显示，该新公司注册资本1000万元，由海博思创全资子公司博清智滨（无棣）新能源科技有限公司持股55%，北京远晔新能源科技有限公司持股45%。
新公司选址山东省滨州市无棣县，经营范围涵盖风力发电技术服务、太阳能发电技术服务、储能技术服务、工程和技术研究和试验发展等，主要承担山东区域风光储能项目开发相关业务。
宁德时代设立雅安新材料公司
8月20日，宁德时代（雅安）新材料科技有限公司成立，注册资本4亿元。
企查查显示，该公司由宁德时代100%持股，法定代表人为吴锡雄，注册地位于四川省雅安市经济技术开发区滨河东路11号。
新公司经营范围包括新材料技术研发、电子专用材料制造、有色金属合金制造、常用有色金属冶炼、矿物洗选加工、资源再生利用技术研发、化工产品销售（不含危险化学品）、以自有资金从事投资活动等，加码电池上游材料与资源再生板块布局。
易储数智再成立储能新公司
8月11日，青海晏储新盛能源科技有限公司成立。
新公司注册资本500万元，注册地址位于青海省海北州海晏县绿色产业园区。企查查信息显示，该公司由易储数智旗下子公司深圳安达新盛能源科技有限公司100%持股。
新公司经营范围包含电池制造、电池零配件销售、光伏设备制造销售、储能技术服务、新能源原动设备制造、资源再生利用技术研发、合同能源管理、软件开发等，聚焦储能电池及新能源装备业务。

title: 超1GWh，晶科/阳光电源等5企获储能订单
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，近期，天启鸿源、三晶电气、晶科储能、阳光电源、华为数字能源等5家企业，相继披露全球储能订单签约合作情况。
天启鸿源签约英国1GWh储能合作
8月21日，天启鸿源宣布近日签约英国储能产品供应合作项目，合作规模1GWh。
根据签约内容，本次合作规模为1GWh，其中首批订单250MWh将于一年内交付，后续750MWh订单将稳步落地。双方将依托各自在技术、产能及本土资源优势，聚焦英国社区能源改造、基础设施绿色升级场景开展深度合作。
此前，8月16日，英国客户来到天津启鸿储能科技有限公司开展实地考察，先后走访产品展厅、标准化生产车间、储能成套产线与产品测试中心。天启鸿源自研的户用浸没式储能系统赢得英方客户高度认可。
三晶电气签约澳洲储能分销商
8月21日，三晶电气宣布，与澳洲顶级分销商Supply Partners达成重磅深度战略合作。SupplyPartners正式成为三晶电气澳洲市场储能解决方案授权分销商。
依托本次战略合作，三晶电气全新EK70一体化储能系统即将于澳洲正式上市。除EK70户用储能系统外，三晶电气B2S分体式储能系统、工商业储能产品也将同步通过Supply Partners覆盖澳洲市场。
晶科储能部署23MWh工商储项目
8月20日，晶科储能宣布，已于近日在山东滨州完成90台SunGiga 261kWh工商业储能系统的部署。
据悉，项目总规模达23.49MWh。SunGiga 261kWh采用高度集成的一体化设计，支持最多12台系统并联，并与站级EMS协同，实现多台储能设备的统一管理与灵活调度。
项目通过储能系统与现场光伏、用电负荷及电动汽车充电设施协同运行，构建“发-网-荷-储”一体化解决方案，探索工商业储能新路径。
阳光电源获菲律宾储能订单
8月15日，壳牌能源（Shell Energy）发布消息，宣布其位于菲律宾巴丹省的Hermosa电池储能系统项目取得重要进展，与阳光电源菲律宾公司和Power Dimension签署储能系统供货和EPC协议，规模为30MW/60MWh。
据悉，该项目将采用阳光电源的PowerTitan 3.0液冷储能系统，提供2h的储能容量。阳光电源菲律宾公司将根据长期服务协议提供持续的维护和运营支持；Power Dimension则主要负责项目的土建设计、电气工程、设备采购等。
华为数字能源获马尔代夫储能订单
8月13日，Solmacher Solar Energy官宣，已与华为数字能源签署供货协议。根据协议，华为将为马尔代夫皇家瑰丽度假岛的智能微网项目供应电池储能系统以及公用事业级、工商业逆变器，规模为40MWh。
据悉，华为数字能源将为该项目提供储能及逆变器整套解决方案。该项目配套16MW光伏电站、40MWh储能系统与柴油发电机组，建成后将成为马尔代夫同类型规模最大的项目。

title: US steelmaker shifts $500m federal hydrogen funds to upgrade coal blast furnace
content:

US steelmaker Cleveland-Cliffs will use $500m in federal funds originally intended to transition its Ohio ironworks to “hydrogen-ready” operations to instead upgrade its coal-fired blast furnace.
Coming 14 months after the company officially abandoned its hydrogen-based steel project in Middletown, it has now established a framework to negotiate and implement a rescoping of the $500m awarded by the Biden administration.
It said the funds would now go toward a $1bn project to make upgrades to its blast furnace, install advanced material handling infrastructure, and AI-enabled process control technologies.
The firm will also look to construct a cogeneration facility to capture and use blast furnace gas to generate electricity and steam for on-site consumption.
It expects the blast furnace to be rebuilt in the first quarter of 2030.
The Inflation Reduction Act funds were awarded to
Cleveland-Cliffs in 2024
to convert its Middletown blast furnace to hydrogen direct reduced iron operations.
In a statement on the new funding use, Goncalves said, “The [Department of Energy’s] support for this project is a testament to the importance of preserving the blast furnace route to produce automotive-exposed grade steels in the US, while advancing American energy dominance.”
Speaking at the Middletown Works, Vice-President JD Vance said the new programme would “protect and create tonnes of new jobs.”
The rescoping comes amid a wider retreat from Biden-era clean energy funding under the Trump administration, which has sought to redirect federal energy policy toward fossil fuels, nuclear power, and projects it considers supportive of US energy security.
In 2025, the DOE terminated hundreds of awards worth more than $11bn across two major rounds of cuts, affecting industrial decarbonisation, carbon capture, grid, and hydrogen projects. Among the casualties were the California and Pacific Northwest regional
clean hydrogen hubs
, which were awarded a combined $2.2bn.
The cuts have added uncertainty around the US clean hydrogen sector when developers are already contending with high costs, limited offtake, and policy uncertainty.

title: Europe’s EV Sales Explode, Now Making Up A Quarter Of New Cars
content:
Europe’s EV Sales Explode, Now Making Up A Quarter Of New Cars
Rising fuel prices are convincing more and more Europeans that electric cars are worth it in the long run.
- European EV sales shot up by 51% last month.
- The rise in fuel prices has convinced more people to switch to electric, boosting the powertrain’s market share.
- One in four new cars sold in Europe was an EV last month.
Europeans’ appetite for electric cars is not slowing down. Last month, EV sales in the region went up by 51% compared to the same month last year, leading to a crisp 25% market share for this type of powertrain, according to Dataforce, which crunched the numbers from 98% of all new car registrations in the European Union, United Kingdom, Iceland, Norway, and Switzerland.
In the first seven months of 2026, EV sales grew 37% compared to the same period last year, helping the entire industry keep its numbers in the green. By comparison, the entire European car market went up by 4.1% last month and 5.7% from January through July.
The compact Skoda Elroq was Europe's best-selling EV in July.
The growth of EV sales outpaced plug-in hybrids and traditional hybrids, too, with PHEV sales rising by 15% in July, while full-hybrid sales were up 9%. Rising fuel prices and an ever-expanding lineup of electric cars are more than likely the main drivers behind the sustained growth of EV registrations in Europe.
France and Germany, two of the biggest car markets in Europe, are leading the EV boom, with more and more battery-powered vehicles hitting the roads every month. In July, France hit a 35% EV share, with over 44,000 registrations. Meanwhile, full-electric cars reached a 29.3% share last month, with nearly 79,000 registrations.
In total, 277,006 EVs were registered in Europe last month, and none of Tesla’s models are at the top of the list. The Skoda Elroq was the best-selling EV in the region, followed by the Volkswagen ID.4 and the Renault 5 E-Tech. However, the Tesla Model Y is still the best-selling EV in Europe after the first seven months of the year, with 115,759 registrations, an increase of 55%. Skoda’s Elroq is second, with 67,679 units, followed by the Tesla Model 3 with 57,086 cars sold.
When it comes to plug-in hybrids, Chinese marques have swept in and captured a huge chunk of the market. Unlike EVs, Chinese-made PHEVs are not subject to hiked import tariffs, so they can be sold at lower prices than locally made models. Overall, PHEV sales went up to 125,530 cars in July, a 15% increase over the same month last year. Chinese models held a 34% share and took over nearly half of the top 10 list. The BYD Seal U was the best-selling PHEV in Europe last month, followed by the BYD Atto 2. The Jaecoo 7 was fourth.
