title: Alpiq buys 103.5-MW operational battery storage plant in Germany
content:
Swiss power producer and energy service provider Alpiq has acquired a 103.5-MW/238-MWh operational battery energy storage system (BESS) in northern Germany from German-Norwegian developer ECO STOR.
The facility, located in Bollingstedt in the state of Schleswig-Holstein, was commissioned in June 2025 and is one of Germany's largest operational battery storage systems. It marks Alpiq's first operational large-scale battery storage asset in Germany.
The financial terms of the transaction were not disclosed.
Bollingstedt is the third and currently largest operational BESS in Alpiq's portfolio, following the
100-MW Chevire
project in France and the
30-MW Valkeakoski
system in Finland. The company also has more than 250 MW of battery storage projects under construction or nearing commissioning, with additional developments planned in Italy and Switzerland.
Alpiq and ECO STOR had previously entered into a long-term tolling agreement for the
Schuby battery
in northern Germany.
Earlier this year, Alpiq
acquired a 90% stake
in pan-European battery storage developer and operator Harmony Energy, gaining access to a multi-gigawatt pipeline across the UK, France, Germany and Poland.

title: CenterNode invests in US solar, storage EPC firm Aquila Energy
content:
CenterNode, an alternative energy investment platform with more than USD 800 million (EUR 685.4 m) in institutional capital commitments, has made a strategic investment in US renewable energy engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) firm Aquila Energy LLC.
Financial terms of the transaction were not disclosed.
The investment will strengthen Aquila’s financial position and bonding capacity, whilst supporting its growth in distributed generation and small utility-scale solar and battery energy storage markets.
Aquila is focused on projects that require institutional-quality execution but are increasingly underserved by larger EPC firms, it said.
“There is a growing need for an EPC partner that can bring institutional-quality execution, financial strength and accountability to distributed generation and small utility-scale projects. With CenterNode as our partner, we can invest in our people, technology and operating capabilities while staying agile and close to our customers,” said Brian Barker, founder and CEO of Aquila Energy.
CenterNode is Forest Road's alternative energy investment platform. It provides capital to projects, developers and operating companies in the power and infrastructure sectors.

title: EIFO provides loan for Vestas-powered wind farm in Ukraine
content:
The Export and Investment Fund of Denmark (EIFO) said today it is providing a EUR-100-million (USD 116.6m) loan to Ukrainian agro-industrial company Kernel to build a 94.5-MW wind farm in central Ukraine that will be equipped with Vestas turbines.
Vestas Wind Systems A/S (CPH:VWS) will supply and install the wind farm’s 21 wind turbines. The Danish manufacturer announced the deal as an undisclosed order in its second-quarter order intake.
The wind farm, which will also include battery storage, is expected to strengthen both Kernel’s own operations and Ukraine's energy transition and security. The Ukrainian company is a large exporter of sunflower oil, which is now expanding into renewable energy.
The financing for the Kernel project is provided through EIFO's Ukraine Facility and marks EIFO's second wind farm financing.
“When half of a country’s electricity production is gone, the priority is to bring new capacity online quickly,” said EIFO CEO Peder Lundquist.
“At the same time, the reconstruction of Ukraine represents a significant business opportunity, where Danish companies — such as Vestas — are helping lead the way. This benefits Danish industry and is crucial for Ukraine,” Lundquist added.
Vestas currently has 1,200 MW of capacity installed or under construction in Ukraine.

title: EU okays Blackstone’s EUR-2bn bet on Eurowind Energy
content:
The European Commission (EC) has given the go-ahead to US investment giant Blackstone’s (NYSE:BX) deal to invest up to EUR 2 billion (USD 2.33bn) in Danish renewables developer Eurowind Energy to get an initial minority stake in the business and back its growth.
The nod was granted unconditionally as the investment is not seen to harm competition, given the companies' limited market positions resulting from the proposed transaction, the EC said today.
The deal was
announced at the end of April
. Under its terms, Blackstone will acquire a 24.7% stake in Hobro-based Eurowind, joining energy and telecommunications group Norlys as a fellow shareholder.
Founded in 2006, Eurowind specialises in the development, construction and operation of renewable energy parks. Its portfolio includes wind, solar, hydrogen, biogas, power-to-heat solutions and battery storage projects. The company has more than 700 employees and operations in 16 markets across Europe and the US.
Upon completion, Norlys will hold a 37.65% ownership interest in Eurowind Energy. The rest of the business is owned by the company's directors and employees.

title: Field secures planning consent for 200-MW/3.6-GWh UK LDES project
content:
.UK battery storage developer Field has secured irrevocable planning consent for its 200-MW/3,600-MWh Rigifa long-duration electricity storage (LDES) project in northern Scotland.
The consent comes after the project recently received
a "minded-to" decision
from energy regulator Ofgem under its cap-and-floor mechanism for LDES, Field's head of development Bex Sherwood said in a LinkedIn post.
Rigifa is one of five Field projects included in Ofgem's June decision, allowing the developer to advance a total 1.6 GW/26.8 GWh of planned lithium-ion battery storage under the cap-and-floor scheme. The projects are designed to provide between 16 and 18 hours of storage, substantially longer than conventional grid-scale battery installations.
Field said in June that the five projects were in late-stage development and that construction was scheduled to start from late 2027.
Rigifa is planned alongside Field's New Deer, Netherton and Fyrish projects in northern Scotland and the Long Stratton project in East Anglia. The sites are located close to renewable generation and network constraints to help absorb surplus wind and solar power and release electricity when demand is higher.
Field said Rigifa's planning consent was an important milestone as it moves the project towards being ready to build. The company currently has four other sites under construction in the UK and six operational sites across the UK and Germany, Sherwood said.
Under Ofgem's cap-and-floor mechanism, supported projects receive a revenue top-up if their market revenues fall below a set floor, while revenues above a specified cap are returned to consumers.

title: Final electrolyser array arrives at 100-MW German green H2 project
content:
Siemens Energy AG (ETR:ENR) announced the delivery of the final electrolyser array for the 100-MW Hamburg Green Hydrogen Hub (HGHH) project on the site of the former Moorburg coal-fired power plant in Hamburg, Germany.
“This milestone reflects the dedication and expertise of hundreds of colleagues across engineering, manufacturing, supply chain, project management, and service,” the German technology supplier said in a brief statement.
HGHH
entered the construction phase
in December 2025. The project is majority owned by Luxcara, with a 74.9% shareholding, while Hamburger Energiewerke is a minority partner with a 25.1% stake.
The site is expected to become operational in 2027. Its output will be delivered to customers via the
Hamburg Hydrogen Industry Network
(HH-WIN) as well as a planned trailer loading station.
Siemens Energy supplied the electrolyser technology under a
contract from September 2024
. At the time, the parties said that the order comprises six units of Siemens Energy’s latest proton exchange membrane (PEM) electrolyser model, with the stacks to be fabricated at the company’s Gigafactory in Berlin and assembled at its Muhlheim site and at a European partner.

title: Finland has over 26 GW of solar projects in pipeline, 4.6 GW permitted
content:
More than 26 GW of utility-scale solar power capacity is currently being planned in Finland, including 4.6 GW across 77 projects that have already secured municipal building permits, according to an
updated project portfolio
by Renewables Finland.
The country currently has 300 utility-scale solar projects at various stages of development, while some 15 projects, totalling 1.4 GW, have completed the zoning process.
The capacity of projects with building permits has increased by more than 1 GW in the six months since Renewables Finland's previous review, pointing to a rapid increase in the number of advanced, construction-ready projects, the industry association said.
Not all projects in the development pipeline will eventually be realised, but Finland has a substantial number of projects that are sufficiently advanced to be built on a relatively short timeline, Renewables Finland said.
Satakunta tops the chart as the region with the biggest pipeline, both in terms of number of initiatives and overall capacity -- 29 projects totalling 3.3 GW. It is followed by South Ostrobothnia with 2.7 GW and Northern Ostrobothnia with 2.6 GW.
The update comes as Finland's parliament considers a proposed Land Use Act that will introduce a zoning requirement for solar plants covering more than 50 hectares. Renewables Finland warned that the measure could add bureaucracy and delay projects, particularly those planned on remote wasteland and former peat production areas, which are precisely the types of areas to which solar power development is also intended to be directed.

title: ForeFront Power installs 7.7-MW solar canopy, BESS for Ventura County
content:
US commercial and industrial renewables developer ForeFront Power have finalised a 7.7-MW solar and battery storage project for California’s Ventura County at the county's Government Center, the parties said on Tuesday.
The project involved the installation of what ForeFront Power and Ventura County said is one of California's largest solar canopy-plus-storage installations. The set-up consists of a 5.8-MW solar canopy covering several car parks at the county's main government campus and a 1.9-MW battery energy storage system (BESS).
The solution is expected to generate nearly 9 GWh of electricity a year, enough to cover the annual electricity consumption of more than 1,500 homes. It will offset about 53% of the Government Center's energy use and reduce carbon dioxide emissions by about 5,000 tonnes a year, ForeFront Power and the county said.
ForeFront Power developed the project under a 20-year power purchase agreement (PPA) without the country bearing any upfront costs. The developer will own, operate and maintain the solar and battery system and sell electricity to the county at a fixed rate below the applicable utility rate.
The arrangement is expected to save Ventura County more than USD 21 million (EUR 18.0m) in energy costs over the life of the PPA, according to the statement.
The Government Center is one of Ventura County's largest energy-consuming sites. The county had already secured renewable electricity through community-choice energy procurement, but said on-site generation and storage would provide a more economical way to meet its sustainability objectives while improving energy cost predictability.
ForeFront Power, headquartered in San Francisco, said it has developed more than 1,900 behind-the-meter and community solar projects in the United States and Mexico, totalling more than 1.6 GWdc of solar capacity.

title: Galia secures EUR 87m for biomethane projects in Poland
content:
Polish biogas investor Galia Green Power has obtained PLN 376 million (USD102m/EUR 87m) from a consortium of banks for the development of biomethane projects.
The banks behind the agreement include PKO Bank Polski, development bank BGK and mBank. The financing will be used for the acquisition of biogas plants and investments in new projects or the expansion of existing facilities, Galia said on Tuesday.
The agreement, signed for 18 years, enables flexible inclusion of projects that meet specific technological and environmental criteria. The funding may be increased by PLN 225 million, allowing for additional investments.
The banks reaffirmed their commitment to projects supporting the country’s energy transition and highlighted the potential of biogas and biomethane projects in this regard.
Warsaw-based Galia Green Power was founded in 2024 with a focus on biomethane, biogas and bio-CO₂. It is supported by Eiffel Investment Group.

title: Goldwind posts 25% profit rise in H1
content:
Chinese wind turbine maker Goldwind Science & Technology Co Ltd (SHE:002202) on Wednesday reported net attributable profit of CNY 1.85 billion (USD 275m/EUR 236m) for the first half of 2026, marking an increase of 24.67% from the same period of 2025.
Revenue increased 18.25% to CNY 33.7 billion, with revenue from the sale of wind turbines and components rising 24.73% to CNY 27.26 million. During the six-month period, external sales of wind turbines totalled 12,364.38 MW, up 16.19% from a year ago.
The company exited the first half with 40,602.36 MW of external orders, as well as 10,356.72 MW of external unsigned orders that have been won in tenders, bringing its external order backlog to 50,959.08 MW. It also had 3,183.15 MW of internal orders.
Goldwind, which according to the Global Wind Energy Council (GWEC) was the
leading wind turbine supplier
in 2025 with 29.7 GW installed, said it is deepening its Offshore and Overseas Strategy. In the first half, revenue from international business grew 29.98% year-over-year to CNY 10.89 billion and overseas orders rose 28.93% to 9,489.02 MW.
The company’s newly installed offshore wind power capacity in China was up 48%.
Looking ahead, Goldwind said it will focus on high-quality development and advancing from scale-driven growth to value-driven growth, from energy equipment manufacturing to clean energy services and green energy applications, and from international business expansion to global operations.

title: Gore Street Capital's GS EU fund buys 195 MW of Irish BESS projects
content:
UK private equity investment manager Gore Street Capital has acquired two ready-to-build battery energy storage system (BESS) projects totalling 195 MW/390 MWh in Ireland for its GS EU Fund SCSp.
The fund acquired the 120-MW/240-MWh Kilmannock project and the 75-MW/150-MWh Mucklagh project, taking full ownership of both sites. Both projects have secured grid connections, land rights and planning permissions, Gore Street Capital said on Monday.
Kilmannock was acquired in full from Gore Street Energy Storage Fund plc (LON:GSF), while Mucklagh was acquired from the same fund, which previously held a 51% stake alongside a joint venture partner. Both GSF and GS EU funds are managed by Gore Street Investment Management, a wholly owned subsidiary of Gore Street Capital.
Gore Street said the transactions were conducted on an arm's length basis, with strict information barriers and independent third-party verification of valuations.
Financial details were not disclosed “due to commercial sensitivity”, the GSF fund said separately. The GSF will use the proceeds to finance shareholder distributions
under a capital recycling strategy
announced earlier this year.
The projects have an initial two-hour duration and could be expanded to four hours over their operating lives. Kilmannock is expected to start commercial operations in the first quarter of 2028, followed by Mucklagh in the second quarter.
The acquisitions represent the first investments by GS EU Fund, Gore Street Capital's third managed vehicle, following
its first close
at the end of 2025. The fund is backed by the National Treasury Management Agency, which manages Ireland's Strategic Investment Fund (ISIF).
Gore Street said Ireland's growing renewable generation, increasing power demand from data centres and supportive policies for longer-duration battery storage made the country an attractive market for the fund.
GS EU is targeting a subsequent fund close in the fourth quarter of 2026 and a final close in the first quarter of 2027.

title: Hydrogen mobility firm US Hybrid partners with California H2 authority
content:
California-based hydrogen and electric propulsion company US Hybrid Corp will establish its headquarters and manufacturing operations in Lancaster, California, under a partnership with First Public Hydrogen Authority (FPH2) that will supply hydrogen for its vehicles, the organisations said on Tuesday.
US Hybrid plans to manufacture hydrogen-powered buses and trucks at the facility and convert existing vehicles to fuel-cell propulsion. The company said operations are expected to begin in 2027 and the project will create about 1,200 manufacturing and engineering jobs.
US Hybrid develops fuel-cell systems, power electronics and vehicle integration technology and plans to use the Lancaster facility to supply zero-emission vehicles and repowered fleets across California.
FPH2, a California joint powers authority founded by the cities of Lancaster and Industry, will secure hydrogen supply for US Hybrid under what the authority described as one of its first commercial off-take partnerships.
The joint goal is to have a marketplace where fleet operators can access both hydrogen-powered vehicles and the fuel to run them.
"We are building more than vehicles," said Jason Lucas, president of US Hybrid. "We are building the ecosystem, from the hydrogen to the fleets that run on it, and the workforce California will need to keep it running for decades. No company does that alone. Our partnership with FPH2 is what makes it possible, and Lancaster is where it comes together."
US Hybrid’s solutions are already deployed at the ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach, which have committed to transitioning cargo-handling equipment and drayage trucks to zero emissions over the next decade. The companies said vehicles manufactured in Lancaster and fuel from FPH2 could support those efforts by providing hydrogen-powered equipment for port operations.
The partners refrained from naming the “colour” of hydrogen they intend to source. Outside of Tuesday’s press release, FPH2 says it seeks to bring to the market clean hydrogen, while its recent solicitation was focused on procuring “low-carbon” hydrogen, including electrolytic obtained from green and renewable sources.

title: Iberdrola seeks permits to repower 30.4-MW wind farm in Spain
content:
Iberdrola SA (BME:IBE) has applied for permits to repower its 30.39-MW MW Monte Treito wind farm in Galicia, northwestern Spain, seeking approval to replace 40 turbines commissioned in 2001 with seven larger units, according to a notice published in the official gazette of Galicia on Tuesday.
The project affecting four municipalities in A Coruna province would have seven Vestas V136 turbines, each rated at 4.5 MW, with a 136-metre rotor diameter and an 82-metre hub height. The capacity of the renovated wind farm will be 31.5 MW, while the electricity evacuation capacity will remain at 30.39 MW.
The new Monte Treito would have an annual net output of 109,373 MWh, Galicia’s regional authorities said in the notice.
The Spanish utility plans to invest around EUR 34 million (USD 39.7m) in the repowering project, which besides the turbine dismantlement will also include removal of their transformers, foundations, a meteorological mast, underground electrical cabling and roads that will not be needed under the new configuration.
The project also includes environmental restoration of affected land and modifications to the existing Treito 66 kV substation to accommodate the new wind farm. The number of medium-voltage circuits from the turbines would be reduced from four to three, while the plant control and SCADA systems would be replaced.
The existing 66 kV overhead transmission line connecting the Monte Treito wind farm to the Tambre-Padron line would remain in use and is not part of the project, the notice said.
Iberdrola filed applications for consent, a construction permit and the environmental impact study for the projects. All of these documents are now being submitted to public consultation for 30 days from the day after publication of the notice in the official gazette of Galicia.

title: JinkoSolar names new CEO, posts reduced Q2 net loss
content:
Chinese clean energy technology company JinkoSolar Holding Co Ltd (NYSE:JKS) appointed Wei “Dimi” Du as chief executive officer on Wednesday, succeeding Xiande Li, who resigned from the role as part of a planned leadership transition, and reported a year-on-year reduction of its second-quarter net loss, helped by gains from investments and the disposal of a subsidiary.
The solar panel maker said in a statement that Xiande Li will continue serving as the chairman and chair of the compensation committee and the nominating and corporate governance committee of the board of directors. Jinko stressed that his resignation is not the result of any disagreement with the company.
"This transition is part of a carefully planned succession process. As we enter the next phase of development, this arrangement allows me to focus on our long-term strategy, board governance, and major strategic decisions, while our new CEO will lead management in overseeing day‑to‑day operations, strategic execution, and capital allocation at the group level,” Li explained.
The new CEO served as vice president of strategic investment at JinkoSolar from April 2026 until today, and before that, between December 2021 and March 2026, was the general manager of strategic investment and assistant to the chairman of the company. Du was also the assistant to the chairman of Jinko Power Technology Co Ltd from February 2021 to December 2021.
Q2 FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE
For the second quarter of 2026, JinkoSolar reported a net loss attributable to its ordinary shareholders of CNY 697.3 million (USD 103.8m/EUR 88.9m), which compares with an attributable net loss of CNY 463.5 million for the prior quarter and a loss of CNY 876.4 million from a year back. This improved bottom line takes into account the impact of a change in fair value of a long-term investment, as well as a pre-tax disposal gain of about CNY 236.6 million in connection with the sale of a stake in a subsidiary. Excluding those non-recurring items, adjusted net loss rose to CNY 910.8 million from CNY 549.3 million in the first quarter of 2026 and CNY 856.4 million in the second quarter of 2025.
On the other hand, total revenues were up 0.9% sequentially and down 31.3% year-over-year to CNY 12.36 billion, with quarterly solar module shipments amounting to 15,961 MW, up 16.7% from the prior quarter and down 34.4% from a year earlier.
Gross profit margin halved to 4.2% in Q2 from 8.3% in Q1 2026, but rose from 2.9% a year back. The company blamed the sequential decrease on a lower average selling price of solar modules.
“Looking ahead, we expect our annual integrated production capacity to reach approximately 100 GW by year-end 2026, including approximately 14 GW from overseas facilities. Considering demand dynamics in certain markets, we will place greater emphasis on balancing shipment volume, profitability, cash flow and order quality, and are adjusting our full year 2026 module shipment guidance to between 60 GW and 70 GW, with high-efficiency products accounting for over 60% of the total shipments. For the third quarter of 2026, we expect module shipments to be between 15 GW and 17 GW,” the new CEO commented.

title: Kuwait Fund grants sovereign loan for 11-MWp solar project in El Salvador
content:
The Kuwait Fund for Arab Economic Development has signed an agreement to provide El Salvador with a KWD-3-million (USD 9.72m/EUR 8.34m) loan to finance an 11-MWp solar photovoltaic plant, the fund said on Tuesday.
The formal signing comes just over two months after
El Salvador's parliament voted to approve
the government's plan to turn to the Kuwait Fund for the financing of the San Matias solar project in La Libertad department.
Total project costs, including contingencies, price adjustments, interest during implementation, taxes and fees, are estimated at about USD 13.95 million (EUR 11.98m), or KWD 4.3 million. The Kuwait Fund's loan will cover about 69% of the cost, with the Salvadoran government financing the remainder and any additional cost increases, the statement said.
The loan has a 25-year term, including a three-year grace period, and will be repaid through 44 semi-annual instalments. It carries annual interest of 2.5%, plus a 0.5% charge for administrative and implementation costs.
The San Matias solar farm will be built on about 108,000 square metres of leased land at Hacienda San Lorenzo in the San Matias municipality, northwest of the capital San Salvador. The project will involve the installation of ground-mounted solar panel arrays, inverter stations, a containerised step-up substation, ancillary infrastructure and a connection to the national grid operated by El Salvador's DELSUR. Once up and running, the plant will generate about 20 GWh to 25 GWh of electricity a year.
Construction is expected to take about two years, with completion targeted for the first half of 2028.
The Kuwait Fund, which provides loans to developing countries, said this loan was its first to El Salvador. It has also provided the country with a KWD 90,000 grant to finance engineering studies and preliminary designs for flood-control barriers and flow regulation in the Buenos Aires Basin.

title: Lightstar wins 27.3 MW in New Jersey's agrivoltaic pilot programme
content:
US community solar developer Lightstar Renewables has secured eight conditional awards totalling about 27.3 MW of planned dual-use solar capacity in New Jersey's inaugural agrivoltaic pilot programme, the company said on Tuesday.
The projects, being developed through Lightstar subsidiary NJ Solar 2000, are located across Monmouth, Salem, Warren and Cumberland counties. Lightstar was one of three developers selected in the first solicitation of the New Jersey Board of Public Utilities' (NJBPU) Dual-Use Solar Energy Pilot Program.
The NJBPU conditionally approved 16 projects across the state, representing 52.06 MW of solar capacity. The programme seeks to promote renewable power generation alongside continued agricultural or horticultural production on the same land.
The selected projects combine solar generation with farming activities including crops and livestock production, such as soybeans, hay, grains, vegetables, fruit and grazing animals.
The first solicitation attracted 33 preliminary proposals totalling about 140 MW, Lightstar said. Lessons from the pilot will be used to shape a permanent agrivoltaics programme, with potential deployment of up to 200 MW over the next three years.
Lightstar said its awards remain conditional and depend on completing regulatory filings, coordinating with the New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection and meeting programme requirements during a 36-month development period.

title: Long-awaited offshore wind tender for 2 GW opens in Victoria
content:
The Victorian government on Wednesday officially launched the state’s maiden offshore wind auction, a long-delayed competitive process aiming to award 2 GW of capacity.
The Request for Proposal (RFP) is open for projects located off the Gippsland coast, a zone
officially declared
suitable for offshore wind deployment. Once commissioned, the capacity is expected to diversify the electricity mix and stabilise power supply as the state’s ageing coal-fired generators retire, generating electricity for around 1.5 million homes annually.
Proposals will be accepted by August 2027, with contracts due to be awarded in 2028.
“This auction is a giant leap towards getting Australia’s first offshore wind projects built – attracting billions in investment, creating thousands of jobs and delivering the reliable power we need as coal retires”, said Victoria’s Minister for Energy and Resources Jaclyn Symes.
The offshore wind competition was
originally planned
to be held last September but
was delayed
at the request of developers amid uncertainty over government funding support and the lack of needed infrastructure.
Victoria is currently the only Australian state with legislated offshore wind targets. The state’s goal is to have 9 GW of installed offshore wind capacity by 2040, with interim goals for at least 2 GW by 2032 and 4 GW by 2035.
Earlier this year
, the state government dedicated AUD 124.5 million (USD 89.1m/EUR 76.3m) to advance the Victorian Renewable Energy Terminal at the Port of Hastings to enable companies to assemble turbines before their offshore installation, thus supporting the industry’s expansion.

title: Maine selects developers of 800-MW wind farm, transmission line
content:
Maine regulators have selected Clearway Energy Group LLC to build an 800-MW onshore wind farm and Avangrid Networks Inc to install transmission facilities for its interconnection, the state Public Utilities Commission (PUC) said on Tuesday.
The projects were awarded following a Request for Proposals (RfP) launched by the PUC under the Northern Maine Renewable Energy Development Programme. The two companies will now enter contract negotiations.
For the generation portion of the project, Clearway has received an award for both energy and the renewable energy credits (RECs) from the future wind farm, of which 600 MW will be set aside for Maine. A power purchase agreement (PPA) for the procurement is due to be finalised after final review and approval by the PUC.
The wind park’s construction in Aroostook County depends on the advancement of the related transmission project allocated to Avangrid Networks. Specifically, the company will install 1,200 MW of transmission lines to Haynesville to connect the wind complex to the grid under a multi-state initiative that will see the states of Maine, Massachusetts, Connecticut, Vermont and Rhode Island share the construction costs.
Plans for the transmission component need to be greenlit by the Federal Energy Regulatory Committee (FERC). The remaining 400 MW of available capacity not reserved for the wind farm will be offered via additional RfPs, the Commission said. According to its estimates, the transmission and generation projects are expected to bring some USD 2.4 billion (EUR 2.05bn) in economic output to Maine.
The RfP was initially issued back in 2021 but was not successful and no deals were closed as the
selected projects
were stalled amid rising costs following the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Metafuels, PSI open green methanol-to-SAF demo plant in Switzerland
content:
Zurich-based sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) producer Metafuels and the Paul Scherrer Institute (PSI) have inaugurated a demonstration plant that will use green hydrogen and CO2 to produce green methanol, which is then converted into sustainable aviation fuel (SAF).
Located at PSI's campus in Villigen, Switzerland, the “aerobrew” facility is designed to produce 50 litres (13 gal) of SAF per day and will test the technology under industrially relevant conditions as the partners prepare it for commercial deployment.
The process uses renewable electricity to produce green hydrogen from water. The hydrogen is combined with CO2 from sustainable sources to make green methanol, which is converted into synthetic kerosene using Metafuels' patented "aerobrew" technology.
PSI said the facility is the world's first to combine all the production steps for SAF from methanol under one roof.
Metafuels plans to bring the first commercial plant for the production of SAF using the “aerobrew” technology into operation starting in 2030.

title: Metlen reports milestones for 1.3 GWh of BESS projects in Europe
content:
Greek energy and industrial group Metlen Energy & Metals (ATH:MYTIL) said on Wednesday it had advanced battery energy storage system (BESS) projects totalling 532 MW and 1,323 MWh across the UK, Italy and Greece, spanning engineering, procurement and construction work and renewables development and operation.
In the UK, Metlen signed a balance-of-plant contract with battery storage developer and operator Pulse Clean Energy for the 129-MW/362-MWh Penn BESS project in the West Midlands.
Metlen said its scope includes grid connection works, and expects the site to be energised by the end of 2027.
The Penn project adds to Metlen's UK storage activities, with the company having delivered or working on about 30 battery storage units, including hybrid and co-located solar and storage projects, representing nearly 2 GWh of capacity.
In Italy, Metlen secured EUR 18 million (USD 21m) in long-term financing for a 25-MW/75-MWh BESS project in Apulia's Brindisi province. The battery facility became fully operational during 2026 and is backed by a seven-year physical tolling agreement with Dolomiti Energia Group.
Metlen described the financing structure as one of the first of its type in Italy's energy storage market. The company has been active in Italy since 2017 and has built a portfolio with about 3 GWh of energy storage capacity in the country.
In Greece, Metlen and Karatzis Group of Companies have developed
a 330-MW/790-MWh standalone BESS project
in the Thessaly region, which the company touted as the country's largest planned standalone battery
The battery’s output has been integrated into Greece's national electricity transmission system, a step towards full operation and participation in grid services, Metlen said.
Metlen also recently finalised the 48-MW/96-MWh Aenaos battery project in Polygyros, in Halkidiki, Central Macedonia. The project was developed under Greece's national recovery plan, Greece 2.0, with funding from the European Union's NextGenerationEU programme.

title: Next2Sun launches EUR-5m share issue to speed up vertical PV projects
content:
German vertical bifacial photovoltaics firm Next2Sun AG on Monday said it is launching a share issue to raise up to EUR 5 million (USD 5.8m) to finance its next phase of growth.
The company seeks to accelerate the implementation of its own solar projects and scale its business model. Next2Sun expects to deliver around 50 MW of projects in 2026, almost matching the total delivered over the previous 10 years. It expects project volume of more than 70 MW in 2027 and aims to reach annual volumes in the hundreds of megawatts in the medium term.
The company says it is well positioned to benefit from the structural changes in the PV market as its vertical solar systems generate most of their output in the morning and evening hours, enabling higher market revenues ​​compared to conventional, south-facing ground-mounted solar installations.
Under the share issue, new shares will be offered to existing shareholders until September 4 and to all interested investors until September 30.
Set up in 2015, Next2Sun has completed over 65 MWp of projects in Germany and abroad. This includes a
17.4-MW vertical PV park at Frankfurt Airport
.

title: Northern Sun breaks ground on 23 MW of NY solar projects
content:
US solar and storage contractor Northern Sun Energy said on Tuesday that it has kicked off construction of two community solar projects totalling 23 MWdc in upstate New York for developer Seaboard Solar.
The projects in Waterford and Boonville are supported by grants from the New York State Energy Research and Development Authority (NYSERDA) and will employ local workers during construction.
Northern Sun said the projects presented different engineering and logistical challenges. The Waterford development spans two parcels that can only be accessed by a bridge with a 20-tonne weight limit, requiring the company to adapt its equipment delivery plans.
At the Boonville project, updated snow-load requirements are among the highest in the United States. Northern Sun worked with racking supplier GameChange Energy to design a system capable of meeting the revised structural requirements while keeping construction on schedule.
The projects add to Northern Sun's portfolio of solar installations in upstate New York and extend its partnership with Seaboard Solar, which began in 2017.
Northern Sun provides engineering, procurement and construction services for utility-scale solar and battery storage projects and has more than 2 GW of collective industry experience, it said.

title: Siemens Energy to split off industrial energy solutions unit
content:
Siemens Energy AG (ETR:ENR) plans to separate into a standalone company its Transformation of Industry business, which supplies industrial energy technologies including steam turbines, compressors, electrolysers for hydrogen production, generators and motors, as well as maritime and subsea technologies, among others.
The German energy technology group is preparing the legal and operational separation of the unit and will subsequently explore a new ownership structure, with options ranging from bringing in external investors to a potential capital markets transaction. The plan is to eventually deconsolidate the business while keeping “a meaningful minority stake.”
The standalone business will initially operate under Siemens Energy's
future brand, Omterra
, once launched.
Transformation of Industry serves customers in sectors including oil and gas, chemicals, process industries, paper, cement and maritime. The business employs around 17,000 people and generated EUR 5.7 billion (USD 6.65bn) in revenue in fiscal 2025, with a profit margin of 11.3%. It has more than 85,000 installed units worldwide.
The carve-out would give the business greater entrepreneurial flexibility and growth opportunities, Siemens Energy said, noting that its markets and investment needs are different from those of the rest of the group.
The planned separation is also part of Siemens Energy's broader strategy to concentrate on its power generation and power transmission businesses, where it sees higher immediate returns.

title: Spain to require data centres use 80% renewables on hourly basis - report
content:
Spain will require data centres to cover at least 80% of their electricity consumption with new renewable generation on an hourly basis under draft rules aimed at regulating the sector's rapid expansion, news agency Europa Press reported.
The draft decree, approved for fast-tracked legislation by the cabinet on Tuesday, will apply to data centres with more than 1 MW of electrical capacity. The government plans to put the proposal out for public consultation.
Spain's artificial intelligence strategy estimates that computing capacity will reach 2.5 GW by 2030, requiring between 3.5 GW and 4 GW of electricity demand. But data centre projects seeking access to Spain's power grid have far exceeded that target, with more than 12 GW of grid access and connection rights granted since 2021, Europa Press reported.
Under the proposed rules, at least 80% of a data centre's electricity consumption would have to come from renewable generation until renewables account for more than 90% of Spain's electricity mix.
The renewable supply would have to be additional to existing generation. Each new MW of data centre consumption would have to be matched by 1 MW of new renewable generation installed within the 18 months before the facility begins operating.
The requirement could be met through on-site generation or power purchase agreements (PPAs), according to the report.
Compliance would be measured hourly, meaning at least 80% of electricity consumed in each operating hour would have to be matched by renewable electricity generated in that same hour.
Projects seeking grid access would have to demonstrate compliance with the requirements to obtain access and connection rights. Failure to comply would trigger increasing surcharges on grid charges and network tariffs and could ultimately result in the loss of grid access rights.
The proposed surcharges would be intended to compensate the electricity system for additional costs arising from non-compliance with the requirements for additional renewable generation and hourly matching, Europa Press reported.
Data centre projects already under development would have six months to comply with the new requirements, or three months if they are awaiting a grid-access tender. Projects that do not comply could surrender their access and connection rights without the associated guarantees being enforced.
The rules would also impose requirements on energy and water efficiency. Facilities would have to meet the highest levels of the European data centre energy and water efficiency labelling scheme, which is being developed by the European Commission and is expected to take effect within a year.
Once the European scheme enters into force, the draft decree would require data centres to meet its highest, Category A, rating for both energy and water efficiency.
Government sources told Europa Press the draft decree would not amount to a moratorium on data centre activity. Proposals for new projects would continue to be submitted, but they will have to meet the new standards, the agency reported.

title: TotalEnergies signs PPA to get power from Walney wind farm off UK
content:
TotalEnergies Gas & Power Ltd has signed a long-term power purchase agreement (PPA) to source power from the Walney offshore wind farm in the UK.
The deal is with Offshore Partners Walney (OPW), which owns a 24.8% stake in Walney I and II, a combined 367-MW offshore wind farm. Under the PPA, TotalEnergies will buy Renewable Energy Guarantees of Origin (REGO)-backed electricity from OPW's share of the Walney I and II output through to 2030.
Located in the Irish Sea and operated by Ørsted, the Walney wind park has been in operation since 2012.
TotalEnergies Gas & Power, a unit of France’s TotalEnergies SE (EPA:TTE), is a supplier of gas and electricity to businesses and the public sector in the UK. It said the Walney PPA will bolster its renewable electricity portfolio and help meet growing demand from customers for traceable renewable energy.
“This agreement reinforces TotalEnergies' commitment to expanding its renewable power portfolio in the UK and supporting customers seeking high-quality, traceable renewable electricity,” commented PPA Originator Daniel Gell.

title: Trina Solar supplies 3 MWp of solar, BESS to Corona Resort in Vietnam
content:
China's Trina Solar Co Ltd (SHA:688599) has supplied a 3-MWp solar photovoltaic array and a 10-MWh battery energy storage system (BESS) to entertainment complex Corona Resort on Vietnam's Phu Quoc island, the company said.
The project was developed by Nam Viet Green Energy JSC and is expected to connect to the grid and start commercial operations in mid-September, Trina Solar said.
The Chinese solar and storage technology company supplied its Vertex N 725W (NEG21C.20) n-type i-TOPCon modules for the solar installation, while the battery system uses Trina Storage Elementa 2 platform. The BESS is AC-coupled to the solar system.
The project initially had 5.5 MWp of solar modules installed, with the additional 3 MWp of Vertex N modules and 10 MWh of battery storage added later, Trina Solar said.
The integrated system is intended to increase the use of on-site solar generation, reduce peak electricity demand and improve energy cost management and power supply resilience for the resort's hospitality, entertainment and tourism operations in a prime destination such as Phu Quoc, according to Trina Solar.

title: US DOE selects Tandem PV for USD-7.7m ARPA-E SCALEUP Ready award
content:
US solar panel maker Tandem PV on Tuesday said it has been selected for a US Department of Energy programme that will provide about USD 7.7 million (EUR 6.6m) to accelerate commercial production of its perovskite-silicon tandem solar technology.
The company's project, called Tandems for American National Dominance in Energy Manufacturing (TANDEM), was selected under the Advanced Research Projects Agency-Energy's (ARPA-E) SCALEUP Ready programme, which supports the commercialisation of emerging energy technologies.
The funding will support the development of Tandem PV's high-efficiency tandem panels towards large-scale commercial production. The technology combines an ultra-thin perovskite layer with conventional silicon to generate more electricity from the same panel area, the company said.
Tandem PV said the programme would help it move towards high-volume manufacturing in the United States and strengthen domestic solar supply chains.
Earlier this year, the company
opened a commercial demonstration factory
in Fremont, California, with annual nameplate capacity of about 40 MW.
Tandem PV has raised USD 100 million in venture capital, debt and government funding from investors and public agencies including Eclipse, Constellation Energy, 8090 Industries, Trellis Climate,
the US Department of Energy
and the California Energy Commission.

title: Vimab unit signs battery park delivery contract in Kosovo

title: Breedr Drives Traceability in Global Beef Supply Chain
content:
Breedr Drives Traceability in Global Beef Supply Chain
Prioritise Us
on Google
Breedr is digitising the global beef supply chain in order to drive traceability and efficiency. Credit: Unsplash
Breedr has raised US$27m in Series B funding, with an aim of digitising the global beef supply chain, encouraging traceability and driving sustainability
The beef supply chain is a significant one, though it is not always thought about. It involves moving cattle from farms to processing plants, before it reaches consumers.
A major concern within beef supply chains is the reduction of emissions – beef production generates high greenhouse gas emissions, involves significant water consumption and land use changes. This translates to
high methane emissions
, ongoing deforestation and significant resource usage.
Breedr, the platform giving each cow a digital record, is aiming to change the game with its increased traceability efforts. Alongside the announcement of its US$27m in Series B funding, the platform is aiming to transform the global
beef supply chain
Key facts
Breedr currently has two million cattle on its books
Breedr has raised US$27m in Series B funding
The aim is to create a traceable pathway for 1.3 billion cattle
Breedr estimates a 20-30% reduction in methane per animal
Funding scope
Breedr was founded in 2018, with the aim of helping farmers produce commercially and environmentally sustainable meat, thus prolonging the resilience of operations and reducing the negative environmental impact of the beef industry. Though it started small, it now has a network of thousands of farmers, working to drive forward-thinking solutions and ensure positive change.
It gives each cow a digital record, meaning it is traced from birth to the supermarket shelf. The platform operates across ten global supply chains and currently has two million cattle on its books. Almost US$500m of livestock has been transacted in the last year using the platform, and its customer base spans across family ranches and major organisations which handle more than 100,000 cattle a year. The aim of Breedr is to reach the entire beef
supply chain
, creating a traceable pathway for all 1.3 billion cattle.
Now, the platform has announced that it has raised US$27m in Series B funding. This has been led by Partech, a global technology investment organisation, through its impact fund. Partech Impact works to support organisations which are aiming to transform value chains across industry, agriculture, infrastructure, healthcare and more.
The funding round included support from Latitude, LocalGlobe and Outsiders Fund, which was a leader in the Series A funding round. Breedr now has a combined funding of US$46.6m, which will help grow the team and capabilities of the platform. With an aim of growing exponentially, the funding will help bring more ranchers and farmers to Breedr and means the company can invest in technological advancements to increase data point capturing – including genomic data.
Traceability and sustainability
are what make a beef business more productive and more profitable," Ian Wheal, Founder and CEO of Breedr, told Supply Chain Digital.
Ian Wheal, Founder and CEO of Breedr
"A supply chain that can trace an animal from birth knows exactly what its genetic history is, what it is worth and where the value is being lost. Sustainability works the same way, the most sustainable animal is usually the most efficient one, the one that puts on weight faster on less feed, and efficiency is simply another word for profit."
Increasing efficiency
Though demand for beef is constantly rising, the US cattle herd started 2026 at its lowest level since 1951, according to the United States Department of Agriculture. Moreover, this year's calf crop is expected to be the smallest on record. To make the most out of each animal and every aspect of the cattle crop, the industry needs thorough insights into the crop. Paper trails are no longer efficient for visibility, which is why Breedr increases capabilities within the sector.
The digital record uses weight, health and family history of each cow, with updates being added at each ranch the animal passes through in its lifespan.
Ian says, "We built Breedr to bring value back to the people who raise the cattle. Demand for beef is climbing while the herd is the smallest it has been in 75 years. The industry has to get more value from every animal, and you cannot do that on paper.
"If you have bought beef from a major retailer in the United States or UK, there is a good chance it has moved through a Breedr-powered supply chain. We already do the same in Australia and New Zealand, and this round enables us to expand connected supply chains globally - where every animal tells its own story and every producer gets paid for the quality they raise."
Breedr includes a dedicated marketplace where producers can trade on – instead of relying on what judges can see at an auction, they can judge using detailed data points. The app offers a thorough digital record and lower fees. It helps inform the optimum point of sale through a growth prediction model which uses AI.
The most sustainable animal is usually the most efficient one, the one that puts on weight faster on less feed, and efficiency is simply another word for profit.
Ian Wheal, Founder and CEO of Breedr
The Breedr platform offers thorough insights into each animal. Credit: Breedr
Ian explains to Supply Chain Digital: "Farmers record data now, but it's all in paper notebooks or in spreadsheets. Breedr replaces paper and best guesses with animal intelligence. A producer can see the performance of every animal, a buyer can understand exactly what they are purchasing, and nobody is doing double data entry. The result is less wasted effort and better outcomes, which means a more productive business at one end and a more profitable one at the other."
Sustainability and traceability
"Beef is one of the most complex decarbonisation problems there is. Breedr cuts emissions while helping producers become more profitable," explains Arnaud Minvielle, General Partner at Partech, who has joined Breedr's board.
Arnaud Minvielle, General Partner at Partech
"Ian and the Breedr team are building the transaction layer for one of the world’s largest unmodernised markets, earning revenue every time an animal changes hands. That alignment between the commercial engine and the environmental outcome is exactly what our impact fund exists to back. We truly believe that Ian, being an insider from this industry, and his team can fundamentally transform this value chain with data intelligence.”
Due to the streamlined transactions and monitoring, producers can earn more than US$500 per animal. This is due to the
keen insights and the traceability
of each animal, offering confidence for the buyer. Alongside this, Breeder has a cattle fund which allows producers to unlock money from animals they are still raising, meaning they can start generating income sooner.
Breedr, operating across the UK, US and Australia, offers a closed-loop system for managing livestock and cattle fund, as well as a data-verified marketplace. Through this, it drives security within the
beef supply chain
, alongside thorough insights and an increased sustainability opportunity.

title: Sedex Launches Regulatory Navigator for Supply Chains
content:
Sedex Launches Regulatory Navigator for Supply Chains
Prioritise Us
on Google
Sedex's new tool gives teams a steer on which supply chain due diligence and sustainability regulations apply to them (Image source: Sedex)
As CSDDD and CSRD thresholds shift and forced labour rules tighten, Sedex has launched a tool to help teams track what applies
Supply chain regulation has not stood still so far this year. The EU finalised sweeping changes to two flagship sustainability laws, forced labour import bans spread across three continents and several countries have come under diplomatic pressure to tighten their own rules, all within a few months.
Against that backdrop, Sedex, a global supply chain sustainability solutions provider, has launched the Regulatory Navigator, a free self-serve tool giving businesses an indicative view of which major supply chain due diligence and sustainability regulations apply to them.
The tool launched on 25 August, arriving as compliance, procurement and sustainability teams face a growing
volume of overlapping legislation
, from the EU Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive (CSDDD) to forced labour product bans.
A regulatory landscape in flux
The scope of Europe's two flagship sustainability laws changed significantly this year. In February 2026, the amended CSDDD was published, raising its threshold from 1,000 to more than 5,000 employees and from €450m to more than €1.5bn in global net turnover, cutting the number of in-scope companies by around 70%.
Mandatory climate transition plans
were dropped and compliance was pushed back to July 2029.
The Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD) also had a similar rebalancing, seeing it now apply only to companies with more than 1,000 employees and €450m or more in net turnover, in turn cutting the number of in-scope companies by almost 85%.
Businesses don't need complexity: they need clarity. The Regulatory Navigator helps teams move from uncertainty to informed action faster and
develop a centralised compliance roadmap
that avoids duplicating the common tasks required, such as mapping supply chain risks across multiple tiers.
Jon Hancock, Chief Executive Officer at Sedex
Forced labour enforcement has moved in the opposite direction, tightening rather than narrowing. The European Commission must establish a forced labour risk database by 14 June 2026 ahead of its Forced Labour Regulation taking effect in December 2027.
Canada introduced draft legislation in June 2026 to strengthen its import ban with new supply chain tracing requirements. In the US, the Trade Representative imposed tariffs of 10% to 12.5% on 60 trading partners in July 2026 over their failure to enforce forced labour import bans, prompting Indonesia, Pakistan and El Salvador to introduce their own.
For teams tracking obligations across multiple markets, that combination of
narrowing EU thresholds
and tightening forced labour rules elsewhere makes it harder, not easier, to know which requirements genuinely apply.
Sedex's tool: How it works
Users are required to answer a short set of questions covering their business's headquarters, approximate annual revenue, global workforce, the markets they operate in and whether they import goods into the EU or the US.
The tool then flags which of eight major regulations are likely to apply, each with a plain-language explanation, key thresholds and a summary of compliance requirements, as well as key deadlines.
Sedex's Regulatory Navigator works as an accessible starting point for understanding potential obligations before formal legal scoping begins (Image source: Sedex)
Regulations covered include:
the EU Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive (CSDDD)
the EU Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD)
the EU Forced Labour Regulation
Canada's Fighting Against Forced Labour and Child Labour in Supply Chains Act (S-211)
Australia's Modern Slavery Act.
Its regulatory content reflects the EU Omnibus Simplification Package I, keeping CSDDD and CSRD thresholds current.
Jon Hancock, Chief Executive Officer at Sedex, says the tool responds to a wider need for clarity rather than added complexity. “Businesses don't need complexity: they need clarity,” he says.
“The Regulatory Navigator helps teams move from uncertainty to informed action faster and develop a centralised compliance roadmap that avoids duplicating the common tasks required, such as mapping supply chain risks across multiple tiers."
Maurizio Capuzzo, Chief Marketing Officer at Sedex, echoes this and frames the launch as a response to one of the most common challenges raised by the company's customers, where multiplying rules and shifting thresholds make it difficult for teams to know where to start.
Jon Hancock, Sedex CEO
Why this matters for supply chain leaders
The Regulatory Navigator gives compliance,
procurement
, sustainability and supply chain teams an accessible starting point for understanding potential obligations before formal legal scoping begins.
That starting point matters most for multinational organisations juggling overlapping requirements across the EU, UK, Canada, Australia and the US, where a single sourcing decision can now trigger several regulatory regimes at once, some narrowing in scope and others tightening enforcement in the same year.
It is important to note that Sedex is clear that results are indicative only, and are not a substitute for legal advice.
Key partner cited: Sedex
Sedex is a global supply chain
sustainability solutions provider
, headquartered in London with an additional base in Chicago. Jon Hancock serves as Chief Executive Officer, with Maurizio Capuzzo as Chief Marketing Officer. Sedex provides tools and data supporting responsible sourcing, ethical trade and supply chain due diligence for businesses managing multi-tier supplier networks.

title: Asahi Kasei opens new facility for wet-process battery separators - electrive.com
content:
Japanese chemical company Asahi Kasei has opened a new coating line for Hipore wet-process battery separators in Charlotte, North Carolina, USA. The facility marks the first step in establishing a regional supply structure for wet-process plants.
Hipore separators by Asahi Kasei
Image: Asahi Kasei
The new facility has been constructed on the existing Celgard plant premises and is scheduled to begin commercial production in the second half of fiscal 2026. This investment coincides with the 40th anniversary of the Celgard site, where dry-process separators have primarily been manufactured to date.
Through this new facility and a concurrently developed
separator factory in Canada
, Asahi Kasei aims to significantly expand its local supply chain in North America. This expansion will enable the company to respond flexibly and directly to rising demand for components used in battery-electric vehicles and stationary energy storage systems (ESS) in the region.
“Opening the Charlotte coating line is a key milestone in establishing our North American supply platform for battery separators,” said Ryu Taniguchi, President of Asahi Kasei Battery Separator Corporation. “By leveraging Celgard’s experienced workforce and established operations, we are expanding our North American product portfolio to include both Celgard dry-process and Hipore wet-process technologies. Together with our planned separator facility in Canada, this investment will bring production capabilities closer to the region’s battery market and position Asahi Kasei to swiftly respond as demand grows across electric vehicles and energy storage systems.”
A battery separator is an extremely thin, microporous plastic membrane placed inside a lithium-ion battery cell as an essential insulating layer between the positive electrode (cathode) and the negative electrode (anode). Its primary function is to prevent physical short circuits – thus avoiding uncontrolled heating or destruction of the cell – while simultaneously allowing lithium ions to flow through its tiny pores. This ion flow, facilitated by the liquid electrolyte, is critical for power generation.

title: SK Innovation reacquires separator subsidiary SKIET - electrive.com
content:
SK Innovation and its subsidiary SK IE Technology (SKIET), which handles the separator business, will merge. Through the merger, set to take effect on 1 January 2027, SK Innovation plans to reorganise SKIET’s separator business within the parent company.
SKIET is a highly specialised company that produces lithium-ion battery separators (LiBS), a critical component of battery cells. Originally a wholly owned subsidiary of South Korean conglomerate SK Innovation, the company was spun off in 2019 and listed on the stock exchange in 2021. However, SKIET has faced significant challenges amid slower electric vehicle market growth, delayed demand recovery in key markets such as North America and intense price competition from Chinese manufacturers.
SK Innovation says bringing SKIET back under its corporate umbrella and ending its independent listed status will strengthen financial stability, mitigate business and financial risks and improve operational efficiency. The merger is also intended to strengthen the separator business over the medium to long term and increase shareholder value. SKIET currently supplies separators to SK Innovation subsidiary SK On as well as
external customers such as LG
The merger is expected to be approved on 24 November by the SK Innovation board of directors and the SKIET general meeting, with the relevant procedural steps to be completed by the merger’s effective date of 1 January 2027. The new shares of SK Innovation issued as part of the merger will be listed on the stock exchange on 18 January 2027.
Following the merger, the company expects to improve operational efficiency within the separator business and reduce costs associated with duplicated structures. Additionally, by combining SK Innovation’s R&D capabilities with SKIET’s product development expertise, the competitiveness of the separator business is expected to strengthen – particularly through the planned expansion into separators for energy storage systems (ESS).
A representative of SK Innovation stated: “Through this merger, we plan to strengthen our financial stability and streamline our business structure, thereby enhancing the mid- to long-term competitiveness of the separator business.” The representative added: “We will do our utmost to ensure that this merger leads to a recovery in business competitiveness and an enhancement of shareholder value.”

title: $1B US fusion facility targets 100-megajoule output in race with China
content: American startup Pacific Fusion has begun construction on a $1 billion manufacturing and research site in Albuquerque, New Mexico. Engineers at the site plan to test a new type of pulsed-power machine by 2030, targeting two long-standing technical benchmarks in nuclear physics.“America pioneered the breakthroughs that brought fusion within reach. Pacific Fusion is focused on converting that scientific leadership into industrial capability and infrastructure that strengthens US energy leadership and national security,” said Dr. Keith LeChien, co-founder and Chief Technology Officer.The primary goal of the facility is to demonstrate net facility energy gain. In past laser and magnetic fusion experiments, researchers measured gain only by comparing the energy that hit the fuel capsule against the resulting fusion output.Using pulsed-power inertial confinementPacific Fusion is measuring efficiency across the entire plant. Net facility gain means the fusion reaction must produce more energy than the total electrical energy stored inside the machine before firing. No laboratory has achieved this level of overall electrical efficiency.The system relies on pulsed-power inertial confinement. Instead of using massive laser arrays or magnetic coils like tokamaks, the machine discharges intense bursts of electrical current directly into a target. This high-current pulse creates extreme magnetic pressure, which rapidly compresses a small fuel capsule to initiate fusion. To keep costs manageable, the company builds its power systems out of modular, standard electrical parts made from widely available industrial materials.Decades of researchThe foundation for this technology comes from decades of research at Sandia, Los Alamos, and Lawrence Livermore national laboratories. Pacific Fusion recently completed a test series on a prototype driver called Sirius, built under a joint agreement at Lawrence Livermore. Sirius uses an impedance-matched Marx generator to deliver short, high-voltage pulses into a load. During the test campaign, the prototype completed more than 3,000 continuous shots. Engineers used the resulting data on voltage stability, switch wear, and circuit timing to design the full-scale pulser module that will power the Albuquerque plant.The Albuquerque demonstration machine is also designed to produce high-yield fusion reactions exceeding 100 megajoules per pulse. Outputs at this scale generate extreme temperatures and pressures known as high-energy-density states. These conditions allow physicists to study the behavior of materials and radiation under conditions found inside nuclear weapons. The US government identified a need for this kind of experimental platform thirty years ago, when underground nuclear explosive testing was halted.Because of these capabilities, the Department of Energy’s National Nuclear Security Administration has signed a formal agreement to collaborate with the company. The partnership focuses on high-energy-density physics, computer modeling, advanced materials, and pulsed electrical networks.Hardware assembly plantAlongside the main Albuquerque campus, the company is opening a hardware assembly plant in Los Lunas. That facility will mass-produce the modular pulsed-power stages needed to assemble the full demonstration system. Local utility Public Service Company of New Mexico has also begun studying how future pulsed-power plants could feed baseload power into the regional grid as electrical demand rises.“Today’s groundbreaking shows that America can still build the hard things, and build them faster than any other country, including China,” concluded LeChien.

title: 120-tonne electric trucks test 624kWh batteries 1,250m underground
content: Two 120-tonne battery-electric trucks are now hauling iron ore deep inside Sweden’s Malmberget mine, showing how electric heavy transport is moving beyond surface operations and into demanding underground production.The Scania-based semi-trailer trucks can carry just over 70 tonnes each and use 624 kWh battery packs. They are operating at depths of up to 1,250 meters below ground as part of LKAB’s effort to reduce emissions from its mining operations.During commissioning, the trucks have already moved more than 100,000 tonnes of iron ore across about 1,500 round trips. LKAB says the vehicles have demonstrated around seven hours of operation per charge, covering roughly 45 trips and moving about 3,200 tonnes of material.The trucks can charge at up to 375 kW, with a full charge taking around 80 minutes. They move ore between underground chutes and crushers at a mine that handles more than 50,000 tonnes of iron ore each day.Heavy electric haulage goes deeperLKAB says the trucks are, to its knowledge, the world’s largest and heaviest battery-electric underground mining trucks. The company qualifies the claim because larger battery-electric haul trucks are already being developed and tested for surface mining.Putting battery-electric equipment more than a mile underground creates challenges that do not exist to the same degree in surface mining. Charging infrastructure has to be integrated into the mine, while vehicle availability and turnaround times must be maintained without disrupting production.The trucks’ seven-hour operating window and 80-minute full-charge time give LKAB data on how electric haulage can fit into those production cycles.The project also provides a test of whether large battery-powered vehicles can maintain the productivity required for continuous mining operations rather than simply demonstrate that they can move heavy loads. LKAB is now preparing another electric truck for a more demanding test.Electric truck targets round-the-clockA separate Scania 8×4 heavy tipper, called Sleipner, is being prepared for continuous 24/7 production. The vehicle weighs about 60 tonnes when fully loaded, carries a 38-tonne payload and has a 416 kWh battery.LKAB is evaluating whether Sleipner can replace a diesel truck performing the same production task. Unlike the 120-tonne underground semi-trailers, the 8×4 is intended to test whether a battery-electric truck can maintain diesel-like availability during around-the-clock operation.The two programs therefore address different parts of mine electrification. The larger trucks are demonstrating heavy battery-electric haulage deep underground, while Sleipner is being tested against the availability demands of continuous production.LKAB and Scania have been working on mining electrification for several years. An earlier Scania electric heavy tipper entered surface operation at Malmberget in 2022 and accumulated around 31,000 miles during its initial test phase.LKAB aims to electrify 30% of its mining fleet by 2027. It also wants to haul and load at least five million tonnes of material annually without tailpipe emissions.“We may have built the world’s heaviest battery-electric underground truck — but we’re just getting started, with bigger, better and smarter things already in the making,” said Pär Sundqvist.The next challenge is therefore not simply proving that a 120-tonne electric truck can work underground. title: A high-flux reactor could help US commercialize new nuclear fuels
content: The United States could use Oak Ridge National Laboratory’s (ORNL) High Flux Isotope Reactor (HFIR) to accelerate the development and qualification of fuels needed for new and existing nuclear power plants.HFIR is one of the few American research reactors capable of exposing experimental fuels and materials to the intense neutron conditions required for advanced testing.Its experiments can produce performance and safety data for developers, utilities, and technical reports supporting regulatory qualification by the US Nuclear Regulatory Commission.Three regions support different experimentsHFIR is one of the world’s highest-flux steady-state research reactors. Its intense neutron flux allows scientists to study materials across different neutron energies and reproduce some of the conditions fuels experience inside commercial reactors.The facility contains three primary irradiation regions. Small and relatively simple “rabbit” capsules can be rapidly designed, assembled, and placed in the reactor’s central flux trap, where samples receive the highest neutron exposure.HFIR’s removable and permanent beryllium reflector regions can accommodate larger and more complex experiments.These can include sensors, instrumentation, and thermal neutron shields used to modify the neutron spectrum reaching a sample.Oak Ridge researchers have used the reactor for separate-effects tests, which examine individual fuel behaviors, and integral tests that evaluate several interacting processes. Previous work at HFIR helped establish the architecture of the tri-structural isotropic (TRISO) particle fuel developed for high-temperature gas reactors.Modern systems improve testing accuracyModernization has expanded HFIR’s ability to conduct instrumented experiments with greater control. ORNL’s Materials Irradiation Facility regulates test temperatures through controlled mixtures of sweep gases and can independently manage several temperature zones within one experiment.Automated systems continuously measure temperature, pressure, and gas composition. Researchers can also monitor experiments remotely and adjust their operating conditions while irradiation is underway.These capabilities have been used to detect fission gas released from TRISO fuels during irradiation. They also allow HFIR to support several sophisticated experiments simultaneously, increasing the amount of information that can be collected during a testing campaign.The reactor’s flux trap can additionally accommodate extensive fuel-cladding irradiations, helping scientists examine how fuels and their surrounding materials behave under neutron exposure.Data could support fuel qualificationResults generated at HFIR can contribute to technical reports used by the NRC when evaluating new nuclear fuels. The reactor can provide data on fission gas release, changes in fuel microstructure, and interactions between a fuel and its cladding.HFIR is also located near several ORNL facilities used to manufacture, examine, and analyze nuclear materials. These include the Coated Particle Fuel Development Laboratory, Low Activation Materials Development and Analysis laboratory, Irradiated Fuel Examination Laboratory, and Irradiated Material Examination and Testing Facility.Together, the reactor and supporting laboratories provide a pathway for moving fuels from early experiments toward regulatory qualification. A paper published in Nuclear Engineering and Design outlines how the Department of Energy research reactor in Tennessee can help address a growing fuel-testing backlog.The paper argues that more strategic use of HFIR could help meet rising testing demand as utilities pursue longer plant lifetimes and developers prepare advanced reactors for commercial deployment.

title: Alternative C-band signals beat intense GPS jamming on standard gear
content: TrustPoint has shown that its C-band navigation signals can keep working through satellite navigation interference on an established commercial receiver platform.The test, conducted under a U.S. Navy research contract, paired TrustPoint’s signals with an enhanced receiver from NovAtel, a Hexagon business. The result could help speed the development of navigation systems designed to operate when GPS becomes unreliable.GPS remains central to military operations, aviation and autonomous systems. Yet electronic warfare can jam or degrade those signals, leaving vehicles and equipment without reliable positioning data.TrustPoint is developing an alternative approach using signals in the C-band spectrum. Its latest demonstration tested whether those signals could work on receiver technology already familiar to commercial and defense users.Testing navigation under interferenceDuring the demonstration, the receiver acquired and tracked TrustPoint’s C-band signals despite GNSS interference. It also used those signals to produce precise positioning information.The work took place under a Phase II Small Business Innovation Research contract. The Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division led the effort for Naval Air Systems Command.That matters because resilient navigation systems often require specialized hardware. TrustPoint and NovAtel instead tested C-band capability on an established receiver platform.Patrick Shannon, TrustPoint’s founder and CEO, called the result an important benchmark for resilient positioning. “For the first time, C-band signals have operated through interference on a receiver the industry already trusts,” Shannon said.The test does not replace GPS. Instead, it points toward receivers that could use another source of positioning when conventional satellite navigation faces disruption. That capability could prove valuable for military aircraft, autonomous platforms and other systems operating in contested electromagnetic environments.Different navigation signalMost satellite navigation systems rely on L-band frequencies. TrustPoint’s approach uses C-band signals instead. C-band’s higher frequency gives engineers another option for delivering positioning and timing services. TrustPoint wants those signals to complement existing satellite navigation rather than force users to abandon GNSS equipment.NovAtel’s involvement could also shorten the route toward practical deployment. Its receivers already serve demanding aerospace, defense and industrial applications.Sandy Kennedy, vice president of research and development for Hexagon’s Aerospace & Defence division, said the work shows how established receiver technology can adapt to emerging navigation signals. The collaboration also pushes receiver development beyond traditional L-band services.For the Pentagon, the broader challenge is clear. GPS remains a critical capability, but adversaries increasingly field systems designed to interfere with satellite navigation. A resilient backup could give operators another source of positioning when GPS signals become degraded or unavailable.Testing navigation under interferenceThe interference test follows earlier C-band milestones from TrustPoint. In 2025, the company demonstrated live-sky transmission and real-time reception of its C-band GNSS signal with Hexagon. TrustPoint has also carried out a ground-to-space PNT demonstration.Three commercial free-flying satellites have already supported the company’s technology development. The new test brings that work closer to a practical receiver architecture.TrustPoint now faces the harder task of turning technical demonstrations into commercially available hardware and services. Still, proving that C-band signals can survive interference on a recognized receiver platform offers an important data point.For U.S. defense users, the appeal is straightforward. Navigation systems need options when GPS cannot deliver. TrustPoint’s latest demonstration suggests C-band could become one of them.
