title: Researchers Solve Two Major Problems Holding Back SiC Electronics
content:
Technology
The newly created SiC junction transistor and its electrical characteristics from room temperature to 600°C. Credit: Science Graphics
A new bottom gate design takes advantage of the intrinsic properties of SiC.
For more than 20 years, silicon carbide – SiC – has been viewed as a promising material for electronics that must function in extreme environments. Yet despite years of research, that promise has rarely translated into practical devices. Researchers at Kyoto University are now trying to move the field beyond that barrier.
“We believe the lack of development is because the research community has been trying to apply silicon-era thinking to a fundamentally different material,” says first author Mitsuaki Kaneko.
Conventional designs limited SiC performance
The researchers focused on junction field-effect transistors, or JFETs. Earlier work suggested that complementary circuits built from SiC JFETs could provide low-power integrated electronics capable of operating under extreme conditions.
But the group’s previous JFETs, which used conventional top-gate structures fabricated in semi-insulating SiC substrates, had two major shortcomings: poor controllability and substantial leakage current at high temperatures. Solving both problems was considered essential for practical applications.
“Our goal is to open a new path forward with complementary JFETs designed to harness the intrinsic properties of SiC itself,” says Kaneko.
Instead of creating an entirely new manufacturing process, the researchers used industry-standard fabrication methods. They adopted a bottom-gate structure to improve control over the transistor’s threshold voltage and replaced the semi-insulating substrate approach with well-based isolation to reduce leakage current at high temperatures.
The transistor operated at 600°C
The redesigned SiC transistor worked on the team’s first attempt. Testing showed that the device could continue operating at 600°C. The bottom-gate architecture substantially improved threshold voltage control and sharply lowered leakage current to a level close to the theoretical limit expected from the intrinsic properties of SiC.
The results show that SiC is already a mature power device material and highlight the potential of the new bottom-gate structure for building reliable SiC-based integrated circuits capable of operating at extreme temperatures.
Significant challenges remain before the technology can be used in practical systems. The researchers plan to develop more complex circuits, expand fabrication to wafer-level production, and ensure that complete device packages can withstand extreme environments.
Reference: “Over 600 °C operation of ion-implantation-based SiC bottom-gate JFETs” by Mitsuaki Kaneko, Shunya Shibata and Tsunenobu Kimoto, 17 August 2026,
APL Electronic Devices

title: Scientists Develop an Implant That Could Help the Body Clock Recover From Jet Lag Faster
content:
An experimental cell therapy that temporarily boosts leptin signaling helped rodents and nonhuman primates adjust more quickly to disrupted light-dark cycles. Credit: Shutterstock
A peer-reviewed study highlights how encapsulated leptin-producing cells can accelerate circadian realignment in preclinical models.
Jet lag and shift work can throw the body’s internal clock off course for days, disturbing sleep, altering metabolism, and contributing to other health effects. Researchers at Rice University, supported by the Rice Biotech Launch Pad, and Northwestern University have developed an implantable cell therapy that may help the body adjust more quickly when its normal schedule is disrupted.
In the study, researchers used encapsulated cells engineered to continuously release leptin, a hormone involved in metabolism. The treatment shortened the time animals needed to adjust to changes in the light-dark cycle designed to simulate jet lag and shift work. Published in
Advanced Science
, the results provide early evidence that metabolic signaling delivered through engineered cells could be used to influence circadian rhythms.
“Current approaches for adjusting circadian rhythms rely heavily on precisely timed behaviors such as light exposure, meal schedules or melatonin administration,” said Omid Veiseh, professor of bioengineering at Rice and faculty director of the Rice Biotech Launch Pad. “We wanted to explore whether a temporary cell therapy could provide a more practical way to help the body adapt to changing schedules.”
Engineered cells provide temporary leptin support
The treatment uses human retinal pigment epithelial cells modified to produce leptin, a hormone widely known for its role in appetite and metabolism. Researchers enclosed the cells inside microscopic spheres made from alginate, which shield them from the immune system while still allowing therapeutic proteins to enter the body. After a subcutaneous injection beneath the skin, the cells temporarily raise leptin levels in the bloodstream before gradually losing viability.
“Metabolism and circadian rhythms are closely connected, but the therapeutic potential of that relationship remains largely unexplored,” said Martha Hotz Vitaterna, professor of neurobiology at Northwestern University and co-corresponding author on the study. “These findings suggest that metabolic signals can be leveraged to accelerate adaptation to circadian disruptions.”
Animals adapted faster to shifted schedules
In experiments with mice, those given the leptin-producing cells adjusted significantly faster to both advances and delays in the light-dark cycle. When their schedule was delayed by four hours, treated mice adapted 50% faster than control animals.
The researchers then tested the approach in cynomolgus macaques to examine whether the results might translate to an animal with sleep-wake patterns more similar to those of humans. The treatment was well tolerated and shortened adjustment following six-hour schedule changes by about one day compared with controls.
Omid Veiseh and first author Samantha Fleury. Credit: Rice University
“The fact that we observed similar effects in both rodents and non-human primates suggests that the underlying biology may be conserved across species,” said Fred Turek, director of Northwestern’s Center for Sleep and Circadian Biology and a senior author on the study.
To determine how completely the animals had adjusted, researchers tracked several physiological measures associated with circadian alignment, including activity, heart rate, and core body temperature. Across these indicators, animals receiving the leptin-producing implants reached the new schedule faster than untreated controls.
The treatment also did not appear to interfere with sleep. Analysis in non-human primates found no decrease in total sleep time, rapid eye movement sleep, or non-REM sleep. After some schedule changes, researchers also recorded greater slow-wave sleep activity, which suggested that sleep quality during recovery may have improved.
The therapy was temporary and well tolerated
The researchers also examined the platform’s safety and practical characteristics. Blood testing and clinical monitoring found no evidence of significant toxicity in non-human primates, while animals given multiple doses over one year showed no long-term adverse effects. The encapsulated cells continued functioning for several days before naturally declining, making the treatment temporary and reversible.
“Our goal was not to permanently alter the circadian system,” Samantha Fleury, first author on the publication, said. “We wanted a therapy that could provide short-term support during periods of disruption and then naturally resolve.”
The researchers say the technology could eventually be investigated for situations involving repeated disruption of the body clock, including shift work, military operations, international travel, and other circumstances that require rapid adjustment to changing schedules.
“This work provides further evidence that metabolic pathways can be harnessed to influence circadian biology,” said Jonathan Rivnay, professor of biomedical engineering and materials science and engineering at Northwestern University and a senior author on the study. “More broadly, it demonstrates how engineered cell therapies can be used to deliver biologically active molecules in ways that would be difficult to achieve through conventional dosing.”
The researchers next plan to study how leptin influences circadian regulation and develop new versions of the platform that could provide adjustable or repeatable support for realigning the body clock.
Reference: “Encapsulated Leptin-Producing Cells Facilitate Entrainment of Circadian Rhythms in Rodents and Nonhuman Primates” by Samantha T. Fleury, Xuanyi Lin, Peter D. Rios, Christopher Olker, Eun Joo Song, Alejandra Cobos Perez, Cody Fell, Daisy Lopez, Ira Joshi, Hafsa Nasir, Cecelia Curtis, Danna Muringi, Kaiyuan Wang, José Oberholzer, Fred W. Turek, Isaac B. title: World’s Largest Trial of Robotic Knee Surgery Delivers a Surprising Result
content:
Robot-assisted knee replacement can place implants with greater precision, but the largest randomized trial of its kind found that accuracy alone did not improve pain, mobility, or recovery after one year. Credit: Shutterstock
Robot-assisted knee replacement surgery is more precise than surgery performed without robotic assistance, but it does not currently improve patient outcomes.
A robotic arm can help surgeons position a knee replacement more precisely, but that extra accuracy does not necessarily mean patients recover better. Results from RACER-Knee, the world’s largest clinical trial of its kind, found no improvement in patient outcomes during the first year after robot-assisted surgery compared with conventional knee replacement.
The trial, coordinated by the
University of Warwick
and University Hospitals Coventry and Warwickshire (UHCW) NHS Trust, was published in
The Lancet
. It adds important evidence about the expanding use of robotics in health care and where further development may be needed.
Robotic assistance is already used in about six percent of knee replacements in the UK, compared with 16 percent in the US and 42 percent in Australia. The technology is intended to help surgeons position implants more accurately and adjust the operation to fit each patient’s anatomy.
The UK-wide RACER-Knee trial was funded by the National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) in partnership with Stryker, which makes the robotic system tested. Led by the Warwick Clinical Trials Unit, UHCW NHS Trust, and the Royal Orthopaedic Hospital in Birmingham, it is the world’s largest double-blinded randomized controlled trial comparing conventional total knee replacement with surgery assisted by the Stryker Mako system, the most widely used robotic system of its kind worldwide.
Mako robotic system in use. Credit: UHCW NHS Trust
Greater precision did not improve recovery
One year after surgery, people in the robotic and conventional groups had similar levels of recovery, mobility, and pain. Although robotic assistance allowed more precise surgery, that advantage did not produce better patient outcomes during the first year. Serious adverse events were also no more common with robotic surgery, suggesting that the approach was as safe as conventional treatment.
The study was led by two Chief Investigators in the UK.
Professor Andrew Metcalfe, Warwick Medical School, University of Warwick, and Consultant orthopedic surgeon at UHCW NHS Trust: “We are delighted to have completed this world-leading randomized trial of an exciting technology that is now being used globally and at scale. It is an important step in the process of innovation and will stimulate lots more high-quality studies. We are very grateful for the support of the many patients who took part, which is so important, but also the NIHR and Stryker for working so well together to support this critical study. Technology such as this could really help the care we give for patients, but for robotic-assisted knee replacements, there is still work to do before we see benefits such as less pain or better movement.”
Mako system being prepped for surgery. Credit: UHCW NHS Trust
Professor Edward Davis, Consultant orthopedic surgeon at The Royal Orthopaedic Hospital NHS Foundation Trust and Honorary Professor at University of Birmingham: “The trial demonstrates robotic-arm-assistance allows for higher precision, and in theory the system should allow surgeons to customize the procedure according to a patient’s anatomy. These results are by no means a condemnation of the robotic systems, but more understanding of the ideal position for a knee replacement and personalization for each patient is needed. We’ll then be able to truly take advantage of the advanced precision of robotic systems.”
Professor Anthony Gordon, Director for the NIHR Health Technology Assessment (HTA) Program, said, “Innovation in healthcare depends on evaluating promising technologies rigorously and at scale. While this study shows robotic-assisted knee replacement is not yet improving patient outcomes, it highlights opportunities to refine these technologies and harness their precision to deliver better care in the future. The NIHR continues to fund robust studies, such as RACER, ensuring we learn how to deliver the latest technologies most effectively within the NHS.”
Robotics gives surgeons more control
Total knee replacement is among the most common elective operations performed worldwide to treat knee arthritis. In conventional surgery, doctors use their experience along with a standard set of instruments. With robotic assistance, the surgeon remains in control of a robotic arm that positions instruments with greater precision and provides more flexibility in choosing cutting angles and depths. This makes it possible to tailor aspects of the procedure more closely to an individual patient’s anatomy.
The trial included 339 patients treated by 33 surgeons at 10 hospitals across the UK. Despite the greater precision offered by robotics, there was no meaningful difference between groups after 12 months on the primary measure, the Forgotten Joint Score. This measures how much patients notice their artificial joint during everyday activities.
Results were also similar for walking ability, pain during the first three months and at 12 months, pain while in the hospital, and the likelihood of needing a follow-up operation.
Mako robotic system assisted surgery. Credit: UHCW NHS Trust
Long-term value remains unresolved
Researchers will continue monitoring the participants for ten years to determine whether meaningful differences eventually emerge between the two approaches. Longer follow-up may show whether one method affects the likelihood that patients will need additional knee surgery.
Robot-assisted total knee replacements also required more time and money. Procedures took an average of 10.5 minutes longer and cost about £950 more, although they were more precise and were not associated with a greater risk of serious adverse events. Under current NHS cost limits, the robotic system evaluated in the trial was not cost-effective during the first year after surgery.
Greater precision could eventually become more valuable if robotic systems allow surgeons to tailor knee replacements more effectively to each patient’s anatomy. Reaching that point will require further technological development and research to determine how the additional precision can be translated into outcomes that patients can actually feel.

title: Your Waist Size May Reveal More About Your Health Than You Think
content:
Waist circumference may offer a surprisingly simple way to detect unhealthy levels of body fat. In a study of U.S. adults, the measurement performed nearly as well as more complex obesity definitions that combine several body-size indicators. Credit: Shutterstock
A study found that the measurement performed nearly as well as an obesity definition based on multiple body measurements.
A tape measure around the waist may provide surprisingly useful information about obesity-related health risks.
Rutgers Health
researchers found that waist circumference can identify potentially unhealthy levels of body fat with accuracy comparable to more complicated approaches that require several body measurements.
The study, published in
JAMA Network Open
, found that waist circumference alone, or waist circumference combined with body mass index (BMI), performed as well as a recently proposed definition of obesity that incorporates multiple measurements.
The results suggest that measuring the waist could give clinicians and patients a practical way to identify excess body fat and related health risks without relying on a more complicated screening process.
“Pay attention to the need to loosen your belt or get bigger pants,” said Aayush Visaria, a faculty member of the Rutgers Health-RWJBarnabas Health Center for Climate, Health, and Healthcare and lead author of the study. “Although clothing size isn’t the same as a proper waist circumference measurement, it can be an early sign of unhealthy amounts of body fat. Measuring your waist, along with your weight, can help identify health risks earlier and provide an opportunity to reduce your risk of diabetes, heart disease, stroke, and some cancers.”
Simpler measures match complex screening
To compare different ways of identifying obesity, the Rutgers Health researchers analyzed data from 1,900 U.S. adults ages 20 to 59 who took part in the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey. They evaluated several obesity definitions against a highly accurate method for measuring body fat.
One of those approaches was a recently proposed framework developed by a multidisciplinary group of independent experts. It combines BMI, waist circumference, waist-to-height ratio, and waist-to-hip ratio. Although that framework identified more people with excess body fat, the researchers found that simpler methods produced similar accuracy.
Using either BMI or waist circumference provided a better balance between correctly detecting people with obesity and limiting false positive diagnoses. Waist circumference by itself performed nearly as well.
That simplicity could matter in routine medical care. Hip circumference, which is required for one of the measurements in the newly proposed framework, is rarely recorded in clinical practice. Waist circumference, by comparison, is relatively easy to measure in primary care and is receiving greater recognition in clinical guidelines.
“Our findings show that you don’t necessarily need multiple complex measurements to identify obesity-related health risks,” said Visaria, who also is an instructor in the Department of Medicine at Rutgers Robert Wood Johnson Medical School. “A waist measurement provides much of the information needed and is feasible for clinicians and patients alike.”
BMI alone misses some obesity cases
BMI by itself was less complete. The researchers found that it failed to identify a substantial number of people who met body-fat criteria for obesity, adding to concerns that BMI does not fully account for differences in body composition or where fat is stored.
The findings could help shape future recommendations for obesity screening and support more routine use of waist circumference in health care.
Reference: “Lancet Definition vs Other Criteria for Obesity Diagnosis in Adults” by Aayush Visaria, Douglas Corsi, Dylon Patel, Keerthana Kesavarapu, Ethan A. Halm, Jeffrey Carson and Soko Setoguchi, 7 August 2026,

title: Atlassian Rides the Knowledge Graph Boom
content: The rise of AI agents that automate coding projects and other white-collar tasks has prompted software firms such as Atlassian to offer so-called knowledge graphs or graph databases, which help the AI analyze the relationships between different types of data inside an organization. Software firms typically promote these new data management tools because they can help them make money from storing the information the AI requires to do its job. Firms like Microsoft have even put up some walls around their customers’ data so competing software firms won’t be able to access it, my colleague Kevin reported earlier this year. Graph databases, also referred to as knowledge graphs, differ from other data management platforms like those offered by Databricks and Snowflake, which mostly organize huge amounts of data into columns and rows. While both types of databases clean up troves of data so AI can analyze it and spot trends in customer spending during a given quarter, for example, proponents of graph databases say they require the AI to do less processing, which can save on costs. Databricks, meanwhile, says its data management products are better than standalone graph databases because they have more complete, real-time information, and the AI can communicate with its database more easily. Both Databricks and Snowflake have reported strong financial performance lately, and both store much more of a customer’s proprietary data than enterprise app firms like Atlassian or ServiceNow do. In any case, many companies think it’s worth having some options. Knowledge graphs are a collection of labeled “nodes” that connect to one another. For example, one node could be the name of a company employee. For instance, in a graph at The Information, my name Laura Bratton would be one node labeled as “person” and “employee,” and another node could be the firm that employs me, The Information, labeled “company.” A connection between those two points would indicate that I work at The Information. Previously, developers created the graphs by drawing connections between data points. But AI is now automating this process when it’s connected to a company’s business applications. Atlassian said in May that customers that use its graph database alongside tools such as Codex and Claude Code to develop a new app, for instance, used nearly 50% fewer tokens than if they didn’t tap the database. Atlassian first launched its graph database, Teamwork Graph, in 2023 but is now advertising it heavily to customers. In a shareholder letter this month, CEO Mike Cannon-Brookes called Teamwork Graph the “most underappreciated part of Atlassian” because of how it helps customers use AI more effectively. Atlassian doesn’t currently charge customers for Teamwork Graph but a spokesperson said that could change in the future, when customers may be billed in part based on how often their AI taps the database. ServiceNow in April launched its own version of a knowledge graph, which pulls customer data in real time from across its IT management and other applications. The company charges customers that use outside AI like Claude Code to tap the product. Amazon and Salesforce, which typically store a lot more data for customers compared to ServiceNow and Atlassian, also offer graph databases or similar data management products. Neo4j, which helped pioneer graph databases after its founding in 2007 and was privately worth $2.4 billion as of 2021, appears to be booming: The company’s second quarter revenue, for instance, was higher than its full-year 2025 revenue, according to CEO Emil Eifrem. “For 20 years, I've been screaming into the void about the value of graphs,” Eifrem told me. “And now all of a sudden, everyone is talking about it.” Microsoft Patches Copilot Security Flaw Microsoft has patched a security flaw in its Copilot AI software that could allow hackers to trick the AI into leaking companies’ data, a Microsoft spokesperson confirmed. The flaw was found by researchers at PromptArmor, a small startup that has emerged as a watchdog for such AI vulnerabilities. (Anthropic last year tweaked its Claude for Excel product after The Information reported on PromptArmor’s research into potential security flaws.) PromptArmor researchers in June found that hackers could create a malicious “ skill ”—a set of instructions for Copilot that companies can configure—and trick Copilot into spitting out data from across the company’s Microsoft accounts, including emails from Outlook, files from SharePoint, and Teams messages. Like other recently discovered Copilot security flaws , this one relied on getting Copilot to send data that was meant to stay within the Copilot application to a proxy server that hackers could remotely access, according to PromptArmor cofounder Shankar Krishnan. Skills for chatbot assistants are increasingly popular, and they function similar to a Chrome browser plugin in that anyone can create one and post it online for others to use. Chatbots like Claude, ChatGPT, and Perplexity also support skills. Microsoft has a built-in skills scanner for Copilot meant to detect malicious skills, but it didn’t catch the malicious skill PromptArmor designed, Krishnan said. “We appreciate PromptArmor for reporting this through coordinated vulnerability disclosure,” the Microsoft spokesperson said in a statement. “We have addressed the report, and customers are already protected and do not need to take any action. title: DeepSeek’s Revenue Reaches $70 Million as of July, Tenfold Jump from 2025
content: DeepSeek generated about 475 million yuan ($70.7 million) in revenue in the first seven months of this year, roughly tenfold its full-year 2025 revenue, as the Chinese AI lab goes full steam ahead in its second round of funding, according to two people with knowledge of the company’s financial data. DeepSeek recorded a net loss of about 715 million yuan between January and July, compared to 935 million yuan for the entire 2025, the two people added. The company is having ongoing discussions with existing and new investors about the funding round, which aims to raise 50 billion yuan at a valuation of 500 billion yuan. DeepSeek didn’t immediately respond to an emailed request for comment. While DeepSeek’s revenue is still minuscule compared to U.S. AI model developers such as Anthropic and OpenAI, the company is achieving a healthy gross profit margin. That’s because it has managed to keep the costs of running its models low, such as improving the efficiency of its AI infrastructure so that the AI systems can perform tasks using fewer chips. DeepSeek’s gross margin for the first seven months was 44.6%, and the gross margin for selling access to its models through application programming interface was 82.9%. By comparison, OpenAI generated $5.7 billion in revenue and a 39%  gross margin in the first quarter, while Anthropic recorded $11.5 billion in revenue in the second quarter and projected that its gross margin in 2026 would rise to 63% from 40% in 2025. The revenue and other numbers, which haven’t previously been reported, show an accelerated pace in just the last few months. The Information last month reported that DeepSeek’s annualized revenue had reached between $400 million and $500 million. DeepSeek’s revenue growth could give a boost to the funding talks and a potential initial public offering down the line. The company raised 50 billion yuan in its first-ever funding round closed in June and almost immediately started its second funding round. It has hired investment banks to help prepare a listing in Shanghai next year. The growing revenue highlights the greater adoption of DeepSeek’s open-source AI models. Its flagship V4 series, especially the small-size V4-Flash , is popular among developers around the world due to their low costs and solid capabilities. DeepSeek has recently taken steps to further increase its revenue. Earlier this month, the company increased its API prices. The price of its flagship V4-Pro model, for example, rose to $3.96 for output per 1 million tokens at peak hours and $1.98 at non-peak hours—up sharply from the current price of $0.87. But even after the price hike, DeepSeek’ models are still much cheaper than other popular Chinese and American models. Moonshot’s Kimi K3 charges $15 for output, while Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5 costs $25 for output. DeepSeek’s expenses are growing fast, too, albeit still tiny compared to the U.S. labs. In the first seven months of this year, DeepSeek spent about 11 billion yuan on AI infrastructure-related expenses, including renting servers equipped with AI chips or purchasing chips and other computing equipment. In 2025, the company spent only about 1.2 billion yuan on such expenses.

title: How Companies Are Using Old-School Software to Grade AI Agents
content: Measuring the quality of an AI model’s work can be tricky, especially when it comes to AI agents that can take a broad range of actions to autonomously solve a task. As businesses turn to agents to automate longer and more important tasks, they are getting savvier about how to evaluate the performance of those agents. “Enterprises are getting more sophisticated,” said Brad Kenstler, director of general agents at Scale AI, where he focuses on developing evaluations for Scale’s enterprise customers. “They’re looking to deploy agents into much more business-critical operations.” One surprisingly important way that enterprises are improving evaluations is by grading agents using software programs, rather than relying on another AI to serve as a judge. Scale is discussing developing these so-called “programmatic verifiers” with all its customers, including Mayo Clinic, real-estate and finance firm Howard Hughes and educational publishing company Cengage. When companies started adopting agents, evaluators would often use an AI judge to monitor, for example, whether the agent correctly cited its sources or kept its answer below a certain word count. But that requires paying to run a second AI model. Software code is cheaper to use. The move toward traditional software for certain evaluation work might seem counterintuitive at a time when AI is supplanting so much of traditional software, but it also reflects enterprises’ growing familiarity with the limitations of AI models, such as their high costs and unreliability. For example, my colleagues reported late last year that Salesforce was deprioritizing large language models in Agentforce , in favor of traditional software automation that followed if-then rules. AI judges remain an effective approach when the criteria for determining success are “squishy,” Kenstler said. In such cases, to provide a grade, a judge scores an agent’s outputs against a grading rubric. For example, if an agent is told “I want you to write a report on the Revolutionary War,” the rubric might include criteria like “the report mentions that George Washington was the general of the Continental Army,” Kenstler said. Programmatic verifiers can evaluate performance on more black-and-white criteria, such as whether an agent has solved a math problem, correctly formatted a spreadsheet or included a specific phrase in its output. An enterprise that is evaluating how well an agent can work with a CRM database could use a programmatic verifier to check whether the database has been updated, without relying on another AI to serve as a judge. Increasing use of these programmatic verifiers “is bringing a greater level of rigor and outcome-orientation to the way that enterprises are doing evals,” said Kenstler. Because they’re cheaper, programmatic verifiers allow enterprises to more thoroughly evaluate their agents’ actions, potentially catching more errors and better understanding the pros and cons of different agents. While Kenstler is primarily focused on evaluations, which measure the performance of an AI model after it has been trained, both of these techniques can also be used to improve AI agents during reinforcement learning. So are programmatic verifiers going to put AIs out of their jobs as judges? Not quite. “The best evaluations combine both,” Kenstler said. For example, if an AI agent was tasked with producing a regulatory filing, it might have to follow a standardized format, which can be checked programmatically, as well as include the right details and adhere to a company’s guidelines about how information is presented, which are better suited for AI. In fact, for some tasks the trend has gone the opposite direction: from relying on programmatic verifiers to increasingly drawing on AI judges. “Coding agents is a great example of a use case that starts with programmatic and is now trending rubric,” Kenstler said. For example, older coding benchmarks such as the popular SWE-Bench use automatic tests to check whether an AI wrote successful code. But measuring whether the AI followed good style requires bringing in an AI judge. To be sure, evaluating agents will continue to be a challenge for the foreseeable future, but using all the available tools will help enterprises select the best AI models for a given task and maybe even help catch naughty agents trying to hack into other companies. title: Inside Nikesh Arora’s Deals Hunt for Palo Alto Networks
content: Palo Alto Networks CEO Nikesh Arora has never shied away from deals, acquiring more than 40 companies in the eight years since he took the helm of the world’s biggest standalone cybersecurity firm. But over the past 18 months, Arora’s appetite for acquisitions has reached a new fever pitch as he expanded the company’s products to handle new AI threats as well as capture more revenue from existing customers. For instance, he explored acquiring Datadog, which sells software that helps businesses identify security threats and monitor how cloud applications perform, and Okta, which helps companies ensure workers have access to the right systems, according to two people with knowledge of the situation. Arora had fallback plans when those two potential deals didn’t pan out. In February, Palo Alto Networks paid $25 billion to buy CyberArk, an identity software firm that competes with Okta in some areas. And in January it paid $3.35 billion for Chronosphere, a smaller competitor to Datadog. Behind Arora’s dealmaking is his conviction that AI will fundamentally change how companies protect IT systems against cyber threats by requiring that companies constantly monitor their systems to ward off AI agents that can now pull off hacks that humans never could. By adding a variety of new services, he also wants to convince enterprises to expand their budgets with Palo Alto Networks at the expense of rivals Fortinet, Zscaler, Microsoft and Cisco, according to people who have spoken to Palo Alto Networks executives. Arora is currently interested in potentially acquiring products that complement Chronosphere by helping companies cut the cost of analyzing their log data and databases, according to a person with knowledge of his thinking. Companies that sell such products include Cribl, a startup valued at $3.5 billion after its last funding two years ago, and ClickHouse , valued at $15 billion after a funding round in January, said the person. More recently, Arora has been exploring potential deals in AI security, including firms that make products designed to help companies protect against cyberattacks that target the AI their employees are using, another person said. But its AI product ambitions seem broader; in May, Palo Alto Networks bought Portkey, a so-called router or gateway that helps companies use AI models from multiple providers and monitor usage and spending, for hundreds of millions of dollars, according to someone with direct knowledge of the deal size. A Palo Alto Networks spokesperson said the company doesn’t comment about “rumors or speculation.” Spokespeople for Datadog and Okta didn’t comment. Arora’s “platformization” strategy to get more businesses to buy a suite of products is a work in progress. But Palo Alto Networks’ shares are up 90% this year, giving it a nearly $280 billion market capitalization, as AI’s increasing ability to spot software vulnerabilities has prompted companies to pay more for security. Arora has told shareholders that revenue from AI-related products is growing quickly but the company hasn’t yet broken out exact revenue from such sales. The company reports its July quarter earnings next week. Shares of competing firms such as CrowdStrike and Fortinet have also performed well this year. CrowdStrike has been buying companies that resemble the ones Palo Alto Networks has bought, though CrowdStrike’s deals have had much lower prices. Microsoft, meanwhile, is overhauling its security business to make AI-powered security tools a selling point for its broader suite of traditional security products. “The consolidation wave is real, especially as these firms rethink what security solutions look like in the age of AI,” said Menlo Ventures partner Rama Sekhar, who said he expects “at least three or four” more major acquisitions of AI-focused security firms. Arora joined Palo Alto Networks in 2018, after years spent as Google’s chief business officer and a two-year stint as president of SoftBank. Before Arora began his effort to strike megadeals last year, he had only done smaller acquisitions, generally worth less than $1 billion, while at Palo Alto Networks. In late 2024, Arora had his eyes on identity security, a subset in cybersecurity that manages employees’ logins to make sure that they (and the AI tools they’re using) only access the data they’re supposed to. With lots of established competitors in the field, including Microsoft, Okta and CyberArk, Arora felt he needed to do a big deal to have a real seat at the table, according to a person familiar with his thinking. That led Arora to approach Okta. Between late 2024 to early 2025, Arora held a series of meetings with Todd McKinnon, CEO of Okta, which was valued at about $13.5 billion at the start of last year, according to two people with knowledge of the talks. These talks progressed to a point where the companies discussed how their products could potentially complement each other, but ultimately stalled after the companies couldn’t agree on a price, these people said. By July, Palo Alto Networks agreed to acquire CyberArk, another publicly traded identity software firm for $25 billion. (Okta shares are up about 30% since July of last year, giving it a $23 billion market capitalization.) In the spring of 2025, Arora met with Datadog CEO Olivier Pomel and pitched him on a hypothetical acquisition of Datadog, which was publicly valued at more than $40 billion at the time, according to someone with knowledge of the situation. Pomel wasn’t receptive and the talks never resulted in a formal offer, this person said, eventually leading Arora to pursue Chronosphere instead. Since then, Datadog’s market capitalization has roughly doubled to more than $80 billion, making it even less likely that Pomel would consider such a tie-up. In June, Palo Alto Networks said Chronosphere and CyberArk contributed $338 million of the $3 billion in revenue the company generated in the April quarter. Companies have been raising their cybersecurity budgets to protect against new threats from AI, and both Anthropic and OpenAI are selling AI-powered cybersecurity products that aim to discover and patch vulnerabilities. Anthropic in May launched Mythos, which companies have used to find vulnerabilities in their systems, and OpenAI last month said its AI had hacked its own systems and those of Hugging Face and other app developers, underscoring the threat other businesses may face. Palo Alto Networks uses models from Anthropic and OpenAI for research and to power some products for customers, but it’s racing to launch more of its own. For instance, Palo Alto Networks recently developed a product that uses AI as well as data observability features from Chronosphere to scan companies’ IT systems and detect potential AI threats in a matter of minutes, said a person with knowledge of the product, which hasn’t been announced. More than 600 of Palo Alto Networks’ customers, including FedEx, Home Depot, and DHL, are already using it, this person said.

title: Why Big Tech is Suddenly Paying Up for Startups
content: When The Information broke the news that OpenRouter was in talks to sell the company last month, a shock wave rippled across Silicon Valley. My phone lit up with bankers asking me if I had also heard that there had been a record nine suitors for the company, which helps customers switch between different AI models and centralize billing. I got the sense that at least two people I called about the deal turned around and placed their own bids as soon as I hung up. The scene would have been unusual a year ago. OpenRouter, founded just three years ago, was on a tear. The company more than doubled its valuation to $1.3 billion in a year. It recently hit $160 million in annualized revenue, The Information reported . Companies with that kind of growth typically don’t head for the exits. But this is not 2025. In the first half of 2026, there has been a big shift. Big tech companies are, all of a sudden, willing to pay astronomical prices for startups. SpaceX snapped up AI coding giant Cursor—which hit annualized revenue of $4 billion in June—for $60 billion. Stripe nabbed OpenRouter for more than $7 billion. And Hugging Face, a popular platform for sharing AI models, is also in talks for a sale at an eye-popping potential multiple . The acquirers are opening up their wallets because they see major revenue opportunities by integrating these startups into their services. And the cost of capital is cheap, so the risk is relatively small. Many are willing to pay up for these deals simply to avoid the risk of losing out down the line if they don’t move into new businesses. And the Trump administration isn’t resisting these deals. “Big tech companies are willing to pay up for opportunity cost,” Adrian Aoun, a longtime Valley entrepreneur and investor, told me. “Those are the transactions going left, right and center.” Their wild offers are causing changes of heart among founders who previously never thought of selling—and leaving many in the Valley speechless. It’s a validation of something I’ve long thought investors in big tech are overlooking: the fact that tech giants can make huge sums of money by applying AI to their existing businesses. Founders recognize the power of scale too. The current demand for deals is being driven by “the strategic premium attached to scale in the AI era, the growing cost of inaction as this technology cycle accelerates and a more constructive macro and financing environment that is giving boards the confidence to act,” Kim Posnett, global co-head of investment banking at Goldman Sachs, told me Tuesday. Posnett has played leading roles in many recent deals, including the SpaceX IPO. But some caution the M&A appetite has its limits. Investors and founders don’t expect to see some of the larger-revenue AI startups—Vercel, Sierra and Lovable, for example—taken out anytime soon. Doing so would require much bigger commitments on the part of the acquirers. That hasn’t happened in a big way yet. But I think we’re only at the beginning of this wave, which began to take hold with Meta’s $14 billion deal for a chunk of Scale AI last year. Between antsy founders who worry they are one major GPT or Claude release away from extinction and the rising appetite of the acquirers, much more is to come.

title: Why OpenAI’s Jalapeño Might Sicken Nvidia
content: Exactly who at OpenAI decided to name the company’s first internally designed chip Jalapeño? That might have seemed like a good idea a few months ago—perhaps OpenAI imagined that name would serve as a subtle indicator that the chip is a hot property. But it’s not ideal right now, when the Food and Drug Administration is warning that products containing jalapeños shouldn’t be eaten, served or sold thanks to a salmonella outbreak tied to the peppers. OpenAI must be hoping that’s not an omen, and so far it doesn’t seem to be. The AI firm on Tuesday unveiled the first test results for Jalapeño, claiming the chip showed “a significant performance advance: Jalapeño can serve more AI work per unit of power while also returning responses more quickly.” OpenAI CEO Sam Altman tweeted that “we made a chip and it is fast.” AI research firm SemiAnalysis put out a review claiming that Jalapeño is “better than Nvidia Blackwell.” Ouch. Nvidia chips are of course the ones to beat in AI. It must particularly gall Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang that he’s a major financial backer of OpenAI. Nvidia committed $30 billion to OpenAI just a few months ago . One of the reasons Nvidia invests money in companies is to underwrite demand for its products! OpenAI has a different agenda. As we reported in this story earlier this year , developing its own chip—which it did in conjunction with Broadcom—is a way for it to reduce hardware costs and improve its margins. Nvidia’s AI chips are pricey, after all. And it’s not just about the cash outlays for chips. OpenAI also hopes a chip specially designed for inference—running AI  models—will operate more efficiently than Nvidia’s more general-purpose AI chips. OpenAI noted today that it would continue to use Nvidia chips for both training and inference once it deploys Jalapeño, of course. But that’s a bit like the statements we often hear from Amazon and Google, both of which talk up their own AI chips while also acknowledging that they make Nvidia chips available in their cloud units for customers. The more easily Nvidia’s customers can replace its chips with alternatives, the worse things are for Jensen Huang. Perhaps he should remind people of the health dangers of eating jalapeños. Paramount’s Next Steps California’s attorney general, Rob Bonta, is getting a lot of attention for the lawsuit he and 11 other state attorneys general filed to block Paramount Skydance’s $110 billion purchase of Warner Bros. Discovery. The state attorneys general are operating under the delusion that we’re still in the 1990s—they allege that Paramount would get too much power in the slowly dying cable television industry and the film industry. Someone needs to remind the attorneys general that strength in streaming video, not cable, is what matters now, and in streaming both Paramount and Warner are behind leaders like Netflix. It is possible Bonta is trying to do Paramount CEO David Ellison a favor. After all, the best thing for the company would be to jettison many of the cable channels it would inherit if the Warner deal goes through. And since Paramount is taking on a lot of debt—the combined business would have $79 billion of debt at closing—raising money by selling a few declining assets wouldn’t be a bad idea. Ellison should thank Bonta for the idea and dump as many cable channels as he can! In Other News • LayerZero, a blockchain infrastructure startup that counts Citadel Securities, DTCC, and Intercontinental Exchange among its partners, said it’s launching a new blockchain-based exchange targeting financial institutions this fall. • Zoom Communications reported 4.9% revenue growth for the July quarter, a slowdown from the 5.5% growth it reported in the April quarter, and projected an even slower growth rate for the current quarter. • SpaceX announced on Tuesday its plans to build a $100 billion launch site for its Starship rocket on the coast of Louisiana. The company intends to begin construction in 2027 and is targeting 2029 for the first Starship launch from the site. title: Why Revenue Is Hopping at Data Observability Startups
content: A cluster of startups taking on database giants Snowflake, Databricks and Datadog are experiencing a revenue windfall thanks to rising adoption of AI agents. That could lead to a wave of startup dealmaking, from new investments to M&A. Earlier Tuesday, I reported that ClickHouse’s annual recurring revenue jumped 40% from May to $350 million , and that OpenAI’s use of the startup, which provides free open-source software and paid cloud services to help companies analyze large volumes of data, has jumped this year. OpenAI’s use is notable, since the ChatGPT maker has also been a customer of publicly traded Datadog, the giant in observability—or monitoring the actions humans and AI agents take on computers. ClickHouse last raised funding at a $15 billion valuation in January and fielded many approaches this year from strategic buyers, according to a person with direct knowledge of the discussions. “We don’t dismiss interest because we have a responsibility to our shareholders but we are not selling the company, quite the contrary,” Chief Executive Aaron Katz told me. ClickHouse isn’t alone in benefiting from the large data needs spurred by AI agents. Cribl, which helps companies manage and analyze telemetry generated by both humans and AI agents, says its annual recurring revenue is near $400 million, up 33% from February. “Our enterprise customers are experiencing a massive data growth driven in part by AI and the advent of agents and we’re helping them handle it,” said Cribl cofounder and CEO Clint Sharp. The eight-year-old company says it helps customers including Zoom, ServiceNow and Hilton by routing them to cheaper storage and the most efficient monitoring tool. “The problem we solve is that your data is growing at a 30% compound growth rate, and your budget isn't,” Sharp said. Cribl, which last raised venture funding in August 2024 at a $3.5 billion valuation, is aiming for an initial public offering in the next couple of years, said Sharp. And Grafana, a 12-year-old startup that sells tools that let developers visualize in real time how their applications, cloud servers and AI agents are behaving, says it’s recently seen a pickup in revenue. That’s in part thanks to the company’s AI assistant, which helps companies observe activity on their own apps, said Scott Fingerhut, Grafana’s chief marketing officer. Fingerhut said half of Grafana’s customers this year used the assistant to get the company’s software to monitor their systems or configure tools. The company, which was valued at $9.6 billion in March, on Wednesday passed $600 million annual recurring revenue, up from $400 million in September. It frequently comes up as a possible acquisition target for a larger company interested in data monitoring, say software bankers. Elastic, Snowflake Purchases Already, larger companies have been buying startups that specialize in monitoring data. Elastic, a publicly traded company that provides an open-source search engine for large data sets, on Monday bought Deductive AI, which helps engineers monitor data to resolve issues, for $85 million. Two weeks ago, Dynatrace paid $915 million for Arize AI, whose AI tracks how models and agents behave. Snowflake closed its $1 billion purchase of Observe in June, betting that customers already storing their data in its platform will want the tools to see how their applications are performing. The acquisition, first reported by The Information , followed cybersecurity company Palo Alto Networks’ purchase of observability startup Chronosphere for $3.35 billion. Other acquisitions are likely, investors and bankers say. Cybersecurity firms, big tech companies such as Google, Amazon and Microsoft, and networking companies like Cisco could all make a play for startups that monitor data. “As AI agents take on more autonomous work, companies need visibility into what they’re doing and safeguards to catch failures or security risks before they cause harm,” said Mike Jung, partner at Founders Circle Capital, which has backed Databricks, Vercel, ClickHouse and Cribl. (This story has been updated to add Grafana’s recent annual recurring revenue.) title: “人造太阳”中国环流四号目标图像发布
content:
2026-08-26 16:05 来源：中国新闻网
中国环流四号是第四代磁约束核聚变大科学实验装置，是全球首个高温超导强场稳态燃烧实验平台，将系统验证聚变复杂环境下高温超导强场磁体可靠性;演示聚变堆全域智能控制，实现装置长时间稳态运行。
核聚变能是人类未来能源发展的重要方向，全球主要国家竞相布局核聚变能新赛道。科学技术部副部长张光军当日指出，“十五五”规划将可控核聚变作为未来能源技术纳入能源创新发展重点方向，并将可控核聚变列入国家前沿科技攻关重大工程项目。他指出，要清醒认识到核聚变能实现的艰巨性、复杂性、长期性，尊重科学规律，充分发挥新型举国体制优势，稳步推进核聚变技术工程化、产业化。
8月25日，2026核聚变能大会暨核聚变活动周在上海开幕，“人造太阳”中国环流四号目标图像在此间发布。(中国聚变能源有限公司供图)
上海市政协副主席吴信宝表示，面向未来，上海将加快推进聚变能前沿技术创新和未来产业培育，聚力突破高温超导磁体等关键技术，强化人工智能技术应用，加强创新联合体建设，完善聚变开放创新生态。
中核集团董事长申彦锋表示，中核集团依托中国环流三号先进装置取得“双亿度”等突破性成果，加速推进聚变关键技术攻关。去年3月，中国环流三号装置首次实现“双亿度”突破，标志着中国可控核聚变研究进入燃烧实验阶段。　　当日的开幕式上，《核聚变能装置技术图谱(第一卷)——托卡马克卷》、中国环流四号目标图像、长三角高温超导磁体技术创新联合体聚变堆高温超导磁体研制路线图发布。
据了解，大会为期4天，包括学术交流、主题论坛、工业企业展等多种活动。70余家科研院所、高校、商业聚变公司及供应链企业参加大会配套工业企业展览等活动。

title: 中国环流四号高温超导磁体研制路线图明确
content:
中国环流四号高温超导磁体研制路线图明确
8月25日，2026核聚变能大会暨核聚变活动周期间，中国聚变能源有限公司牵头组建的长三角创新联合体已明确高温超导强场托卡马克磁体研制目标：2028年前建成首条25T高温超导强场磁体研制和测试线，2030年前完成原型磁体研制。
该联合体由中国聚变能源有限公司牵头，成员包括上海超导、东部超导、上海交通大学、上海电气核电集团、超磁新能、能量奇点、杭氧集团、翌曦科技。联合体将重点形成高温超导强场托卡马克磁体研制能力和工程化技术体系，为中国环流四号后续建设提供关键技术支撑。
中国环流四号由中国聚变能源有限公司建设，是全球首个高温超导强场稳态燃烧聚变实验平台。该装置将系统验证聚变复杂环境下25T高温超导强场磁体的可靠性。按照规划，装置建成后聚变增益Q值将大于5;当Q值大于1时，意味着聚变输出能量超过外部输入能量，实现净能量增益。
高温超导强场磁体是磁约束聚变装置的核心部件之一，直接关系到等离子体约束能力和未来聚变堆工程化水平。有研究报告指出，在国际热核聚变实验堆 (ITER) 的关键设备成本结构中，磁体部分占比达28%，为占比最高的单项设备类别;真空室、冷屏和杜瓦等三大部件合计占比约12%。
近年来，全球核聚变投资保持增长，中美在该领域投入规模位居前列，磁约束技术路线受到广泛关注。除中国环流四号外，美国SPARC装置、英国球形托卡马克能源生产装置 (STEP) 等也采用高温超导技术路线。高温超导磁体的研制进展，将成为判断聚变能源工程化进程的重要指标。

日本伊方核电站2号机组沥青固化装置恢复正常
四国电力株式会社 (Shikoku Electric Power Co.) 2026年8月25日通报称，处于退役状态的日本伊方核电站2号机组沥青固化装置已于当天10时45分恢复至正常状态。此前发现异常的混合机上盖结合部垫片已完成更换，试运行结果未见异常。
该事件发生在4月28日。当天，运行人员在反应堆辅助厂房管理区域内启动沥青固化装置时，发现装置混合机温度计附近出现类似水蒸气的现象，随后该现象自行消失。检修人员随后检查确认，15时05分，类似水蒸气的气体来自混合机内部，并从混合机上盖结合部逸出;17时06分，沥青固化装置停止运行。
外观检查显示，混合机上盖结合部的垫片存在变形。垫片到货后，检修人员对设备进行了分解检查，确认混合机本体无异常，并将相关垫片更换为新品。
更换完成后，四国电力对沥青固化装置进行了试运行，确认混合机上盖结合部未再出现类似水蒸气的逸出现象，设备运行状态无问题。四国电力表示，本次事件未对机组造成影响，也未对环境产生放射性影响，后续将继续开展详细调查。

title: 生态环境部华北核与辐射安全监督站开展田湾核电站7号机组首次装料监督
content:
2026-08-26 08:53 来源：生态环境部华北核与辐射安全监督站
近日，田湾核电站7号机组首次装料工作正式启动，第一组燃料组件顺利装入反应堆堆芯，机组正式转入带核运行调试阶段。该机组是中俄两国元首视频连线见证开工的重点合作工程。此次装料，标志着中俄核能合作最大战略合作项目取得重大阶段性成果。
首次装料作为核电工程核心关键工序，是机组工程建设质量、系统调试成效及安全管控能力的一次综合性、全面性核验，对机组后续安全稳定运行具有决定性意义。生态环境部华北核与辐射安全监督站(以下简称华北监督站)始终秉持“严慎细实”的核安全监管作风，紧盯首次装料核心关键环节，对本次装料作业实施全覆盖、全链条、全过程监督管控，切实守牢装料作业安全质量防线。
装料启动前，监督人员聚焦装料先决条件，开展全方位核查，逐项核验组织措施与人员准备、运行许可证执照文件批复情况、相关系统设备准备情况等，为装料作业顺利开展夯实前置基础。
装料实施期间，现场监督人员全程驻守作业一线，紧盯燃料组件起吊、场内转运、堆芯装入、精准就位等关键工序，对每一项操作流程的规范性、合规性进行严格核查、精准把控，全程严控作业风险、及时排查消除隐患，确保装料全过程规范有序、可控在控。
后续，华北监督站将持续跟进机组带核调试阶段各项工作，聚焦首次临界、功率提升等关键重大节点，坚持从严监管、精准把关，对后续各类调试试验实施过程监督，保障机组后续调试工作安全、平稳、有序开展，助力项目稳步投产运行。

title: 科技部副部长张光军出席2026核聚变能大会暨核聚变活动周开幕式
content:
科技部副部长张光军出席2026核聚变能大会暨核聚变活动周开幕式
2026年8月25日，2026核聚变能大会暨核聚变活动周在上海开幕，科学技术部党组成员、副部长张光军出席开幕式并致辞。
张光军表示，我国始终高度重视核聚变能创新发展，“十五五”规划将可控核聚变作为未来能源技术纳入能源创新发展重点方向，并将可控核聚变列入国家前沿科技攻关重大工程项目。我们要坚定信心，同时尊重科学规律，求真务实、开拓创新，充分发挥新型举国体制优势，合力攻坚，加快推进核聚变技术工程化、产业化。
本次大会以“聚力创新聚变未来”为主题，分为核聚变能大会、核聚变活动周两大核心板块，同期举办、联动推进。核聚变能大会聚焦科技研发最新进展，旨在打造我国核聚变能领域高水平学术交流平台。核聚变活动周着力推动核聚变能科技与产业深度融合，将举办工业企业展、圆桌论坛及核聚变科普等多场活动。
大会由中国国际核聚变能源计划执行中心、核工业西南物理研究院、中国科学院等离子体物理研究所、中国工程物理研究院共同主办，中国聚变能源有限公司和上海国有资本投资有限公司承办。科技部、上海市、中国核工业集团有限公司等有关负责同志和单位代表、ITER组织代表等出席开幕式。

title: IAEA总干事披露海上核能专项新倡议即将出台
content:
IAEA总干事披露海上核能专项新倡议即将出台
国际原子能机构(IAEA)总干事拉斐尔·格罗西(Rafael Grossi)近日表示，该机构正准备启动一项新倡议，以推动民用核技术在海上场景中的应用。
这项名为“海上应用原子技术许可”(ATLAS)的倡议，将于8月26日至27日在美国华盛顿特区举行的国际原子能机构部长级活动上正式发布。该倡议旨在为核动力船舶、浮动核电站等海上民用核应用的部署提供支持，并推动相关许可和监管工作衔接。
格罗西表示，ATLAS倡议可为全球贸易提供支撑，也有助于为偏远社区和工业用户提供能源。他在倡议启动前与美国能源部长克里斯·赖特(Chris Wright)举行会晤，并感谢美国对该倡议的支持。
双方会谈还涉及核不扩散等议题。根据目前公布的信息，ATLAS倡议将重点围绕海上核能应用的安全、许可和部署条件展开，以帮助相关技术从示范应用走向更广泛的民用场景。

title: 俄罗斯库尔斯克核电站VVER-TOI机组提前完成年度发电计划
content:
俄罗斯库尔斯克核电站VVER-TOI机组提前完成年度发电计划
俄罗斯库尔斯克核电站新建VVER-TOI机组已提前4个月完成年度发电计划。截至8月25日，该机组向俄罗斯统一电力系统累计送电超过44.6亿千瓦时，使库尔斯克核电站发电量较国家计划目标超出近50%。
该机组为俄罗斯国家原子能公司 (Rosatom) 旗下功率最大的创新型VVER-TOI机组，也是三代加核电机组。库尔斯克核电站方面称，其发电量相当于库尔斯克市居民约两年的用电需求。
这台新机组于2025年12月31日首次并网，并于2026年5月1日起进入电能与容量市场，正式向俄罗斯统一电力系统用户供电。今年4月底，该机组投入商业运行，转入在运状态，并根据库尔斯克核电站自1976年以来各机组设计、建设和投运顺序，正式命名为库尔斯克核电站7号VVER-TOI机组。
库尔斯克核电站站长亚历山大·乌瓦金表示，这一结果验证了VVER-TOI新型机组系列的效率。该三代加反应堆机组有助于提高燃料循环效率，并增强电力供应能力。
目前，Rosatom正在库尔斯克核电站替代容量场址继续建设两台VVER-TOI机组。按照俄罗斯电力设施布局总体规划，到2034年，库尔斯克核电站替代项目计划形成4台机组、总装机容量5000兆瓦的规模，用于逐步替代现有RBMK-1000机组。
库尔斯克核电站是俄罗斯原子能发电公司 (Rosenergoatom) 下属分支机构，也是俄罗斯“中央”电力系统的重要节点之一。该电力系统覆盖俄罗斯中央联邦区19个州。目前，库尔斯克核电站3号、4号RBMK-1000机组以及7号VVER-TOI机组按调度计划运行;1号、2号机组因达到规定运行期限，处于无发电运行状态。核电站及周边地区辐射本底处于机组正常运行水平，未超过天然本底值。

title: 俄罗斯罗斯托夫核电站向冷却池投放小球藻强化生态防控
content:
俄罗斯罗斯托夫核电站向冷却池投放小球藻强化生态防控
俄罗斯罗斯托夫核电站 (Rostov NPP) 近日在厂区技术水库开展年度生态防控作业，向水体投放3.6吨以浮游藻类小球藻为基础的生物活化剂，以抑制水华风险，维护冷却池生态平衡。
罗斯托夫核电站隶属于俄罗斯国家原子能集团 (Rosatom) 电力业务板块的俄罗斯核电运营公司 (Rosenergoatom)。此次作业属于该核电站长期实施的“藻类调控”措施，主要用于在气候变化和异常高温条件下稳定水体状态，保障相关设备平稳运行。
小球藻可作为天然生物过滤因子，能够抑制部分病原微生物繁殖，增加水体含氧量，并减少对化学药剂的依赖。核电站方面表示，该方法有助于在不使用化学品的情况下维持大面积技术水库水质。
罗斯托夫核电站冷却池内栖息着20多种鱼类。核电站工作人员每年还会向池中投放草鱼、鲤鱼、鲢鱼和俄罗斯鲟鱼等鱼类，用于消耗过度繁殖的水生植物和斑马贻贝，配合维持水域生态稳定。
罗斯托夫核电站环境保护部代理主任尤利娅·费季索娃 (Yulia Fetisova) 表示，核电站按照严格的科学标准监测水库状态，并通过研究浮游植物群落评估措施效果。每个季节至少由经认证实验室采样三次，监测范围不仅包括核电站技术水库，也包括齐姆良斯克水库大坝段的水化学指标。
罗斯托夫核电站厂长安德烈·萨尔尼科夫 (Andrey Salnikov) 表示，夏季气温升高会增加水库生态系统压力。对核电站而言，这既是环境管理问题，也关系到运行安全。该站自2008年以来每年开展相关藻类调控工作，期间技术水库未发生大规模藻类暴发。核电站方面称，综合防控措施有助于确保水质符合技术和环境标准，并保障俄罗斯南部地区电力供应稳定。

title: 加拿大安大略省为兰姆顿核电方案社区咨询拨款
content:
加拿大安大略省为兰姆顿核电方案社区咨询拨款
加拿大安大略省政府 (Government of Ontario) 将投入50万加元，用于在安大略省 (Ontario) 西南部兰姆顿县 (Lambton County) 科伦纳 (Corunna) 社区就新建发电项目开展进一步咨询。该项目拟建在已关闭的兰姆顿燃煤发电站旧址，未来能源方案将在核能和天然气之间进行比较和讨论。
根据安排，这笔资金将支持地方市政当局、原住民社区及相关居民参与咨询。安大略省能源部长斯蒂芬·莱切 (Stephen Lecce) 表示，省方倾向于发展清洁能源和高出力发电项目，但最终推进方向将取决于纳税人、地方政府和原住民社区的意见。
兰姆顿燃煤发电站于2013年关闭，当时造成近400人失业。安大略省希望利用该旧址约485公顷土地，以及既有分区条件、输电线路和交通连接，以缩短新发电设施建设周期。拟建项目若建成，预计可向电网新增900兆瓦电力，约可满足90万户家庭用电需求。
莱切说，如选择建设小型核电设施，从建设到投运发电可能需要长达十年时间。目前，该项目的具体技术路线、投资成本和就业规模尚未确定。
圣克莱尔镇 (St. Clair Township) 镇长杰夫·阿加尔 (Jeff Agar) 表示，推动该发电站旧址重新投入使用是其任内重点目标之一。圣克莱尔镇议会此前已通过动议，支持包括核能在内的潜在发电项目。莱切强调，省方将与当地社区合作推进相关讨论，在形成地方意见后再决定项目后续方向。

title: 国际原子能机构第70届大会将举办核能相关边会
content:
国际原子能机构第70届大会将举办核能相关边会
国际原子能机构 (IAEA) 核能部将于2026年9月14日至18日在奥地利维也纳举行的国际原子能机构第70届大会期间，举办例行核电运营者论坛和三场核能相关边会。相关边会日程将在确定后公布。
核电运营者论坛将以“微型反应堆：塑造新的运行格局和应用”为主题，计划于2026年9月17日10时30分至12时30分在C楼七层CR3会议室举行。论坛将通过行业和技术专家专题讨论，介绍微型反应堆研发与部署的国际进展，议题包括关键设计特征、新兴技术、燃料和部署方案，以及安装、运行中的实际考量和在建项目经验。会议还将关注微型反应堆设计多样化、研发格局变化，以及实际应用、社会因素和市场预期对技术选择的影响。
“天然放射性物质管理和可持续解决方案方面的国际合作”边会将于2026年9月15日10时30分至11时30分在M楼底层M4会议室举行。该活动将围绕天然放射性物质残留物的整体管理展开，介绍表征、清单编制和管理方面的实用方法，并探讨符合循环经济原则的再利用与资源回收机会。主要议题包括全球天然放射性物质来源和存量、工业管理挑战、资源回收、循环经济应用、退役相关问题，以及国际合作和支持机制。
“培养下一代核能领导者：非洲的经验”边会定于2026年9月17日15时至16时30分在M楼一层M6会议室举行。会议将讨论领导力发展如何支撑全球核能行业可持续发展，并重点关注非洲新兴核电项目。与会专家将结合IAEA支持的相关举措和成员国经验，探讨人员绩效、劳动力发展、知识转移、青年参与，以及先进核技术和人工智能对核能人才队伍和行业发展的影响。
“扩大核能项目融资途径”边会将于2026年9月17日16时至17时在M楼一层M4会议室举行。IAEA预测，到2050年全球核能装机容量将接近1太瓦。围绕这一部署规模，会议将讨论核能项目融资和风险缓释的新兴方法，内容涵盖与多边开发银行合作、可持续金融工具和碳市场等方向。

title: 埃及达巴核电站四台机组同步建设
content:
VVER-1200
俄罗斯国家原子能公司
俄罗斯国家原子能公司 (Rosatom) 总裁阿列克谢·利哈乔夫 (Alexey Likhachev) 与埃及电力和可再生能源部长马哈茂德·伊斯马特 (Mahmoud Esmat) 近日就达巴核电站建设进展进行讨论。达巴核电站是埃及首座核电站，规划建设4台VVER-1200型反应堆机组，建成后预计可为约2000万人提供电力。
利哈乔夫表示，项目已进入关键建设阶段，4台机组正在同步推进。其中，1号机组是项目建设的先导机组，计划于2028年并网发电。为实现这一目标，项目方还需完成多项工作，包括在2027年交付核燃料。
2号机组建设也在继续推进。今年7月，该机组反应堆压力容器已安装至设计位置，相关发电启动准备工作正在进行。
目前，达巴核电站3号、4号机组的安装和土建施工同步展开，相关工作包括实体防护系统以及陆上水工建筑物建设。项目现场共有约2.5万名工人参与施工。
利哈乔夫称，除埃及企业深度参与本地化生产外，欧洲企业也参与项目供货，部分货物来自中国。目前，汽轮机厂房设备、电气设备及控制系统供应总体正常，欧洲和亚洲供应商均按计划交付产品。
俄方还将为达巴核电站培训1700名运行和管理人员，以支持电站未来投运后的运行工作。

title: 日本JT-60SA实验团队推进下一运行阶段准备工作
content:
日本JT-60SA实验团队推进下一运行阶段准备工作
JT-60SA实验活动下一阶段筹备工作正在推进。技术团队正按计划开展综合调试，实验团队同步完善相关工具和软件，以提升下一运行阶段的科学产出能力。
在QST组织的一次培训课程中，EUROfusion的参与者正在学习如何使用人机界面(HMI)设置放电设置，为下一次JT-60SA作战行动做准备。图片来源：QST
第三届JT-60SA实验团队研讨会已于2026年7月27日至31日在日本量子科学技术研究开发机构 (QST) 那珂中心举行。约50名专家参会，其中包括来自欧洲的20名代表，人员来自欧洲聚变发展联合体 (EUROfusion) 相关实验室、大学以及欧洲聚变能源开发联合企业 (Fusion for Energy, F4E)。会议重点围绕欧洲和日本研究团队协作、实验准备及技术交流展开。
研讨会期间，QST组织了面向参会人员的培训课程，重点介绍专用于JT-60SA实验设置的人机界面 (HMI)。在QST专家完成讲解后，学员进入控制室开展实践操作，学习如何配置放电参数，并利用HMI准备后续实验研究。欧洲参会人员在QST团队指导下完成培训，同时就HMI功能和易用性提出反馈意见。
欧洲团队还持续参与先进数值工具开发，为JT-60SA高质量实验设计提供支撑。会上，瑞士洛桑联邦理工学院 (EPFL) 的多梅尼科·弗拉托利洛 (Domenico Frattolillo) 和意大利国家研究委员会 (CNR) 下属等离子体科学与技术研究所 (ISTP) 的卡洛·索齐 (Carlo Sozzi) 介绍了脉冲设计模拟器功能。该平台可用于实验和运行方案的开发、测试与优化，相关方案在实施前可先完成模拟验证。
除培训外，研讨会还讨论了等离子体控制策略、数据分析以及JT-60SA专题小组相关工作。会议最后，来自EUROfusion和日本多所大学的新学员进行了汇报，分享HMI培训体验，并介绍研讨会期间取得的进展。
JT-60SA实验负责人之一、QST的吉田麻衣子 (Maiko Yoshida) 表示，随着技术和科研团队持续推进准备工作，本次研讨会标志着JT-60SA实验活动向下一阶段迈出重要一步。欧洲方面实验负责人叶夫根·卡扎科夫 (Yevgen Kazakov) 表示，欧洲和日本团队在研讨会期间围绕QST的人机界面、分析工具，以及EUROfusion的分析软件和脉冲设计模拟器开展了双向交流，这类知识共享对下一阶段JT-60SA实验具有重要意义。

title: 美国HFIR研究反应堆助推新型核燃料验证
content:
美国HFIR研究反应堆助推新型核燃料验证
美国能源部 (DOE) 位于橡树岭国家实验室 (ORNL) 的高通量同位素反应堆 (HFIR)，正在成为美国新型核燃料研发和鉴定体系中的关键设施。8月25日发布的一篇研究论文指出，在美国商业核电和先进反应堆建设需求增长的背景下，可用于新型燃料测试的研究反应堆资源趋于紧张，HFIR有望缓解相关试验能力不足的问题。
图片来源：Gunes Ozcan/橡树岭国家实验室，美国能源部
HFIR是全球中子通量最高的稳态研究反应堆之一，长期用于核燃料和材料辐照试验。论文认为，该反应堆能够提供验证新型燃料所需的重要数据，为延长反应堆寿命、提升运行效率以及推动先进反应堆技术部署提供支撑。
在试验适应性方面，HFIR可覆盖多种测试条件和实验平台。该反应堆设有三个主要辐照区域，可布置小型“兔式”辐照胶囊。这类胶囊设计、制造和部署周期较短，可放入反应堆中心的通量阱，使样品接受最高水平的中子通量。HFIR的可拆卸铍反射层区和永久铍反射层区还可用于规模更大、结构更复杂的辐照实验，包括配备仪器、传感器或热中子屏蔽装置的试验，以调节中子通量谱。
在燃料研发方面，橡树岭国家实验室长期利用HFIR开展分离效应试验和整体燃料试验。该反应堆曾在高温气冷堆燃料架构研发中发挥重要作用，特别是三结构各向同性 (TRISO) 燃料颗粒相关研究。近期，研究人员还基于微型燃料 (MiniFuel) 概念开展试验，辐照对象包括事故容错燃料 (ATF)、涂层燃料颗粒和金属燃料等。这些工作与HFIR通量阱内开展的大量燃料包壳辐照实验形成补充。
HFIR的现代化改造进一步增强了仪器化实验能力。通过材料辐照装置 (MIF)，ORNL可利用受控吹扫气体混合物调节温度，并在同一实验中独立控制多个温度区域。自动化监测系统能够持续跟踪温度、压力和气体成分，并支持研究人员远程实时监测和调整实验参数。相关能力已用于TRISO燃料在辐照过程中的裂变气体释放测试，显示HFIR可同时支持多个复杂高通量实验。
论文还指出，HFIR获取的燃料性能数据可为美国核管理委员会 (NRC) 进行核燃料鉴定提供技术依据。这些数据涉及裂变气体释放、微观结构演变以及燃料与包壳相互作用等关键性能指标，可用于验证燃料性能、支撑安全分析，并为新型燃料监管审评相关技术报告提供基础。
HFIR所在的ORNL园区还配套有较完整的核燃料检测和分析设施，包括包覆颗粒燃料开发实验室、低活化材料开发与分析实验室、辐照燃料检测实验室以及辐照材料检测与测试设施。依托这些设施和ORNL长期积累的燃料研发经验，HFIR已形成覆盖燃料制备、辐照、检测和分析的综合试验平台。
研究认为，随着电力公司推动现有反应堆延寿，先进反应堆开发商加快商业化进程，HFIR在快速获取高质量燃料数据、推动燃料从概念阶段走向监管认证阶段方面仍将发挥重要作用。该研究由美国能源部核能办公室先进燃料计划支持。

title: 美国NRIC遴选13个核能启动平台项目
content:
美国NRIC遴选13个核能启动平台项目
美国能源部 (U.S. Department of Energy, DOE) 下属国家反应堆创新中心 (National Reactor Innovation Center, NRIC) 当地时间8月24日宣布，13个新项目入选“核能启动平台”计划。NRIC设在爱达荷国家实验室 (Idaho National Laboratory, INL)。
NRIC主任布拉德·托默 (Brad Tomer) 表示，本轮入选项目反映出开发商推进相关技术发展的意愿持续增强。该计划将为企业提供获得能源部授权的优先路径，并提供专家资源、设施条件和针对性监管支持，以推动先进核技术从概念阶段走向商业化应用。
根据该计划申请指南中的评审标准，DOE与NRIC本轮共遴选出12家开发商的13个项目。项目方向涵盖反应堆开发和核燃料循环改进，涉及制造、浓缩和转化等技术。入选企业可开始与NRIC对接，使用“核能启动平台”提供的技术、监管和部署支持。
本轮入选开发商包括安塔瑞斯核能公司 (Antares Nuclear)、阿特拉斯原子公司 (Atlas Atomics)、部署式能源公司 (Deployable Energy)、福奇原子公司 (Forge Atomics)、赫克西姆公司 (Hexium Inc.)、光桥公司 (Lightbridge Corporation)、努萨诺公司 (Nusano)、奥克洛公司 (Oklo)、雷文-弗林特核能公司 (Raven-Flint Nuclear)、斯卡尔特德原子公司 (Scalted Atomics)、萨布莱姆核能公司 (Sublime Nuclear) 和瓦拉尔原子公司 (Valar Atomics)。
NRIC表示，“核能启动平台”计划将继续接受申请，并根据资源情况滚动开展后续遴选。未在本轮评审中入选的项目，可修改申请材料后在后续轮次重新提交。
美国能源部负责核燃料循环的副助理部长乔什·贾雷尔 (Josh Jarrell) 表示，稳定的核燃料供应链对美国未来能源体系具有重要意义，本轮入选项目体现了制造、浓缩和转化技术方面的实际进展。能源部将与相关企业合作，加强本土燃料供应能力。
美国能源部代理副助理部长奇米·扎科特 (Chimí Zacot) 表示，反应堆试点项目和燃料管线试点项目早期进展良好，本轮遴选结果显示，一批先进核能项目正继续朝部署方向推进。
爱达荷国家实验室主任约翰·瓦格纳 (John Wagner) 表示，INL具备核能研究基础设施、技术专长和长期运行经验。“核能启动平台”将这些能力向开发商开放，帮助其以安全、高效的方式推动技术从设计阶段进入部署阶段。
“核能启动平台”计划旨在支持私营企业加快先进核技术开发和应用。该计划建立在DOE于2025年6月启动的反应堆试点项目，以及2025年8月启动的燃料管线试点项目基础上，利用更灵活的技术和监管框架，推动先进核技术在联邦土地和非联邦土地上部署。
该计划包括两条路径：爱达荷国家实验室启动平台 (Launch Pad INL) 依托INL的核能研究基础设施、运行经验和监管支持;美国启动平台 (Launch Pad USA) 则将相关框架扩展至美国各地的联邦和非联邦机构。NRIC成立于2019年，主要任务是联合工业界和国家实验室，推动先进核技术跨越概念、示范与商业化之间的衔接阶段。

title: 美国推进高燃耗乏燃料运抵爱达荷州研究准备
content:
美国推进高燃耗乏燃料运抵爱达荷州研究准备
INL 被选定为接收地点，主要因为其具备处理乏核燃料所需的专用设施、设备和人员经验。美国能源部称，这些能力通常并非商业核电站常规配置。高燃耗燃料是指在反应堆中停留时间较长、以提高能量输出的核燃料。
近期，美国能源部核能办公室 (NE)、环境管理办公室 (EM) 代表及私营部门合作方在爱达荷州开展协调工作，并参观相关核设施和清理设施，以推进此次运输准备。其中，爱达荷州核技术与工程中心 (INTEC) 是重点参观点之一。该中心工作人员长期承担乏核燃料接收、处理、包装和储存任务，支持环境管理办公室的清理工作。
参访人员查看了 INTEC 一处历史水池设施。该设施可容纳约 300 万加仑水，曾长期用于乏核燃料水下储存。2023 年，爱达荷州清理项目及其承包商爱达荷州环境联盟 (IEC) 已完成相关乏核燃料转移，将其迁入 INL 厂址内较新的干式储存系统。
参访人员还考察了辐照燃料储存设施。该设施目前仍由受训人员负责接收并安全储存来自 INL 厂址先进试验反应堆的乏核燃料。
运输配套方面，相关方还讨论了 INTEC 铁路线翻新进展。爱达荷州环境联盟提出，可重新利用 INTEC 既有铁路基础设施，以支持高燃耗研究容器转运。该方案被认为有助于提高运输效率、降低成本，并为未来往返 INL 厂址的乏核燃料运输建立必要通道。
按照当前安排，该研究容器预计将于 2027 年底运输至 INL。届时，爱达荷州环境联盟工作人员将在 INTEC 接收并储存该燃料容器;美国能源部环境管理办公室和核能办公室将继续推进现场转移准备，以服务后续研究。
美国能源部表示，此次高燃耗研究用乏燃料容器运输将是 20 多年来首次有乏核燃料运抵爱达荷州，相关工作建立在美国能源部持续遵守 1995 年《爱达荷州和解协议》的基础上。该研究将为乏核燃料长期安全储存和未来运输提供数据支持。
该运输任务属于核能办公室与电力研究院 (EPRI) 合作开展的高燃耗干式储存研究项目。爱达荷州清理项目还将协助把宾夕法尼亚州立大学布雷泽尔研究反应堆 (Breazeale Research Reactor) 的乏核燃料运往 INL。相关燃料曾服务于大学研究反应堆运行，并支持核能和医学研究。

title: 美国聚变路线图瞄准2030年代中期早期电厂部署
content:
美国聚变路线图瞄准2030年代中期早期电厂部署
美国能源部 (DOE) 近期发布《聚变科学与技术路线图》，提出在2030年代中期加快早期聚变发电厂部署。该路线图是美国联邦层面推进聚变技术从实验研究走向工程化、商业化的重要安排，由2025年11月成立的聚变办公室协调实施。
与现有核电站依靠裂变反应释放能量不同，聚变装置试图将轻原子核聚合在一起，其能量来源原理与太阳相同。聚变发电被视为潜在的低碳能源方向，但行业目前仍处于实验和示范阶段，私人开发商尚未实现商业意义上的“净能量增益”，即聚变反应产生的能量超过启动和维持反应所需能量。
路线图提出三项重点任务：建设关键基础设施，缩小聚变材料和技术差距;推动人工智能、先进计算和研究设施开放共享，加快技术创新;通过公私合作扩大供应链和人才队伍。文件还设置了短期、中期和长期里程碑，聚焦结构材料、面向等离子体部件、燃料处理技术等关键环节。
目前，美国有28家聚变公司从事相关技术开发。多数企业采用托卡马克或仿星器路线，通过强磁场约束超高温等离子体;也有企业探索激光驱动的惯性约束聚变等方案。业内人士认为，不同技术路线虽然装置形式不同，但普遍面临相似难题，包括氚燃料分离与再处理，以及制造能够长期承受高能中子辐照的部件。
Realta聚变公司 (Realta Fusion) 对外事务主管罗布·休斯 (Robb Hughes) 表示，路线图为商业部署提供了较完整路径，但目标能否实现取决于联邦资金支持力度。他认为，如果关键环节投入不足，聚变商业化时间表可能被推迟。
聚变工业协会数据显示，截至2026年7月的12个月内，全球聚变企业融资额达到44.8亿美元，资金主要来自私人投资者;自2021年以来，累计融资额已达142.4亿美元。美国政府主要通过聚变能源科学计划 (FES) 支持聚变研究。2022年通过的相关立法授权2027财年该计划最高可获得11亿美元拨款，但国会最终安排的拨款为7.9亿美元，低于2026年已执行的8.057亿美元。
路线图还强调通过公私合作推动研发。美国能源部现有项目包括基于里程碑的聚变能源开发计划和“聚变创新网络”(INFUSE)。其中，里程碑计划在2022年至2027年期间预算为4.15亿美元，企业在达到预定技术目标后获得付款。参与企业包括联邦聚变系统公司 (Commonwealth Fusion Systems, CFS)、Focused Energy、Realta Fusion、Thea Energy、Tokamak Energy、Type One Energy、Xcimer Energy和Zap Energy。
INFUSE项目则帮助私营聚变企业直接使用美国能源部国家实验室和高校的专业能力、计算资源及测试设施。联邦聚变系统公司、Type One Energy、Zap Energy、Pacific Fusion和Realta Fusion等开发商已获得相关支持，并与劳伦斯·利弗莫尔国家实验室 (Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory)、橡树岭国家实验室 (Oak Ridge National Laboratory)、普林斯顿等离子体物理实验室 (Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory) 等机构开展合作。
美国能源部还在2025年1月通过FIRE计划向六个研究联盟提供1.07亿美元资金，推动国家实验室、高校和私营企业之间的协作。今年早些时候启动的Fusion BRIDGE项目，则将共同出资建设共享型中小型实验设施。
在数字化研发方面，路线图提出促进人工智能、先进计算和量子技术用于聚变工程。相关工具可帮助开发商建立反应堆数字孪生体，在制造前对部件进行压力测试，并优化磁场控制，以提高等离子体稳定性。美国能源部计划建设人工智能聚变数字平台，把实验设施和测试设施数据与模拟、数字孪生及工程工具连接起来，从而缩短聚变系统从实验到设计、再到运行的周期。

title: 荷兰推进两座新核电站前端工程设计
content:
荷兰推进两座新核电站前端工程设计
荷兰核能组织(NEO NL)已向法国电力公司(Électricité de France，EDF)和西屋电气公司(Westinghouse Electric Company，Westinghouse)授予合同，由两家公司为荷兰拟建的两座新核电站开展设计研究。相关工作被视为建设准备阶段的下一步，两家公司将在夏季结束后启动第一阶段研究。
此次设计研究在国际上称为前端工程设计第一阶段(FEED 1)，将分两个阶段实施。第一阶段为FEED 1a，不依赖核电站具体厂址，因此可在荷兰政府推进选址程序的同时继续开展相关准备工作。
待荷兰内阁作出首选厂址决定草案(oVKB)后，第二阶段FEED 1b将启动。该阶段将围绕已选定厂址展开更具针对性的研究。通过分阶段推进，所有与厂址无关的工作可按既定计划先行开展。
根据计划，EDF和西屋电气将在研究中评估各自基于成熟三代半反应堆技术的设计方案，如何满足荷兰法律法规和监管要求。评估内容包括建筑法规、许可要求、技术标准以及项目总体进度安排等，同时也将及早识别潜在风险和需要重点关注的环节。
研究成果将为两座核电站后续筹备提供重要依据，并有助于明确未来核电站业主与技术供应商之间的职责边界。相关研究预计耗时12至18个月，具体周期将取决于荷兰政府何时通过首选厂址决定草案。
当前阶段，荷兰方面尚不会确定最终技术供应商。技术供应商的选择将在正式招标程序完成后作出，该程序将在后续阶段启动。
此次研究还将帮助EDF和西屋电气为核电站建设提交更充分的方案，进而提高成本可预见性，降低实施风险，并支持形成更稳健、管理更审慎的采购流程。
本轮设计研究是在此前可行性研究基础上推进的。此前研究主要评估相关反应堆设计是否适合在荷兰部署;新的设计研究则将在更详细层面，对照荷兰完整的法律和监管要求进一步审查相关设计方案。

title: 韩国启动下一代核能科研人才培养计划
content:
韩国启动下一代核能科研人才培养计划
韩国面向核能领域博士后研究人员的人才培养计划正式启动，将以高校实验室为基础，推动未来核技术研究、产学研合作和就业衔接。
8月25日，在“2026气候与能源招聘会”期间，韩国气候能源环境部 (Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment)、韩国能源技术评估规划院 (Korea Institute of Energy Technology Evaluation and Planning, KETEP) 和韩国辐射促进协会 (Korea Radiation Promotion Association) 举行“核能领域下一代能源领袖培训计划”揭牌仪式，宣布相关工作全面展开。
该项目由韩国气候能源环境部和韩国能源技术评估规划院支持，韩国辐射促进协会负责实施。项目重点面向博士后研究人员，目标是在提升科研能力的同时，推动高校积累的研究成果进入产业应用场景。
按照计划，该项目不局限于科研经费支持，还将把联合研究、技术交流、面向产业需求的能力培养以及就业支持纳入同一体系，形成覆盖科研、产业合作和职业发展的全周期培养机制。
韩国方面认为，核能产业的技术范围正在从传统大型核电机组拓展至创新型小型模块化反应堆 (i-SMR)、核安全、乏核燃料与放射性废物管理、核设施退役以及核聚变等方向，对高层次科研人才的需求持续上升。
目前，韩国全国10所高校的17个实验室参与该项目，相关高校包括庆熙大学 (Kyung Hee University)、东国大学WISE校区 (Dongguk University WISE Campus)、首尔大学 (Seoul National University)、世宗大学 (Sejong University)、延世大学未来校区 (Yonsei University Mirae Campus)、蔚山科学技术院 (Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology)、济州大学 (Jeju National University)、浦项科技大学 (Pohang University of Science and Technology)、韩国科学技术院 (Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology) 和汉阳大学 (Hanyang University)。
参与实验室将与博士后研究人员共同开展研究，方向涵盖小型模块化反应堆、核安全、核燃料、辐射应用和核聚变等未来技术领域。项目同时要求研究工作与产业界实际技术需求相衔接，以提高成果转化和合作应用的可能性。
韩国辐射促进协会计划分阶段推进未来技术研发、产学研合作项目、技术交流、产业需求导向培训、专家研讨会、专业人士指导以及面向参与实验室和博士后研究人员的就业支持。
该人才培养计划还将纳入人工智能应用能力训练。韩国辐射促进协会执行副总裁朴正基 (Park Jeong-ki) 表示，随着人工智能等前沿技术发展，核能研发环境正在快速变化，协会将支持博士后研究人员成长为兼具专业研究能力和人工智能应用能力的核心科研人才。
项目后续成效将取决于高校实验室研究成果能否进一步转化为产业合作、技术转让和就业机会。韩国方面希望借此提升核能产业技术竞争力，并形成从高校实验室通向产业一线的高层次人才培养生态。

title: 韩国机张郡与KHNP磋商古里核电站居民沟通问题
content:
韩国机张郡与KHNP磋商古里核电站居民沟通问题
韩国釜山机张郡8月25日表示，机张郡方面当天与韩国水力原子能公司 (KHNP) 就古里核电站相关待解决问题进行会谈，重点涉及居民沟通、共生支持资金分配、乏燃料干式贮存设施以及小型模块化反应堆项目等事项。
据机张郡介绍，韩国水力原子能公司社长金会天 (Kim Hoe-cheon) 当天到访机张郡政府，与机张郡郡守禹成彬 (Woo Sung-bin) 会面。金会天自3月18日就任以来，持续走访核电站所在地，了解地方诉求，此次到访古里核电站所在地机张郡，也是相关沟通行程的一部分。
会谈中，机张郡方面提出，古里2、3、4号机组继续运行所涉及的共生支持资金分配问题，已在当地引发担忧和分歧。禹成彬表示，围绕协商程序和分配标准的疑虑正在加深居民间矛盾，KHNP应更主动提出公平、合理的解决方案，减少核电站周边居民的失落感和对立情绪。
针对乏燃料干式贮存设施建设，机张郡要求在推进相关程序前，与地方政府开展实质性协商，并制定能够促进地区共同发展的配套措施。机张郡还提出，应依据《高放射性废物管理特别法》，由高放射性废物管理委员会、地方政府及相关处置机构等组成协商机制，在征求居民意见前先拿出具体的共生方案。
机张郡同时强调，KHNP正在推进的创新型小型模块化反应堆 (i-SMR) 首台机组项目，如需签署相关谅解备忘录，应以充分沟通和居民理解为前提。禹成彬表示，在开展行政协作前，必须优先回应居民对小型模块化反应堆安全性的疑虑;作为项目实施主体，KHNP应直接提供客观、透明的信息，并提前面向居民举行安全说明会。
金会天表示，将认真听取核电站所在地居民的意见，关注古里2、3、4号机组继续运行所需共生支持资金分配引发的地方问题，并寻求平稳解决。他还表示，对于居民说明会等事项，KHNP将事先与机张郡保持密切协商。
禹成彬表示，机张郡将把居民利益和社区和谐放在首位，避免核电站周边居民产生被排除感。他要求KHNP作为化解地区矛盾的重要一方，更积极地与居民沟通，并推动当天讨论事项形成可执行的解决方案。

title: 韩国研发AI模型用于核设施震后检查排序
content:
韩国研发AI模型用于核设施震后检查排序
韩国标准科学研究院 (KRISS) 与蔚山科学技术院 (UNIST) 联合研究团队开发出一种深度学习模型，可在地震发生后辅助核设施快速判断重点检查区域。该模型仅利用单台地震仪采集的地震波信号，实时预测核电站内部多个位置的振动响应，并对潜在风险进行量化排序。
研究由韩国标准科学研究院高级研究员李在范 (Jae-Beom Lee) 和蔚山科学技术院教授李英柱 (Young-Ju Lee) 团队共同完成。研究人员表示，该技术可在不为每个关键位置安装传感器的情况下，推断核设施内139个未布设传感器位置的振动情况，从而帮助运行方更快缩小震后排查范围。
地震后，即便设施未出现明显损伤，安全确认和详细检查仍可能导致较长停运时间。资料显示，2016年韩国庆州发生5.8级地震后，月城核电站1至4号机组经过约80天的性能确认和详细检查后恢复运行。今年7月日本熊本发生强震后，台积电熊本1号工厂也曾暂停运行，并在设备检查和调整后逐步恢复正常。
该研究的核心在于“虚拟传感”技术。模型通过分析单台地震仪记录的地震波，实时推断设施内部不同位置的振动响应;即便面对未参与训练的实际地震记录，也表现出较好的预测能力。研究团队还将结构特性带来的不确定性纳入计算，将各位置振动响应超过预设风险标准的概率量化为0%至100%。
这一方法并非简单给出“安全”或“危险”的二元判断，而是按风险概率高低对检查点位进行排序。对核电站等大型复杂设施而言，这有助于专家在震后优先核查高风险区域，提高安全验证效率。
研究团队还提出了一种根据结构固有频率推导最优人工智能结构的设计公式，减少了反复设计、比较模型所需的试错过程。按该方法设计的AI模型，在准确性上可与部分最新深度学习模型相当，但参数量远低于后者，计算负担也明显降低，更适合在计算资源受限的现场环境中应用。
由于该AI模型可根据不同结构的振动特性进行灵活设计，研究团队认为，相关技术未来还可扩展至半导体工厂、数据中心等大型工业设施的震后安全评估。
李在范表示，在安全人工智能领域，准确预测和认识模型判断边界同样重要。后续研究将继续提升模型可靠性，使其能够在存在不确定性的场景下辅助人员作出判断。
相关成果已形成三篇论文，其中包括发表于国际期刊《可靠性工程与系统安全》(Reliability Engineering & System Safety) 的论文。研究得到韩国国家研究基金会个人基础研究项目和韩国标准科学研究院基础研究项目支持。

title: 工信部回应新能源汽车“内卷”：要坚守住产品质量底线--中国能源新闻网

工信部回应新能源汽车“内卷”：要坚守住产品质量底线
“新能源汽车已经成为中国制造的一张亮丽名片。我们要清醒地看到，当前产业发展也存在一系列的问题和挑战。”工信部副部长辛国斌26日在国务院新闻办发布会上说道。
他表示，非理性竞争的问题仍然较为突出，一些“激进式”创新设计未经充分实验验证就装车应用，还出现了个别引发社会关注的汽车产品质量、自动驾驶安全等事件。这些问题都不容忽视、不可回避，是“十五五”时期必须要加力解决的重点问题。
为此，工信部研究制定了《智能网联新能源汽车产业发展“十五五”规划》，通过规划引导、部门协同、政策支持等多措并举，推动产业持续高质量发展。
辛国斌表示，完善行业治理体系。推进汽车企业生产资质集团化管理改革，优化产业布局。加强产品创新设计准入审查和测试验证管理，严禁未经充分测试验证的产品进入市场。加大产品生产一致性监督检查力度，切实维护好消费者的合法权益，进一步规范好产业竞争秩序。
“十四五”时期，我国新能源汽车产业规模从百万辆级跃升到千万辆级，年销量从136.7万辆增加1649万辆，在汽车新车销售中的占比也从5.4%提高到47.9%。整车集成、动力电池、激光雷达等技术水平已经跻身世界前列，新能源汽车、动力电池及关键材料产量占到全球的70%以上。
与此同时，新能源汽车产业的国际影响力也在持续增强，产品远销到100多个国家和地区，培育了一批具有较强竞争力的领军企业。
面向“十五五”，辛国斌表示，进一步提升产品供给质量。将支持重点企业加大技术攻关力度，持续提升动力电池低温适应性、耐久性，提高自动驾驶安全性、可靠性。要积极稳妥推进智能网联汽车准入和上路通行试点，“车路云一体化”试点，为广大消费者提供更加绿色智能的智能网联新能源汽车产品。要坚守住产品质量底线，为广大消费者负责。
此外，要优化配套使用环境。要开展汽车以旧换新、新能源汽车下乡、县域充换电设施补短板试点，推动实现充电站“县县全覆盖”、充电桩“乡乡全覆盖”。这方面目前广大农村地区还是有不完善的地方。同时，建立健全汽车改装管理制度，优化新能源汽车车险政策、降低维修成本，切实解决消费者后顾之忧，让消费者愿意买、放心用。（

title: “人造太阳”中国环流四号目标图像发布--中国能源新闻网

“人造太阳”中国环流四号目标图像发布--中国能源新闻网
中国能源传媒集团
中电传媒股份有限公司主办
能源中国IOS版
“人造太阳”中国环流四号目标图像发布
中新社上海8月25日电 2026核聚变能大会暨核聚变活动周25日在上海开幕。“人造太阳”中国环流四号目标图像在开幕式上发布。
中国环流四号是第四代磁约束核聚变大科学实验装置，是全球首个高温超导强场稳态燃烧实验平台，将系统验证聚变复杂环境下高温超导强场磁体可靠性；演示聚变堆全域智能控制，实现装置长时间稳态运行。
核聚变能是人类未来能源发展的重要方向，全球主要国家竞相布局核聚变能新赛道。科学技术部副部长张光军当日指出，“十五五”规划将可控核聚变作为未来能源技术纳入能源创新发展重点方向，并将可控核聚变列入国家前沿科技攻关重大工程项目。他指出，要清醒认识到核聚变能实现的艰巨性、复杂性、长期性，尊重科学规律，充分发挥新型举国体制优势，稳步推进核聚变技术工程化、产业化。
8月25日，2026核聚变能大会暨核聚变活动周在上海开幕，“人造太阳”中国环流四号目标图像在此间发布。(中国聚变能源有限公司供图)
上海市政协副主席吴信宝表示，面向未来，上海将加快推进聚变能前沿技术创新和未来产业培育，聚力突破高温超导磁体等关键技术，强化人工智能技术应用，加强创新联合体建设，完善聚变开放创新生态。
中核集团董事长申彦锋表示，中核集团依托中国环流三号先进装置取得“双亿度”等突破性成果，加速推进聚变关键技术攻关。去年3月，中国环流三号装置首次实现“双亿度”突破，标志着中国可控核聚变研究进入燃烧实验阶段。
当日的开幕式上，《核聚变能装置技术图谱(第一卷)——托卡马克卷》、中国环流四号目标图像、长三角高温超导磁体技术创新联合体聚变堆高温超导磁体研制路线图发布。
据了解，大会为期4天，包括学术交流、主题论坛、工业企业展等多种活动。70余家科研院所、高校、商业聚变公司及供应链企业参加大会配套工业企业展览等活动。

title: 44名专家坐诊一线 难题当场“开药方”华北油田公司技能专家巡诊服务精准破解生产卡点
content:
今年以来，该公司人事处锚定一线生产堵点痛点，持续深化技能专家巡诊服务机制，把技术课堂搬到井场、把攻关阵地设在班组，推动专家资源向生产末梢下沉。8月24日，该公司技能专家协会采油采气分会集结各单位44名技术骨干组成巡诊团，联合采油四厂、河北储气库开展专场技术帮扶，为基层难题精准“把脉开方”。
跨界“组队”：多兵种联合作战，打通专业“隔墙”
本次巡诊打破以往单一单位、单一专业的帮扶局限，由采油四厂与河北储气库联合承办，横跨采油、采气、轻烃装置等多个专业领域，组建跨工种复合型攻坚团队。针对新能源场景下的交叉性难题，多专业专家同步研判、协同施策，补齐了“单一专业解不了综合问题”的能力盲区。
与此同时，巡诊全程推行“师徒结对”参与模式，所有报名人员均由师傅带徒弟共同上阵，把巡诊现场变成流动实操课堂。从被动听讲解到主动揭榜攻关，从练熟操作到琢磨创新，从个人提升到团队共进，通过“实操演练＋创新研讨＋成果共享”的传帮带路径，实现技术传承与价值创造双向赋能。
现场“摆摊”：成果实物开讲，附赠“终身售后”
针对一线生产的共性痛点，本次巡诊精选《自润滑扶正式偏心井口盘根盒》《天然气硫化氢含量检测气体安全采样装置》等5项成熟创新成果集中推广。不同于传统“念材料、发手册”的灌输模式，现场全程实物演示，由成果主研人拆解结构原理、演示操作步骤、讲明注意事项，手把手带着参会人员上手试用，确保当场弄懂原理、学会操作。
更让一线员工暖心的是，所有推广成果均配套完整使用说明，同时附上发明人联系方式，相当于给出“终身技术售后”承诺。后续现场使用遇到任何问题，都能直接对接主创人员答疑指导，彻底解决了“学的时候会、回去用就忘、出问题没人管”的后顾之忧，让创新成果真正用起来、见实效。
挂账“销号”：一题一策一抓到底，不解决不松手
为避免巡诊“一阵风”，本次活动建立“难题预征集—专家现场办—挂账持续跟”的全闭环机制。活动前期就面向基层征集筛选出9项重点生产难题，提前匹配对应专业专家，做到“带着问题来、盯着问题解”。
现场实行“一题一组、一策一案”的攻坚模式，9个难题逐一对应专家小组，当场研判、现场攻关。最终，采气井井口安全阀拆卸难等4项问题当场形成解决方案并完成现场验证；其余5项复杂棘手问题，由认领专家与属地单位无缝对接，明确整改时限、建立跟踪台账、定期跟进进度，确保难题不解决不销号、服务不到位不脱钩。

title: 7个方面、20项措施 国家电网发布“十五五”碳达峰目标实现若干举措

一、推动能源电力结构转型
1.服务新能源等清洁能源高质量发展。推动国家和地方、电源与电网规划衔接，全力保障沙戈荒大基地、分布式、海上风电等新能源“应并尽并”。滚动开展新能源消纳能力测算，服务地方主管部门优化新能源发展规模、布局和时序，合理设置利用率目标。支持存量水电站增容改造和设备更新，推动核电和灵活调峰气电有序发展。“十五五”经营区年均新增新能源装机2亿千瓦左右。
2.促进煤电清洁高效利用。坚持优容量、控电量、促转型，服务新一代煤电建设，积极支持煤电低碳化、灵活性改造，推动绿氨掺烧、CCUS等减碳固碳技术商业化应用，推动燃煤自备机组参与电网调峰，推广北方供热机组热电解耦，2030年经营区煤电平均最小发电出力达到35%额定负荷。
3.加强抽水蓄能、新型储能调节能力建设。加快新疆哈密、吉林安图等一批抽蓄电站建设和前期工作，“十五五”公司新投产、新开工抽蓄均超过3000万千瓦，力争2030年公司在运在建抽蓄规模超1.2亿千瓦。服务新型储能更大规模发展，“十五五”经营区新增新型储能装机1.4亿千瓦。
二、打造清洁能源优化配置平台
4.提升电网清洁能源大范围配置能力。加快特高压通道建设，“十五五”新投产跨区直流15回，跨省区输电能力达到5亿千瓦。推进华中—南方、华中—华东等省间电力互济工程建设，跨区灵活互济能力大幅提升，较“十四五”末扩大两倍以上。加强区域主网架建设，华北、华东、华中和西南特高压交流电网规模翻一番，西北、东北省间联络整体加强。
5.提升电网多元要素承载能力。持续加强配电网建设，提升电网对分布式电源接纳承载能力，满足年均6000万千瓦以上新增分布式电源接网需要。提升新型主体与电网高效互动能力，推进农村能源革命试点，建设一批县域有源配电网、村镇级微电网、末端保供型微电网示范工程，协同推进工业绿色微电网发展，促进新能源就地高效利用。
6.提升系统低碳运行能力。增强对各类清洁能源的预测与调控水平，加强新能源场站和储能调度运行，合理确定煤电调度顺序，加大启停调峰力度，保障新能源“能发尽发”。强化源荷高效互动，加快虚拟电厂建设，提升负荷资源需求响应能力。加快推进新增用电量由新增清洁能源电量覆盖，2030年经营区新能源发电量占比达到30%以上。
三、服务重点领域节能降碳
7.大力支持算电协同、零碳园区等新业态发展。推动新能源基地与算力设施协同布局，推进算力跨区域跨时段低碳调度，加强算电协同线上服务专区建设，支撑新建算力设施主要使用非化石能源电力。支持新能源就地消纳，提供建档立户“一站式”服务，实现业务全流程高效办理。积极服务零碳园区、零碳工厂等建设，支撑经营区首批国家级零碳园区及后续国家和地方试点按期建成。
8.全力支撑工业、建筑、交通等电能替代。推广电锅炉、电窑炉、电炉冶炼等技术应用，推进工业领域电能替代。推进建筑光伏一体化，加强“煤改电”供电服务保障，推动采暖、厨炊等领域电气化改造。优化私人乘用车充电报装接电服务，推进公共充电设施焕新升级，支撑农村地区充电服务网络延伸，持续做好港口岸电、电气化铁路供电服务。积极对接零碳运输走廊规划布局，服务兆瓦级充电设施建设，支撑新能源重卡规模化应用。2030年电能占终端能源消费比重达到35%。
9.强化重点领域行业节能降碳服务。深化“供电+能效服务”，聚焦工业、建筑、数字基础设施、公共机构等重点领域开展能效碳效诊断。深化绿电绿证服务，支撑重点行业企业完成可再生能源消费最低比重目标。依托全国公共机构节约能源资源综合信息平台，支撑公共机构能耗定额管理和能效分级，推广能源托管等服务模式。持续开展“e起节电”活动，提供线上智能化能效碳效账单服务，倡导绿色低碳生产生活方式。
四、提升公司绿色低碳水平
10.加强公司节能降碳。制定实施公司高质量节能降碳指导意见，推进办公生产外购电100%绿色电力消费，推动绿色建筑改造、车辆清洁化替代，加强绿色数据中心、绿色工厂、零碳供电所等示范建设。加强公司碳资产管理，开发电网相关碳减排方法学。在公司碳达峰基础上，“十五五”碳排放强度降低超过18%、能耗强度稳步下降。
11.强化绿色电网建设。加强电网工程全生命周期碳足迹管理，电网规划环节充分贯彻节能降碳理念，强化建设过程碳排放监测与管控，建设一批零碳变电站。加强电网线损精细化管理，提升电网经济运行效能，推广应用高效节能变压器，推动综合线损率稳步下降。强化六氟化硫气体回收利用，加快替代技术研究应用，稳妥推进混合气体GIS设备改造。
12.深化绿色供应链建设。完善绿色低碳评价标准体系，强化电工装备典型设施产品碳足迹核算和绿色采购应用，稳步提升绿色采购规模。完善绿色仓储建设标准，加快仓储绿色基础设施建设。建设绿色拆解分拣中心，推动退役回收物资绿色处置。
五、完善促进清洁能源发展市场机制
13.健全清洁能源参与市场机制。有序推动气、水、核等电源参与市场，推广沙戈荒大基地“联营不联运”模式，公平无歧视服务新型主体入市。加大跨省区电力交易力度，常态化开展跨经营区交易，提升通道输送清洁能源电量比例。推动发用两侧报量报价参与现货交易，通过充分竞争促进清洁能源消纳。
14.深化绿电绿证市场建设。优化多年期绿电交易机制，推广小时级绿电交易，开展度电赋码等技术研究及应用，扩大以绿电方式落实省间新能源优先发电规模计划。提升绿证核发全覆盖质效，完善绿证全生命周期管理机制，推广绿证中长期购买模式。2030年经营区绿电绿证交易规模达到8000亿千瓦时。
15.推动完善电力价格机制。以价格信号引导清洁能源消纳与系统调节，配合完善分时电价，推动扩大峰谷电价差，探索体现分时价值差异的零售市场和需求响应价格机制。配合完善新能源可持续发展电价政策，推动就近消纳价格机制平稳实施，落实重点行业节能降碳差别化电价政策。
六、服务碳双控制度落地实施
16.支撑碳排放统计核算体系建设。落实国家双碳综合评价考核工作要求，配合政府开展非化石能源消费占比、年度新增用电量中新增清洁能源电量占比等重点指标计算。积极参与全国及地方双碳动态监测预警制度构建，发挥能源大数据中心作用，推进煤、油、气、热等能源消费数据归集和在线监测。推进省级碳计量中心全覆盖，加强电碳计量设备及配套检测装置研发，扩大碳排放监测示范区建设覆盖范围，积极推广火电碳排放实时监测。
17.加快构建分时分区电碳因子体系。构建层级清晰、时段精细、品类完备的电碳因子数据库，推动纳入国家温室气体排放因子数据库和碳足迹背景数据库，支撑国家温室气体排放因子动态更新。构建服务政府、企业、园区、项目、产品全方位应用生态，满足精细化电碳核算多元需求。
18.积极培育电碳融合业务。围绕地方碳考核、行业碳管控、企业碳管理、项目碳评价、产品碳足迹等领域，发挥专业和技术优势，创新具有电网特色的电碳融合业务。探索“核算-管控-降碳-交易-评价”全链条电能碳服务，积极拓展地方碳账户、企业碳效码、产品碳标识等应用场景。深化绿色金融服务，探索为金融机构碳减排支持工具提供模型、标准、认证等支撑。
七、加强高水平科技创新
19.加快关键技术攻关与转化应用。加强与发电企业、装备企业、科研机构协同攻关，突破沙戈荒全绿电外送、海上风电汇集送出、新能源精准预测主动支撑等关键技术，加快长时储能等研发应用。加强通信网、数字网、算力网等数智基础设施建设，构建数字孪生电网，深入实施“人工智能+”专项行动，加快新型电力系统示范项目落地。
20.深化技术标准交流合作与衔接互认。加快研制电力碳排放核算、产品碳足迹评价、碳排放监测量化、零碳园区等领域标准，推进电力低碳标准体系建设。积极参与全球能源和气候治理，推动特高压、新能源并网、智能电表等领域产品、技术、服务一体化“走出去”，支撑因子数据、认证结果和服务机构等国际认可。围绕绿色能源领域标准、认证等核心业务，积极推进国际标准布局、规则衔接与国际互认。

title: 上半年数字产业收入同比增长13.6%
content:
工业和信息化部数据显示：今年上半年，数字产业实现收入20.71万亿元，同比增长13.6%，增速同比加快4.1个百分点。
利润大幅增长。受国内人工智能需求增长和出口增势强劲双重拉动，数字产业盈利水平持续改善，1—6月实现利润总额1.79万亿元，同比增长19.3%，增速较上年同期加快10.3个百分点。收入利润率达8.6%，较上年同期提升0.7个百分点。
数字基础设施持续优化升级。截至6月底，5G基站达到510.2万个，具备千兆网络服务能力的10GPON端口达3286万个，建成5G行业虚拟专网超8万个。
数字制造业量效齐升。电子行业增加值同比增长14.8%，增速较一季度加快1.2个百分点，高于整体工业9.4个百分点。规模以上电子信息制造业实现营业收入12.15万亿元，同比增长17.8%;实现利润总额7036亿元，同比增长66%。

title: 中国石油长庆油田第一采气厂多维施策筑牢极端天气下生产安全防线
content:
靶向防控，破解高温多雨双重考验。第一采气厂五座天然气净化厂通过优化设备巡检制度，增加巡检频次，实时掌握设备温度、压力、动设备运行电流等关键参数，及时发现并解决潜在问题。同时，对易受高温影响的设备，如空压机、胺液循环泵、鼓风机等，采取合理调整负荷、强制降温、增加通风等措施，确保机泵等关键设备始终处于最佳工况温度区间。提前制定防汛应急预案，对厂区排水系统进行全面检查与疏通，确保排水畅通。在低洼地带和关键设施周边设置沙袋、挡水板等防洪设施，防止雨水倒灌。
严字当头，织密安全生产防护网。极端天气下，该厂将安全管理标准再提一级。严格落实领导带班制度，加强24小时应急值守，确保遇到突发情况能够迅速响应、有效处置；聚焦高温多雨环境下的作业风险，通过智能生产调度系统，科学实施错峰作业，将场站修缮等室外作业调整至早晚时段，极端天气期间暂停高空、露天等风险作业，从源头降低安全隐患。对临时用电、高处作业等特种作业，作业前必须开展专项风险评估，坚决杜绝违规操作。
实战练兵，锻造高效应急处置能力。加强员工安全教育培训，通过模拟极端天气下的设备故障处置、有限空间救援等场景，结合案例剖析、班组讨论等方式开展桌面演练，提升员工安全意识与应急处置能力。净化厂构建“15分钟应急圈”体系，按“班组-车间-厂级”三级标准储备应急物资，班组级标配便携式气体检测仪、防爆扳手等，车间级备足防爆轴流风机、应急照明设备等，厂级仓库集中存放大型抢险设备与备用机泵部件，确保突发情况“就近取材、即时处置”。通过与消防中队、片区医务室建立“联勤联动”机制，定期开展联合演练，优化应急路线与协同流程，平均应急响应时间缩短至8分钟，较之前提升40%。
从提前预警到精准防控，从快速处置到持续改进，
第一采气厂以系统化思维筑牢极端天气下的生产安全防线，为气田生产平稳运行提供了坚实保障。

title: 中水物资北京公司推进电子超市商品价格有奖监督机制落地实施
content:
为规范电子超市商品价格管理，营造良好透明采购交易环境，近日，中水物资北京公司正式上线电子超市商品价格有奖监督机制，全面全面开放价格异议反馈渠道，动员电子超市全体用户参与监督，以多元管控举措筑牢阳光采购合规防线。该监督模式覆盖北京公司及中油公司电子超市全部在售商品，包含自主一级长协物资、入驻商城MRO工业品及办公用品，实现采购商品价格监督全覆盖。
公司实行分类精准价格管控，明确刚性定价红线。其中，自主长协商品售价不得高于同品牌、同规格、同渠道市场价格;外部入驻商城商品，除限时、限量、限区域的特殊促销商品外，售价不得高于主流电商平台同款价格及品牌官方标价、指导零售价，从源头杜绝虚高定价、定价不规范等采购乱象，夯实采购价格标准化管理基础。
为保障监督机制落地见效，公司搭建二维码、专项邮箱、监督热线三大便捷反馈渠道，系统内用户可随时提交价格异议问题。对核查属实的价格异常问题，将对反馈人员予以奖励，充分激活全员监督力量，打破传统后台单一管控的局限，构建常态化、全民化的价格监督体系，有效补齐采购监管短板。
此次价格监督机制是公司深化阳光采购、合规采购建设的创新务实举措，有效净化采购交易生态、压降采购成本、完善全流程监督管控体系。下一步，公司将持续迭代优化电子超市运营管控机制，常态化开展价格监督治理，以精细化、透明化、规范化的采购管理，筑牢企业合规经营底线，持续赋能物资采购工作高质量发展，助力企业生产经营提质增效。

title: 书页间的青春
content:
最上面是一本《三国演义》，封面的红底已经褪成了暗粉色，书脊裂开了几道口子，用透明胶带歪歪扭扭地粘着。翻开扉页，蓝色圆珠笔写着一行字——“二〇一四年春购于校门口书店”，字迹圆滚滚的，每一笔都格外用力。那一年我十四岁。
十四岁读三国，其实读的是热闹。翻到赵云长坂坡那一回，书页右上角用铅笔写着四个字：“帅死了！”旁边画了一个竖大拇指的小人。我想起来了，那是初一暑假的午后，我躺在那张一米二宽的小床上读这一回，读到赵云在千军万马中七进七出，激动得从床上坐起来，抓起笔就写。那时候的喜欢直接又坦荡，英雄就是英雄，帅就是帅，不必藏着掖着。再往后翻，诸葛亮五丈原那一页，批注却变了。只有一行极小的字：“他也会死啊。”字迹潦草，墨迹洇开了一小片。十四岁的我大约是被这句话吓着了，一直以为诸葛亮是永远不会老不会死的，书里的神，怎么会躺在病榻上数着灯盏熄灭呢。那一瞬间我突然明白了什么，又说不清楚，只好写下这五个字，像是替自己安放一点不安。
箱角压着一本《边城》，封面是湘西那种湿润的青色。扉页上写着“二〇一五年秋”，字迹比三国那本稳当了些，大约是高二时读的，十五岁。在“这个人也许永远不回来了，也许‘明天’回来”那一句下面，没有字，只有一道铅笔画的曲线，弯弯的，像一个人在缓缓地叹气。十六岁的我已经学会了不轻易说话。有些东西在心里翻涌，却找不到合适的字眼，只好画一道似有若无的线，把说不出的念头藏进纸的纤维里。
旁边是《平凡的世界》，翻得最破的一本。扉页上写着“二〇一五年冬”，旁边是一行极小的字：“我想去外面看看。”那一年我十七岁，高三，每天埋头在成堆的试卷里。孙少平在煤矿井下抬头望见一线天光的时候，我用铅笔在下面写了一行：“光应该很大吧。”十七岁的我从来没离开过关中平原，心里涨满一种说不清的渴望。书的最后一页，我用特别重的笔迹写了一句话，把纸都划破了：“世界很大，我该往哪里走呢？”问号问得认真极了，透着少年人特有的、沉甸甸的迷茫。
箱子最底下是一个牛皮纸笔记本，里面抄满了句子。翻开第一页，高一那年摘的：“面朝大海，春暖花开。”往后翻，有徐志摩、有北岛、有顾城。抄到后来，句子旁边开始有了自己的话，有时是一句感慨，有时是一个问号，有时只是一团乱线——那是十六七岁的夜晚，心里有一团理不清的东西，便抓起笔在纸上胡乱涂满，涂完了便合上本子睡去。
把书重新放回纸箱的时候，我坐在床边发了很久的呆。二十六岁的我已经去过很多地方了。早已不是那个在书页上写“帅死了”的十四岁男孩，也不是迷茫地问“该往哪里走”的少年了。可当我翻开这些旧书，那些字迹还在，波浪线还在，乱线还在。它们像时间的河床，十四岁的我、十六岁的我、十七岁的我，都在岸边蹲着，认真地在石头上刻下自己的话，然后站起身拍拍土走了。只有这些石头留在原地，等着二十六岁的我蹲下来，一个一个地，重新认出来。
箱子封好推回床底。从今往后，我床下便多了一个沉甸甸的东西，装着我的青春期，装着我读过的句子、问过又咽回去的疑问。它们在黑暗里静静地躺着，等着下一个十年后的我，再一次蹲下身来打开。（夏智轩）
